speaker: Liam Cavanagh, Seth Juarez
title: Making Enterprise GPT Real with Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI Service
summary: Liam Cavanagh joins Seth Juarez in this episode of the AI Show to demonstrate how Azure Cognitive Search combined with Azure OpenAI Service allows enterprises to index and retrieve data, finding the most relevant pieces of information, and presenting them to the language model for top-ranked results. This powerful combination enables organizations to deliver in-context, relevant responses while respecting information protection controls.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh, Seth Juarez
title: Making Enterprise GPT Real with Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI Service
summary: In this video demonstration, the speaker showcases an example of using Azure cognitive search and Azure open AI to create a chat experience over HR documents. The system retrieves relevant information from the documents and uses it as a prompt for the large language model to generate grounded answers. The model does not make up answers and only responds based on the available content. The demonstration also includes a developer mode to view the search results and injected prompts.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh, Seth Juarez
title: Making Enterprise GPT Real with Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI Service
summary: The video demonstrates how the chat GPT model can retain previous information and continue conversations, providing context for further discussions. It also showcases the ease of setting up the model and its ability to handle multi-language support with a simple prompt modification. The video emphasizes that any incorrect answers are a result of the model being trained on previous data and not having access to specific information.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh, Seth Juarez
title: Making Enterprise GPT Real with Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI Service
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the capabilities of Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI service. They explain how the models can be trained on specific data and provide instructions in English to generate content. The speaker also mentions that deploying the models is a simple process and encourages viewers to try it out and provide feedback. Overall, the video highlights the powerful and user-friendly nature of these services.

speaker: Justin, Carlos
title: Conversational AI: Bot Building Tools
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Justin and Carlos discuss conversational AI tooling. They highlight the importance of tooling in empowering developers to infuse AI into their applications. The tools showcased in the video support the entire bot development workflow, including conversational modeling, LUIS, QnA maker, and language model dispatching. They also introduce a new and extensible bot emulator. All the tools and the emulator are open source and available on GitHub.

speaker: Justin, Carlos
title: Conversational AI: Bot Building Tools
summary: You can use tools to create a transcript file and playback conversations without building a bot. This allows you to show your management how the experience will be and make any necessary changes before actually building the bot. The transcript file is a Markdown file that is used as input for the chatdown CLI, which outputs a transcript of activities. This transcript can then be imported into the emulator to visualize the conversation flow. This process helps stakeholders understand and approve the bot's functionality before development begins.

speaker: Justin, Carlos
title: Conversational AI: Bot Building Tools
summary: In this video, the presenters discuss a simplified approach to creating complex machine learning models that understand human language. They demonstrate how to define intents and import them into the LUIS model using Markdown and the LUDown command line tool. They also explain the role of the MS Bot command line tool in creating a bot file and connecting services like LUIS. The video showcases the integration between LUIS and the MS Bot emulator, allowing developers to test and interact with the LUIS model.

speaker: Justin, Carlos
title: Conversational AI: Bot Building Tools
summary: In this video, the hosts demonstrate how to use the Microsoft Bot Framework Command Line Interface (CLI) to create and manage chatbots. They show how to generate a bot file, run the bot in an emulator, and deploy the bot to Azure using the Azure CLI. They also highlight the ability to easily enable a bot for different channels, such as Microsoft Teams, using a simple command. The CLI supports various services, including LUIS and QnA Maker, and allows developers to choose between Node.js and C# for bot code.

speaker: Seth Juarez, Vishwac Sena Kannan
title: Bot Framework Composer
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Seth Juarez is joined by Vishwac Sena Kannan, Program Manager for Bot Framework, to introduce and demo Bot Framework Composer. Bot Framework Composer is an integrated development tool for developers and multi-disciplinary teams to build bots and conversational experiences with the Microsoft Bot Framework. It provides capabilities for language understanding, dialogue modeling, and generation. The tool is open source and available on GitHub.

speaker: Seth Juarez, Vishwac Sena Kannan
title: Bot Framework Composer
summary: The video showcases the Microsoft Bot Framework Composer, a tool that allows developers to build and customize conversational bots. The Composer provides a visual interface for creating dialogues and actions, as well as the ability to manipulate memory and access external resources. It also supports language generation and understanding, allowing for more natural and dynamic conversations. The video demonstrates how to get started with Composer and test the bot using an emulator.

speaker: Seth Juarez, Vishwac Sena Kannan
title: Bot Framework Composer
summary: Microsoft Bot Framework Composer is an open-source tool that allows developers to easily build and test chatbot dialogues. It leverages the Louis language understanding service and provides a simple markdown format for managing bot responses. Composer also offers pre-built functions and the ability to create rich and variable responses, including buttons and cards. The tool enables interruptions in conversations and provides flexibility in how the bot responds to user inputs.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: Bharath and Xiaoyong discuss how data scientists can use Microsoft AI and open-source deep learning frameworks to build a lung disease prediction model using chest X-ray images. They explain the motivation behind the project, the data collection process, and the importance of cleaning the data. The episode provides insights into the use of AI technology to reduce the time it takes to diagnose and treat pneumonia in areas without radiologists.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: DenseNet is a state-of-the-art model for image classification that overcomes the vanishing gradient problem in deep neural networks. It uses dense blocks, where each layer can access the feature maps of all previous layers, allowing for better gradient flow. DenseNet trains multiple smaller neural networks and stacks them together, providing flexibility to remove or add layers as needed. This approach combines the benefits of convolutional neural networks with the power of dense connections.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: The video discusses the process of training a deep neural network for image classification using chest x-ray images. The model is inspired by previous work at Stanford and is trained using data augmentation techniques such as flipping, zooming, and rotation. The training process involves setting hyperparameters, including the learning rate and learning rate decay. The use of the Adam optimizer with momentum and RMSprop helps speed up the training process, taking only around an hour to train the model.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: The video discusses the training process of a model for multi-label classification using Keras and TensorFlow. The model was trained in about an hour or two, which is considered fast. The sigmoid function was used for multi-label classification, where each output node represents a label with a probability between 0 and 1. The training loss decreased initially but started to increase later, indicating overfitting. The best model was selected based on validation loss.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: The video discusses the process of improving accuracy in medical image classification using deep learning models. It emphasizes the importance of validation metrics, such as ROC curves, to evaluate model performance. The use of data augmentation techniques, such as cropping and flipping, is also highlighted. The final result achieved an 84% AUC score for the 14 diseases being classified, indicating good accuracy.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the importance of model visualization and interpretation in the context of using AI models in healthcare. They explain that doctors and patients need to understand how the model arrived at its predictions, and demonstrate an example of visualizing a model's prediction for a specific disease. The speaker also mentions the use of ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) as a way to make AI models more portable and usable across different platforms.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: Onyx is a neural net exchange formed by Microsoft and Facebook, with support from hardware and software vendors. It supports popular deep neural net frameworks like CNTK, PyTorch, and TensorFlow. Onyx models use protobufs, and frameworks like PyTorch have built-in exporters for Onyx. Once you have an Onyx model, you can use Windows Machine Learning to natively infer on Windows without additional runtimes. This allows for easy sharing and deployment of machine learning models.

speaker: Bharath, Xiaoyong, Jo, Jessica, Brock
title: Intelligent Edge - Use Microsoft AI to Build a Lung-Disease Prediction Model with Chest X-Ray Images
summary: The video discusses the process of using machine learning frameworks and Windows ML to build and deploy AI models. It highlights the ease of exporting models using ONNX and the ability to call them directly using Windows ML for inferencing. The video also mentions the support and visualizers available in the open source community. Overall, it provides an overview of the machine learning process and the capabilities of Windows ML.

speaker: Seth, Krishna Doss
title: Translate documents at scale and preserve formatting with Azure Translator
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Krishna Doss, Principal Program Manager for Translator Service at Azure, discusses the latest updates to Azure Translator. He highlights the Document Translation feature, which allows users to translate large volumes of documents in various file formats while preserving the layout and structure. Krishna also explains how users can bring their own translation memory and create custom glossaries for translation.

speaker: Seth, Krishna Doss
title: Translate documents at scale and preserve formatting with Azure Translator
summary: The video discusses the functionalities added to support specific customer use cases for document translation. These functionalities include the ability to translate multilingual documents, secure access to storage, support for AAD based authentication, and more. The video also explains the simple flow of uploading the source document, making a request to the service, and retrieving the translated document. Optional parameters are available for custom translation models, glossaries, and filtering specific folders within a container.

speaker: Seth, Krishna Doss
title: Translate documents at scale and preserve formatting with Azure Translator
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to use Azure Translator to translate documents while preserving the original formatting. They showcase a client app that utilizes the document translation API to translate Word documents and PowerPoint slides. The translated documents maintain the same structure, layout, and styling as the originals. The presenter also mentions that code samples and SDKs are available in popular languages like Python and .Net. The video emphasizes the security and privacy measures in place to protect customer data.

speaker: Raouf Merouche
title: AI Show | Similarity and Scoring in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Raouf Merouche, a Software Engineer in the Azure Cognitive Search team, discusses similarity and scoring in Azure Cognitive Search. He explains the indexing and querying processes, document processing, creating inverted indexes, and retrieving and ranking search results. This video provides insights into how developers can customize and enhance the search capabilities of Azure Cognitive Search.

speaker: Raouf Merouche
title: AI Show | Similarity and Scoring in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Azure Search is a search engine that retrieves relevant documents based on a query. It removes stop words and possessives, and supports over 50 languages. Custom analyzers can be created using technical rules, and APIs are available to test analyzers and tokenization. The search process involves creating an inverted index, which allows for quick identification of matching documents. Results can be aggregated based on query configuration. Azure Search also ranks documents based on similarity scores.

speaker: Raouf Merouche
title: AI Show | Similarity and Scoring in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video discusses the calculation of similarity scores in text-based search engines. It explains that most similarity scores rely on two main variables: term frequency (how often a term appears in a document) and document frequency (how many documents contain a specific term). The video also mentions the tf-idf algorithm, which is the term frequency divided by the document frequency. It further discusses the use of scoring profiles to customize the weighting of different text fields in the final score calculation.

speaker: Raouf Merouche
title: AI Show | Similarity and Scoring in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video discusses how to use scoring profiles in Azure Search to determine the importance of different fields in search results. By assigning weights to each field, you can prioritize certain fields over others. Scoring profiles can be applied at query time, allowing for customization based on user preferences or specific scenarios. Additionally, functions can be used to compute boosting values based on non-searchable fields, such as ratings or view counts, to further influence the ranking of search results.

speaker: Raouf Merouche
title: AI Show | Similarity and Scoring in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Azure Cognitive Search allows users to customize the ranking of search results by applying boosting values to documents based on various factors such as recency, distance, and tags. These boosting values are calculated using different parameters and functions set by the user. Customers can experiment with different scoring profiles and even use machine learning techniques to optimize the relevance of search results. Azure Cognitive Search is continuously looking for customer feedback to improve its processes and provide better tools for customization.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki, Joakim Astrom
title: InterpretML in Practice at Scandinavian Airlines
summary: Mehrnoosh Sameki, Senior Product Manager at Azure AI, and Joakim Astrom, Cloud Solution Architect, discuss how Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) is using Microsoft's InterpretML within Azure Machine Learning to understand and debug their EuroBonus fraud detection model. SAS uses InterpretML to gain insights into how the model makes predictions, allowing them to proactively stop fraud and safeguard the EuroBonus loyalty program. Azure Machine Learning provides the necessary tooling for productive and responsible AI solutions.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki, Joakim Astrom
title: InterpretML in Practice at Scandinavian Airlines
summary: SAS, a global leader in analytics, partnered with Microsoft to build a fraud prevention model using Azure Machine Learning. By utilizing AutoML for automatic retraining and InterpretML for model explainability, SAS was able to increase detection capabilities without expanding their fraud detection staff. They reduced the number of features from 54 to 31 without sacrificing accuracy, resulting in improved insights into fraud levels and a 300% increase in fraud detection. The integration of InterpretML within Azure Machine Learning allowed for easy model management and transparency throughout the machine learning lifecycle.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Microsoft MVP Vlad Iliescu joins Seth Juarez to demonstrate how to draw anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion. Stable Diffusion is an open-source model that allows users to generate images from text. Vlad discusses the challenges of running Stable Diffusion and provides a demo of how it works. He also explains how to configure and run Stable Diffusion on your own hardware.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: The video showcases the use of Stable Diffusion, an open-source interface powered by AI, to generate images. The presenter demonstrates how to configure Stable Diffusion to create a perfect vacation scenery, specifically a sunny beach with friendly waves. The Stable Diffusion model gradually refines random noise to generate an image that aligns with the user's request. The video highlights the flexibility and creative potential of Stable Diffusion in image generation.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: The video showcases the process of creating a customized image using an open-source interface on top of table diffusion. The creator utilizes AI and a neural network to predict and answer questions. They explain how they set up the system using an HTML studio and an Azure ML compute instance. The goal is to test how well the compute instance works for running applications, not just notebooks.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: The video demonstrates how to configure computer instances to run Python code using an embedded terminal. This allows for easy access to the interface and management of compute instances from the command line. The use of computer instances in the cloud is necessary for tasks that require a GPU, as it provides faster processing speeds and sufficient VRAM. The UI used in the video is part of the repository and utilizes the radio library for building Python interfaces.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: The video discusses the process of setting up a compute instance for Azure ML users to run and visualize machine learning models. The presenter highlights the importance of setting up authentication for the public URL and explains the steps involved in creating a Conda environment and installing the necessary packages. The video also demonstrates the command to run the radio app and showcases the user-friendly options available.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: The video showcases the use of a stable diffusion model on Azure compute instances without any modifications. The presenter highlights the ease of running the model and mentions the availability of the code and details on their blog. They also demonstrate the ability to use Visual Studio Code on a remote machine in the cloud, emphasizing the convenience and excitement of remote development. The video encourages viewers to explore compute instances for their own projects.

speaker: Vlad Iliescu, Seth Juarez
title: How to Draw Anything with Azure AI and Stable Diffusion
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of running Stable Diffusion on Azure's compute instances. They explain how to connect Visual Studio code to the compute instance and access the terminal. They also mention that the files generated are stored in Azure's file shares, allowing multiple people to work on the same code. The speaker concludes by highlighting the benefits of using compute instances for running Stable Diffusion.

speaker: Shivani Patel
title: No Code Deployment and Enriched Model Registry with AML Service
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Shivani Patel discusses updates to the Azure Machine Learning service model registry, which allows for easier deployment of machine learning models without the need for additional driver and configuration files. The new features include the ability to provide framework and version information, sample input and output data, and input and output schemas. This simplifies the deployment process for certain frameworks like ONNX, AutoML, scikit-learn, and TensorFlow Keras models.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Seth Juarez demonstrates how to build an end-to-end solution for anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks and Anomaly Detector. The solution detects numerical anomalies from streaming data coming through Azure Event Hubs. Seth walks through the business problem, solution architecture, code walkthroughs, and provides additional resources for further learning.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: Azure Databricks can be used as the compute engine for real-life solutions, but other options like Azure notebooks, Jupyter notebooks, Azure Functions, or on-premise infrastructure can also be used. Power BI can also be utilized. The video follows the tutorial on Azure documentation for Anomaly Detector. Detailed steps and screenshots are provided to guide users in creating an Azure Databricks workspace and Spark cluster. It is important to select the correct parameters to avoid any issues with the code and unnecessary costs.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: To follow this tutorial, you will need a Twitter application and a Twitter developer account to obtain the necessary API keys and credentials. Once you have created your Azure Databricks cluster, you will need to attach two additional libraries: one for reading data from Event Hubs and another for reading data from Twitter. Follow the tutorial's instructions to properly install and attach these libraries to your cluster.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the Event Hub library and the Twitter library to create an Anomaly Detector in Databricks. The tutorial provides a link for creating Anomaly Detector results and explains how to obtain the endpoint and access keys. It also shows how to create two notebooks: one for data production and one for data analysis. The tutorial includes code snippets and instructions for replacing placeholders with the necessary keys.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: The video demonstrates how to use an anomaly detector object in a notebook. The notebook is divided into different blocks, each with its own functionality. The first block defines the anomaly detector class with two functions: detect latest point and detect batch. The second block is an aggregation function that calls the detect latest point function to detect anomalies in a time series data. The video also covers loading data from an Event Hub and visualizing it in a TableView.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: The video discusses the process of aggregation in data analysis. It explains that data loaded into the Event Hub is randomly distributed based on when it was posted on Twitter. To create evenly distributed data, aggregation or sampling is necessary. The video demonstrates the code block responsible for aggregation, showing how new data is continuously streamed and evenly distributed. The aggregated result is then stored in Delta, a Data Lake Storage in Azure Databricks. The video also showcases the display function to view the aggregated data.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: The video demonstrates anomaly detection using a sliding window of time-series data. The data is prepared and aggregated using specified functions, and the API is called to detect anomalies. The results are displayed, with a true value indicating an anomaly. The video also mentions the need to ensure that the data being analyzed is up-to-date.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Anomaly detection on streaming data using Azure Databricks
summary: The video demonstrates how to detect anomalies in streaming data using Azure Databricks and Azure Anomaly Detector. It explains the process of defining a job in Azure Databricks to detect anomalies in real-time data from sources like Event Hubs or IoT Hub. The video also mentions the availability of a tutorial for step-by-step instructions and additional resources like the Azure Anomaly Detector overview and a Microsoft Teams channel for anomaly detector customers.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: Azure ML Data Prep GUI is a tool that allows users to perform data preparation tasks in a graphical user interface (GUI) instead of writing code. This video demonstrates how the GUI can simplify and speed up data prep, allowing users to focus on modeling. The GUI is currently in restricted preview, but interested customers can request access. The video also provides a summary of previous episodes on data preparation and introduces the cross-platform capabilities of the GUI.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: The video discusses the addition of a new column called "path" in data preparation, which helps in extracting relevant information from file names or paths. It also highlights the importance of interactive data exploration and the ability to create samples for analysis. The tool allows for both top and random sampling, with plans to introduce stratified sampling. Additionally, there are plans to provide statistical comparison and visualization tools for analyzing different samples.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: The video discusses the use of sampling in machine learning experiments to save time and resources. By generating smaller samples that are statistically similar to the overall dataset, researchers can run experiments more quickly and make more informed hypotheses. The video also demonstrates the use of visualization and statistics to understand and analyze data, as well as the use of derived columns to handle complex data formats.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: In this advanced mode, the video demonstrates how suggested examples can be used to improve data quality for AI. By providing examples that represent problematic cases, the AI algorithm can generate a program to fix similar issues in the dataset. The video shows the process of selecting and promoting an example, resulting in a significant reduction in null cases. Visualizations, such as histograms, are used to analyze the impact of data changes.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: The video demonstrates the iterative and interactive process of data preparation using a GUI interface. It highlights the ability to apply various transformations to columns and generate code for scalability on a Spark cluster. The video also mentions the careful optimization of transformations to ensure accurate results when scaling up. Additionally, it showcases a feature from Microsoft Research that allows for frequency analysis and visualization of data.

speaker: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
title: Azure ML Data Prep GUI, Its Not Just About The Code
summary: The video demonstrates a data preparation tool called Microsoft Data Prep User Interface. It uses unsupervised learning and clustering techniques to clean and organize data. The tool allows users to easily visualize and manipulate data clusters, remove or add entries, and adjust similarity thresholds. By automating data cleaning processes, the tool aims to improve efficiency in data preparation and allow data scientists to focus on modeling and analysis.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Jeremy Howard, co-founder of fast.ai, explains in this episode of the AI Show how to become a deep learning practitioner without needing a PhD. He discusses how fast.ai aims to make deep learning accessible to everyone, and shares details on their free software and courses. Howard also talks about his journey into AI and the resurgence of neural networks with the advent of deep learning.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Fast.ai is a platform that aims to make deep learning accessible to everyone, regardless of their mathematical background. They believe that the math required for deep learning is actually quite simple, involving basic operations like addition, multiplication, and derivatives. Their approach to teaching involves providing context and practical applications right from the start, allowing users to create state-of-the-art vision classifiers within the first half hour of their course.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: The video discusses the success of a new approach to teaching deep learning, which focuses on practical applications rather than starting with complex math. The course, called Fast.ai, has been successful in teaching people without technical backgrounds and has led to advancements in various fields, including scientific research and business. The approach has been praised for its effectiveness in providing context and solving real-world problems.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Telecommunication companies, Tesla, and OpenAI are praising the Fast.ai course for its effectiveness in preparing individuals to hit the ground running in their organizations. The course, available for free at course.fast.ai, is part of Fast.ai's mission to make AI accessible to everyone. They are also developing a library, built on PyTorch, to simplify coding and eventually eliminate the need for code altogether. The library aims to make deep learning more accessible to those without coding expertise.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Fast.ai is a library built on top of PyTorch that simplifies deep learning code. With just a few lines of code, you can create state-of-the-art vision classifiers, neural networks for text analysis, collaborative filtering systems, and tabular analysis systems. The library follows consistent APIs and clear API boundaries, making it easy for coders to dive in and customize as needed. Fast.ai is also useful for researchers, as it provides a generic optimizer that simplifies the process of improving neural network weights.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Researchers can benefit from using the Fast.ai library because it provides high-level API concepts that abstract away complex coding tasks. The library includes a data blocks API that simplifies tasks such as data separation, labeling, filtering, and preprocessing. The library also offers multiple levels of abstraction, making it easier for researchers to implement their ideas without spending months writing code. The library's design avoids the limitations of fluent APIs and provides a more intuitive and flexible approach.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: The video features a discussion about the new functional data blocks API in the fast.ai library. The API provides higher-level abstractions for tasks such as vision, text, and medical imaging, making it more concise and clear. It also includes mid-tier APIs for transforms and pipelines. The library is built with Jupyter Notebooks, allowing users to easily access documentation and implementation. More information can be found at docs.fast.ai.

speaker: Jeremy Howard
title: AI Applications Without a PhD
summary: Jeremy Howard, co-founder of fast.ai, discusses the future of deep learning and AI. He believes that deep learning is another way of building programs and predicts that most code will eventually be learned code. Howard emphasizes that deep learning is accessible to everyone, even without large datasets, powerful computers, or extensive knowledge of linear algebra. He also mentions that the book "Deep Learning for Coders with Fast.ai and PyTorch" is available for free as Jupyter Notebooks on GitHub.

speaker: Mei
title: Distributed Processing
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Mei, a program manager on the Azure machine learning service team, discusses how to use datasets in a distributed manner for data pre-processing using Azure machine learning platform. She explains what datasets are, how they can help in machine learning workflows, and demonstrates their use with parallel run in automation and pipelines. The demo showcases the use of datasets to process a large dataset of scholarly articles for exploratory data analysis and NLP training.

speaker: Mei
title: Distributed Processing
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to manage data in Azure storage service as a single source of truth. They create two datasets, one for metadata and the other for research articles. The datasets are registered in the machine learning workspace for data exploration. The presenter then shows how to mount the dataset onto a compute instance and read the files. They also explain how to prepare the data using parallel run and configure the pipeline. The video provides a demo notebook and reference links for getting started with Azure machine learning.

speaker: Noelle Lacharite
title: An Introduction to the Intelligent Kiosk #TWiCognitive
summary: Noelle Lacharite introduces the Intelligent Kiosk, a tool used to test and build projects related to Cognitive Services and Applied AI. The app allows users to explore various functionalities such as computer vision, real-time driver monitoring, news analytics, and emotion analysis. Noelle demonstrates the use of custom vision and Bing Search services within the app. The Intelligent Kiosk is available for download from the Windows Store and can also be built and deployed by users.

speaker: Noelle Lacharite
title: An Introduction to the Intelligent Kiosk #TWiCognitive
summary: Cognitive Services offer developers simple access to powerful image analysis capabilities. By using the Computer Vision API, developers can extract tags, descriptions, celebrities, and colors from images, allowing for personalized user experiences. The OCR feature enables the extraction of text from images, which can be used for search and content enrichment. The Intelligent Kiosk sample on GitHub provides a learning tool and the opportunity to contribute to the project. Additionally, Cognitive Services can be integrated into edge devices like Raspberry Pi.

speaker: Jeff, my friend, Jeff Durstan
title: Conversational AI and Authentication
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Jeff Durstan from the Azure Bot Service group discusses the challenges of connecting bots to external resources and the importance of authentication. He introduces the newly built-in authentication cards supported in Azure Bot Service, which simplify the process of authenticating users against various providers and performing tasks on their behalf. The video demonstrates how to register connections and configure authentication settings in the Azure portal.

speaker: Jeff, my friend, Jeff Durstan
title: Conversational AI and Authentication
summary: The video discusses how to connect various applications such as Azure Active Directory, Box, Dropbox, Facebook, Fitbit, Flickr, GitHub, Google, and LinkedIn. It explains the process of registering these connections and obtaining the necessary tokens and settings. The video also demonstrates how to write bot code that utilizes these connections, allowing the bot to perform actions on behalf of the user, such as scheduling social media posts or accessing email and calendar information.

speaker: Jeff, my friend, Jeff Durstan
title: Conversational AI and Authentication
summary: As a bot developer, you can easily implement OAuth authentication in your bot by passing the connection name, text prompt, and button name. The Azure Bot Service manages the token lifecycle, including refreshing, securing, and caching the token. The first time a user logs in, they will be prompted for consent and any necessary authentication. The service supports a generic OAuth2 provider, allowing you to connect to various services. The Get Token dialog utilizes the OAuth Card to handle the authentication process.

speaker: Jeff, my friend, Jeff Durstan
title: Conversational AI and Authentication
summary: In this video, the host demonstrates how to authenticate a bot using the Azure Bot Service and OAuth. The process involves exchanging tokens between the bot service and a third-party service, such as Facebook, to establish a secure connection. The Azure Bot Service manages the lifecycle of the token, eliminating the need for developers to handle token management themselves. The host showcases the authentication process using the Microsoft Graph API and highlights the convenience and security benefits of this approach.

speaker: Seth, Saumya Soni
title: AI Show | AI for Birds
summary: Seth is joined by Saumya Soni, a high-school student and CEO of AI for Environment, a nonprofit that uses AI, IoT, and Business Intelligence to address global environmental challenges. Saumya showcases her creation, AI for Birds, a phone app that predicts bird species and provides information about them. The app utilizes Microsoft Custom Vision AI and demonstrates the potential of AI in enhancing environmental sustainability.

speaker: Seth, Saumya Soni
title: AI Show | AI for Birds
summary: AI for Birds is a non-profit organization that uses artificial intelligence and business intelligence to address global environmental challenges. Their interactive bird recognition app, AI for Birds, can identify bird species in real-time. The app provides bird attribute reports, including information on endangered species, and allows users to upload images for identification. The goal is to raise awareness about the importance of birds and inspire action against climate change. For more information, visit aiforbirds.com and aiforenvironment.org.

speaker: Seth, Saumya Soni
title: AI Show | AI for Birds
summary: The creator of the AI for Birds app used their passion for birds and learned about data science and AI through courses and online resources. They faced challenges in training the AI model, initially experiencing lower accuracy, but improved it by adding more images. The app aims to raise awareness about the plight of birds and the potential of AI to protect the environment.

speaker: Seth, Saumya Soni
title: AI Show | AI for Birds
summary: Saumya Gupta, the creator of AI for Birds, discusses the challenges she faced and the lessons she learned while developing the app. She emphasizes the potential of artificial intelligence and IoT technologies in promoting environmental sustainability and achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. Gupta also shares her current project, partnering with a non-profit in India to use AI and IoT to help farmers increase productivity and food yield while minimizing resource usage. She concludes by providing links to her non-profit and the AI for Birds website.

speaker: Tony Indiana
title: Meet the New Bot Framework Emulator
summary: Tony Indiana, a developer on the Microsoft Bot Framework and Azure Bot Service Team, introduces the new Bot Framework Emulator. The Emulator has been updated with powerful features including creating and viewing conversation transcripts, debugging running bots, and presentation mode. It provides an end-to-end development workflow for planning, testing, and refining bots. The Emulator's new capabilities make bot development and testing easier and more efficient.

speaker: Tony Indiana
title: Meet the New Bot Framework Emulator
summary: In this video, the speaker explains how to create a transcript of a conversation with a bot using the Bot Framework Emulator. The transcript is a JSON array of conversation activities and can be easily generated by saving a chat session or using the chat down tool. The speaker demonstrates both methods and shows how the transcript files can be accessed and viewed.

speaker: Tony Indiana
title: Meet the New Bot Framework Emulator
summary: The video showcases the Bot Framework Emulator, a tool that allows developers to test and debug their chatbots. It demonstrates features such as conversation transcripts, presentation mode, breakpoints, simultaneous live chats, and integration with services like LUIS and QnA Maker. The Emulator provides a user-friendly interface and allows developers to easily tweak and train their language models.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Mehrnoosh discusses the importance of model interpretability in developing AI in a transparent way. She introduces the Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit, which allows users to use different interpretability methods to explain model decisions. This toolkit can be used during the training phase to verify hypotheses, build trust, debug, validate model behavior, and check for bias. It can also be used at inferencing time to explain predictions to end users.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: Interpretability in machine learning models is important both during training and inferencing. Traditional linear models are easier to interpret, but neural network models pose a challenge. There are two classes of interpretability solutions: interpretable models like linear regression and decision trees, and blackbox explainers that can explain any model. Blackbox explainers use approximations to understand how a model makes predictions. Techniques like SHAFT, mimic explainers, and LIME are used to achieve interpretability.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: Microsoft has developed an interpretability SDK that allows users to bring together various techniques for interpreting black-box models. The SDK, part of Azure Machine Learning, can be used in conjunction with Azure Machine Learning services or locally. It offers explainers for tabular data, including global surrogate models, feature permutation, and Lime. The SDK allows users to understand the features and predictions of their models and can be used with any classifier or regressor.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: An explainer object is introduced in this video to help understand the important factors in a machine learning model. The explainer allows for the examination of global factors and specific data points, helping to identify potential biases or data drift. The video emphasizes the importance of transparency in model predictions and introduces a visualization dashboard to aid in understanding the model better. The dashboard includes tabs for data exploration and global feature importance.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: The video discusses the importance of factors such as job satisfaction and number of companies worked in determining whether an employee will stay or leave a company. It emphasizes the need to consider fairness and mitigate any biases in the data. The video also explains a chart that shows the impact of different feature values on the prediction of staying or leaving, with high values of overtime negatively impacting staying and high values of job satisfaction positively impacting staying.

speaker: Mehrnoosh
title: Machine Learning Interpretability Toolkit
summary: The video discusses the importance of model interpretability and introduces Azure Machine Learning's interpretability features. It explains how these features allow users to understand and explain the predictions made by their models. The video demonstrates various visualizations and tools that can be used to explore and analyze the factors influencing the model's predictions. It also highlights the ability to perform what-if analysis and perturbation exploration to understand the impact of changing input features. Overall, the video emphasizes the importance of model interpretability for building trust and understanding in AI systems.

speaker: Parashar Sha
title: Introduction to Azure ML Services [Part 1/4]
summary: Parashar Sha introduces Azure ML Services in this episode of the AI Show. Azure ML Services provide an integrated, end-to-end data science experience, allowing data scientists to prepare data, develop experiments, and deploy models at cloud scale. The episode provides an overview of Microsoft's AI platform and a walkthrough of the different components of Azure ML Services. The aim is to showcase the capabilities of Azure ML Services and how they can be used in machine learning projects.

speaker: Parashar Sha
title: Introduction to Azure ML Services [Part 1/4]
summary: Azure Machine Learning Services offers a range of capabilities for creating and deploying machine learning models. Users can use their preferred IDE and framework to train and deploy models in the cloud, on-premises, or on IoT Edge. The setup process involves creating an experimentation account to maintain model histories and batch remote compute targets. Azure Machine Learning Services provides flexibility and options for data preparation, model training, and deployment.

speaker: Parashar Sha
title: Introduction to Azure ML Services [Part 1/4]
summary: To set up a data science environment, you will need a machine with spark or a similar tool for scaling, a model management system, and an IDE (optional). The model management system allows for deploying and tracking models, while the IDE provides a coding interface. Azure offers services like the Experimentation Service, Model Management, and Data Science VMs to facilitate this setup process. These services help with hyperparameter tuning, model storage, and infrastructure management.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: Sonya Copyof interviews Nyle Hein, a bioengineering PhD student, about using Azure Machine Learning in neuroscience research. Hein explains how Azure tools and services, such as Azure Machine Learning Workbench and Jupiter notebooks, can be used to analyze EEG data and gain insights into brain activity. While EEG provides a broad understanding of brain activity, it lacks spatial resolution compared to invasive methods like fMRI. The Emotiv Epoch, a device used to record brain activity, generates a significant amount of data for analysis.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video provides an introduction to EEG (electroencephalography) data analysis. It explains how EEG data is recorded using electrodes and discusses the increase in data volume when using more electrodes. The video demonstrates loading and exploring EEG data using Python and the MNE library. It also showcases basic EEG signals and highlights the challenges of interpreting the data visually.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video demonstrates how to process and analyze EEG data using Python notebooks. The presenter explains how to import the data, filter out noise, and visualize the electrode positions. The notebook format allows for organized and interactive exploration of the data. The presenter also mentions that the same analysis can be done using a Python script, but the notebook format provides a more organized and explanatory approach.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video provides an explanation of how to use Fourier transform to analyze brain signals. It discusses the concept of power spectral density and how it can be used to understand the power within different frequency ranges of brain waves. The video also mentions the application of this analysis in brain-computer interfaces. The tutorial uses an open-source dataset and suggests using the MNE package for further exploration.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the M&E package to analyze EEG data and perform classification tasks. The presenter uses a sample dataset and shows how to extract and process the data. They also discuss using an open-source dataset called OpenMIR for musical information retrieval to classify EEG signals based on the song being listened to. The presenter acknowledges that the classification model needs further refinement but highlights the flexibility of using different packages, such as scikit-learn, for analysis.

speaker: Sonya copyof, nyle hein
title: Neuroscience with Azure Machine Learning
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the application of AI in neuroscience, specifically in understanding epilepsy and predicting seizures. They explain how machine learning models can be trained using brain data to detect precursors to seizures and provide warnings to patients. The speaker also mentions plans to release a platform for people to contribute and explore neuroscience data. This application of AI in neuroscience shows promise in advancing the field and helping patients.

speaker: Tracy Chen
title: How to do Batch Inference using AML ParallelRunStep
summary: Tracy Chen, Senior Program Manager on the Azure Machine Learning Team, explains how to use Azure Machine Learning Pipeline's ParallelRunStep for batch inference. Batch inference is commonly used in scenarios such as cybersecurity, customer segmentation, and sales forecasting. ParallelRunStep simplifies the process by handling data partitioning, workload distribution, and cluster management. It automatically retries failed tasks and returns partial successful results. Chen provides an example of using ParallelRunStep for batch inference using a pre-trained digital identification model and the MNIST test dataset.

speaker: Tracy Chen
title: How to do Batch Inference using AML ParallelRunStep
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the ParallelRunStep in Azure Machine Learning to perform batch inference on a dataset. It covers the steps to prepare the input dataset, create the output, register the model, and configure the ParallelRunStep pipeline. Important parameters such as mini-batch size, error threshold, and output organization are explained. The video also mentions the availability of additional configurations and resources for further exploration.

speaker: Chris Lauren
title: Train Machine Learning Models with Azure ML in VS Code
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Chris Lauren demonstrates how to train machine learning models using the Visual Studio Code Tools for AI extension and Azure Machine Learning service. He uses Jupiter notebooks within Visual Studio Code to document and run code, allowing for easy experimentation and debugging. This comprehensive tutorial is a valuable resource for data scientists looking to leverage Azure ML and VS Code for their machine learning projects.

speaker: Chris Lauren
title: Train Machine Learning Models with Azure ML in VS Code
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Azure Machine Learning to enhance the output of Python code. By adding a run object, users can log metrics and visualize the results of their experiments. The logs and any outputs written to the "outputs" folder are automatically uploaded to the cloud. This allows for better visualization and tracking of experiments across different machine learning frameworks. The video also shows how to run the code locally and then use Azure Machine Learning to run it in the cloud.

speaker: Chris Lauren
title: Train Machine Learning Models with Azure ML in VS Code
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to use Azure Machine Learning to attach a local folder and run experiments on a local machine. They also show how to create compute clusters in Azure and set up run configurations for repeated experiments. The video provides step-by-step instructions and helpful tips for using Azure Machine Learning effectively.

speaker: Chris Lauren
title: Train Machine Learning Models with Azure ML in VS Code
summary: The video demonstrates how to set up and run experiments using Azure Machine Learning service and Visual Studio Code tools for AI. It shows how to submit a job, view experiment runs, track metrics, manage dependencies, and create a portable environment. The video also explains how Azure Machine Learning automatically uploads outputs and helps with model testing and deployment. The next episode will focus on using the output in a meaningful way.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: Sanjeev Jagtap joins Seth on the AI Show to discuss the latest advancements in Computer Vision OCR. Microsoft Research has updated Computer Vision with industry-leading models that provide more detailed and accurate tagging of image contents across multiple languages. The new OCR features include support for multiple languages in the same text line, recognition of handwritten and printed text, confidence thresholds, and the ability to process large documents. The episode also includes demos showcasing these new capabilities.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: The video showcases the capabilities of the Computer Vision API, which can analyze and extract text from documents in various languages. The API is easy to use, requiring only a few simple steps to ingest the document and retrieve the extracted text. It also emphasizes the security measures in place, assuring users that their data is not stored or used for training purposes. A Python code sample is provided to demonstrate the API's functionality.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Azure Cognitive Services' Read API to extract text from images. The code shows how to handle both printed and handwritten text, as well as how to process images with a combination of both. The API automatically detects the text and extracts it without the need for specifying the type of text or language. The video provides a step-by-step guide on how to implement this functionality using Azure Cognitive Services.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: The video demonstrates the OCR (Optical Character Recognition) service's ability to extract text from images containing mixed languages. It showcases examples of Japanese, English, and German texts being successfully extracted without specifying any language code. The video also mentions that the OCR service supports a total of 73 languages, with plans for further language expansion in the future.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: The video discusses upcoming language expansion waves and new features in OCR technology. The first wave of language expansion is currently underway, with more waves expected in the next 12 months. The video introduces two new features: Selected Pages, which allows users to specify specific pages or page ranges for processing, and Reading Order, which arranges text lines in natural reading order based on the document layout. These advancements aim to improve OCR accuracy and user experience.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: OCR is just the first step in text extraction. Microsoft's Form Recognizer is a product that uses OCR to extract text from documents and also recognizes checkboxes and tables. The upcoming layout feature of Form Recognizer will be able to identify headers in tables, making it a powerful tool for understanding and analyzing document layouts. This technology is being used as a building block for more advanced software applications.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap, Seth
title: What’s new in Computer Vision OCR
summary: In this video, Sanjeev discusses the use of Form Recognizer and OCR (Optical Character Recognition) for reading and understanding layouts and tables in documents. He also addresses concerns about sensitive documents and legal requirements by explaining how to use OCR containers, which allow organizations to keep documents on-premises and within compliance boundaries. Sanjeev provides links to the Microsoft OCR documentation for further information.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: Vinod Kurpad, a Principal Program Manager on the Applied AI team at Microsoft, discusses the knowledge store feature of Azure Search in this episode of the AI Show. Azure Search is a search-as-a-service platform that allows users to build custom search experiences. The knowledge store feature enables users to enrich their data using AI skills, such as sentiment analysis, and store that information in the search index. This allows for a more comprehensive and customized search experience.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: The video discusses the concept of an enrichment pipeline, which involves applying cognitive skills to data as it moves through the pipeline. The enriched data can then be shaped to match the index schema and projected into a knowledge store. This allows for various uses of the data beyond just search, such as in-app experiences or model retraining. The knowledge store also enables capabilities that act on the entire corpus of data, rather than just on a per-document basis. The video includes a demo of using Azure Search and Power BI to visualize and explore the enriched data.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: In this video, the speaker demonstrates how to create a data source, indexer, and skill set in Azure Search to extract and enrich data from a Blob storage. The data source is configured to extract content and metadata, and the parsing mode is set based on the type of files being dealt with. The speaker also explains the importance of setting up an enrichment pipeline and attaching a Cognitive Services account for document enrichment.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: To enrich documents using Cognitive Services, you need a Cognitive Services key. The key is used for efficient enrichment and you are only charged for successful enrichments. When adding enrichments to your pipeline, you can select the columns you want to enrich and split large files if needed. You can choose from various skills such as sentiment detection, language detection, and key phrase detection. The enriched data can be projected as tables or objects in Blob storage or Azure Tables.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: The video discusses how data can be shaped and stored using the Shaper skill. By creating different shapes for data, users can customize how it is stored and used. The video also mentions the customization of indexes, which determine how data is retrieved, filtered, and faceted. The process of running the indexer is explained, along with the use of Power BI to build dashboards based on the data.

speaker: Vinod Kurpad
title: Knowledge mining using the knowledge store feature of Azure Search
summary: The video discusses the use of Knowledge Store in Power BI to create dashboards and analyze data. It highlights the ability of Knowledge Store to maintain relationships across different tables and project information. The speaker also mentions discrepancies found between human perception and AI analysis of data, such as incorrect reverse geocoding and varying review scales. The video concludes by directing viewers to the documentation page for more information on using Knowledge Store.

speaker: Noelle LaCharite
title: Taking a Look at Computer Vision’s Object Detection #TWiCognitive
summary: Noelle LaCharite discusses computer vision and demonstrates the use of a custom vision, object detection model in a fun use case. She also introduces QnA Maker, a tool that allows users to create chat bots with personality by adding a personal touch to frequently asked questions. Noelle explains the process of creating a knowledge base and suggests using descriptive words in the bot's name to highlight its usefulness.

speaker: Noelle LaCharite
title: Taking a Look at Computer Vision’s Object Detection #TWiCognitive
summary: In this video, the speaker demonstrates how to create a bot using QnA Maker. They show how to import FAQs from a website or TSV files, and how to add personality to the bot. They also explain how to edit and test the bot's responses, and emphasize the importance of testing and fine-tuning the language model. Overall, the video provides a step-by-step guide to building a bot with QnA Maker.

speaker: Francesca Lazzeri
title: AI Show - Democratize AI with Azure Machine Learning designer
summary: Francesca Lazzeri, a speaker on the AI Show, discusses how to democratize AI with Azure Machine Learning designer. Azure Machine Learning offers a wide range of algorithms for various machine learning problems. In this demo, Lazzeri demonstrates how to use Azure Machine Learning designer to create an end-to-end machine learning pipeline. The designer allows users with different technical backgrounds to collaborate and build machine learning solutions without extensive coding.

speaker: Ron Owens, Seth Juarez
title: Project Personality Chat for Bot Developers
summary: Ron Owens joins Seth Juarez to discuss Project Personality Chat, a service for bot developers that helps enhance their bot's conversational capabilities. Personality Chat offers multiple default personas for developers to choose from, allowing them to align their bot's voice with their brand. The service uses intent classifiers and deep neural networks to generate responses consistent with the chosen personality. This helps address the challenge of handling chitchat and small talk queries that often derail bots and disrupt the user experience.

speaker: Ron Owens, Seth Juarez
title: Project Personality Chat for Bot Developers
summary: The video showcases a weather bot that uses an editorial set of responses for common queries and a deep neural network for longer tail queries. The bot has a humorous personality and provides accurate and witty responses. When faced with queries outside its editorial set, it switches to the deep neural network for generating real-time responses.

speaker: Ron Owens, Seth Juarez
title: Project Personality Chat for Bot Developers
summary: The video discusses the use of an editorial set and machine-generated responses in AI chatbots. The editorial set is designed to handle common queries and provide a predefined flow of information. For more unique or unusual queries, the machine-generated responses come into play. The responses are trained for different personalities, and developers have the option to customize the editorial set. This feature saves time and expense for bot developers.

speaker: Ron Owens, Seth Juarez
title: Project Personality Chat for Bot Developers
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the development of voices for AI assistants that support different brand archetypes. They demonstrate a chat with a friendly bot that uses a deep neural network to respond to chat queries. The speaker explains that the bot is designed to stay out of fact-based or task-oriented conversations and only answer chat queries. They also mention that an API is available for developers to integrate this technology into their own bots.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Disha Agarwal discusses Question Answering in general availability. She explains the concept of Question Answering and its applications in building conversational interfaces and chatbots. Disha introduces two capabilities: Custom Question Answering and Prebuilt Question Answering. Custom Question Answering allows users to create a knowledge base and add data from various sources, while Prebuilt Question Answering provides a pre-trained model. The service searches the knowledge base to provide responses to user queries.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: Custom question answering is a service that allows users to update and customize their data, ensuring that users always have the latest information. It runs on an updated knowledge base, providing the most up-to-date responses to user queries. Pre-built question answering, on the other hand, is suitable for enterprises that do not need to maintain custom information or have rapidly changing data. It allows users to send a block of text along with a query and returns a response based on the text received.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: This video demonstrates the difference between structured and unstructured documents using examples from the Surface Laptop. The presenter shows an unstructured document with no hierarchy or table of contents, and then contrasts it with a structured document that has a clear structure and subtopics. The video then moves on to a demo of using the pre-built and custom question answering skills in Azure's Language Studio. The presenter explains the process of creating a language resource and demonstrates how to use the custom question answering feature.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: To get started with custom question answering, the first step is to create a project. A project is like an empty data store where you can add your data sources. Once you've created a project, you can add URLs, files, or even chit chat as data sources. The next step is to edit the knowledge base by adding questions and answers. The system can also extract questions from semi-structured documents for you.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: The video demonstrates how a multi-turn conversation can be maintained using a service that leverages transformer-based models. The service extracts questions and answers from sources, allowing users to search for specific topics and subtopics. The system can also handle variations in user queries, although the confidence in the response may vary. The service is customizable and can be used to answer frequently asked questions or provide guidance to customers.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: The video discusses the use of custom Q&A models in which users can add their own editorial content and set confidence thresholds based on their specific use cases. It also highlights the ability to include short answer responses for specific questions. The video demonstrates the system's capability to extract the correct information from unstructured documents and provide accurate responses. Finally, it emphasizes the importance of deploying the latest version of the knowledge base to ensure up-to-date information is available.

speaker: Disha Agarwal, Seth Juarez
title: The AI Show: Ep 49 | Question Answering in General Availability
summary: Microsoft's Disha Sinha demonstrates how to build custom question-answering bots using Azure Cognitive Services. She explains the process of deploying and linking a knowledge base to a bot, as well as the simplicity of using pre-built question-answering models. Sinha also discusses future plans for analytics and versioning capabilities. Viewers are encouraged to visit the language.cognitive.microsoft.com website for more information.

speaker: Varsha
title: What’s new with Image Captioning
summary: Varsha, a Program Manager on the Azure Cognitive Services team, discusses the latest breakthrough in image captioning and updates in the Azure Computer Vision 3.0 API. Image captioning generates automatic captions for images, improving accessibility in applications and services. The video covers topics such as computer vision cognitive services, novel object captioning at scale, image captioning examples, and a demo of the API integration. The speaker also provides additional resources for more information.

speaker: Varsha
title: What’s new with Image Captioning
summary: Image captioning systems are trained using datasets that pair images with descriptive sentences. These datasets include a combination of COCO dataset, which has captions for about 80 object classes, and Open Image dataset, which only has object tags. The challenge lies in describing novel objects that are present in testing images but not in the training dataset. The model's performance on out-of-domain object classes is also evaluated. The COCO dataset provides semantic coupling between tags, while the Open Image dataset only provides limited information.

speaker: Varsha
title: What’s new with Image Captioning
summary: The video discusses the advancements in AI models for image recognition and captioning. The new model is able to extract more accurate descriptions of images, including unique objects and the intent behind them. Examples are shown comparing the older model to the latest human parody model, highlighting the improved contextual understanding. The video also demonstrates how to integrate the Azure Cognitive Services API into applications for image recognition.

speaker: Varsha
title: What’s new with Image Captioning
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to use the Computer Vision service to generate image captions. They show how to obtain the necessary key and endpoint for the service, and then use it to analyze images from both URLs and local image files. The presenter tests the service with various images, including one of themselves, and discusses the accuracy of the generated captions.

speaker: Varsha
title: What’s new with Image Captioning
summary: Microsoft's computer vision APIs have been updated with new features, including enhanced image captioning. This capability is already being used in Microsoft's Seeing AI app for visually impaired users, allowing them to take a snapshot and receive a description of their surroundings. Image captioning is also available in Microsoft Office products like Word and PowerPoint. Developers can access these features through the Azure Cognitive Services portal and find resources on Microsoft docs.com.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: Besmira Nushi and Marah Abdin demonstrate two new releases as part of the Responsible AI Toolbox on the AI Show. The first release is the Responsible AI Mitigations library, a Python library for implementing and exploring mitigations for Responsible AI. The second release is the Responsible AI Tracker, a JupyterLab extension for tracking, comparing, and validating Responsible AI mitigations and experiments. The speakers discuss the importance of being responsible with AI and how these tools can help in the process.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: The video introduces the RI Tracker, a tool for comparing, visualizing, and validating different model experiments and improvements. It can be easily installed with a simple pip install command. The video demonstrates how to use the RM mitigations library, a Python library that offers data preprocessing capabilities, such as imputation and encoding pipelines. The video also showcases the RI Tracker interface, where models can be registered and evaluated using test datasets.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: The video discusses the use of a Responsible AI Dashboard to analyze data and identify errors in a machine learning model. The dashboard allows for the examination of specific cohorts within the data, such as married individuals, and reveals a higher error rate compared to non-married individuals. This information can be used to mitigate issues and improve the model. The video also demonstrates the use of a rebalancing mitigation technique to create a balance between the two classes in the dataset.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: The video demonstrates the process of rebalancing a dataset and comparing the performance of a baseline model with a new model. The rebalanced dataset shows improved accuracy but a drop in precision. Cohort analysis is used to examine the performance of different groups within the dataset. The video suggests considering a more targeted approach by focusing on the group with improved accuracy and leaving the other group as it is.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: The video discusses rebalancing the label distribution in a dataset to improve precision. The speaker explains that rebalancing the labels can help address precision problems in different cohorts of data. They demonstrate using a pipeline to rebalance the labels and compare the label distribution before and after rebalancing. The goal is to achieve a more balanced dataset for better performance.

speaker: Besmira Nushi, Marah Abdin
title: Responsible AI Mitigations and Tracker
summary: In this video, Bismira and Mara discuss the use of responsible AI mitigation and tracker tools to improve machine learning models. By focusing on data quality and targeted approaches, they were able to achieve a 4% improvement in accuracy and maintain precision. They emphasize the importance of considering data in the machine learning process and provide resources for further exploration.

speaker: Cheng
title: Anomaly Detector v1.0 Best Practices
summary: Cheng, a Program Manager of Anomaly Detector, shares three tips for designing a monitoring application architecture using Azure Anomaly Detector. Tip 1 suggests using "/entire" for batch scenarios and "/last" for streaming scenarios. Tip 2 advises using a data pre-processor to load and prepare data for anomaly detection. Tip 3 highlights the importance of formatting time series data in JSON and evenly distributing data points on the timeline.

speaker: Cheng
title: Anomaly Detector v1.0 Best Practices
summary: The video provides examples of endpoints for the Anomaly Detector service in Azure. It explains that the /entire endpoint is used for batch scenarios, while the /last endpoint is designed for streaming scenarios. Developers and architects need to keep in mind that they need to create an application that acts as the caller to load and prepare the time series data and make HTTP calls to the Anomaly Detector APIs.

speaker: Cheng
title: Anomaly Detector v1.0 Best Practices
summary: The video discusses the use of Azure Anomaly Detector APIs for data preparation and streaming. It highlights the ability of Power BI to call Anomaly Detector APIs with customized queries. The video also emphasizes the importance of using a sliding window approach for data preparation and explains how it works. A demo is provided to showcase the functionality of the Anomaly Detector APIs.

speaker: Cheng
title: Anomaly Detector v1.0 Best Practices
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the Anomaly Detector API for streaming anomaly detection. It shows how to create a sliding window of data and make API calls to detect anomalies. The video also discusses the importance of data preparation and determining the appropriate window size for streaming or batch scenarios.

speaker: Cheng
title: Anomaly Detector v1.0 Best Practices
summary: Anomaly detection results can be influenced by data preparation, parameters, and the number of data points in an API request. Time-series data formatted into a JSON request object is required, with a minimum of 12 and a maximum of 8,640 data points. Evenly distributed data is ideal, but if it's randomly distributed, aggregation by a unit of time is recommended. Missing data points can be filled using statistical algorithms. Seasonality can be accounted for by specifying a period parameter. Providing full periods of data points plus an additional one improves accuracy. For more information, visit aka.ms/AnomalyDetector.

speaker: Seth, Edward, Sarah

They delve into the details of Custom Neural Voice, its use cases, and provide examples of how customers are using it. The episode also touches on responsible AI considerations.
