However, neural TTS, powered by deep learning and neural networks, can create natural-sounding voices with as little as 300 lines of training data. Custom Neural TTS allows users to create their own unique voices.

speaker: Seth, Edward, Sarah
title: What's new with Speech: Custom Neural Voice now in GA
summary: Regular TTS uses traditional methods and requires more training data, resulting in robotic-sounding voices. Neural TTS uses deep neural networks to create more natural-sounding voices with less training data. Custom Neural Voice allows users to create unique voices for their applications and brands, aligning with their users' needs and use cases. Companies like BBC, Progressive Insurance, and AT&T have already used this technology to create their brand voices.

speaker: Seth, Edward, Sarah
title: What's new with Speech: Custom Neural Voice now in GA
summary: The video discusses the advancements in neural text-to-speech (TTS) technology, specifically focusing on the ability to create custom voices. speaker: Harmke Alkemade and Andreas Kopp

summary: Harmke Alkemade and Andreas Kopp discuss leveraging Azure Machine Learning for Medical Imaging in this episode of The AI Show. speaker: Sarah Bird

speaker: Sarah Bird

speaker: Sarah Bird
title: Being Responsible with Generative AI

The technique of retrieval augmented generation, where data is injected into the prompt, is also an application layer decision that affects the risk of the application. The positioning of the application or technology, in terms of setting expectations and purpose, is also important for its reception and perception by users and the responsible AI community.

speaker: Sarah Bird

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

summary: In machine learning projects, common pitfalls include focusing too much on model training and optimization while neglecting automated data ingestion pipelines, which can lead to biased models. Another challenge is the lack of integration between data scientists and data engineers, resulting in unnecessary data columns and slower training processes. Avoiding these pitfalls is crucial for successful machine learning projects.

The velocity of experimentation and the flexibility of solutions are key factors in managing projects effectively. Finally, it is important to acknowledge that sometimes it may not be possible to achieve the desired outcome, and this should be considered by customers.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

summary: Decision trees and logistic regressions are recommended as starting points in machine learning. Considerations for model development include the difference between the model's environment during development and its real-world application. Surprisingly, customers often underestimate or overestimate the quality of their data, and the hype around big data does not guarantee successful AI solutions. Additionally, some businesses mistakenly believe that people-centric flows can replace data-driven processes.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

summary: Replacing data-driven, structured data flows with people-centric flows is not as effective as fully automated pipelines. Lack of standardization and modularization in machine learning frameworks can create difficulties and inefficiencies. To address these challenges, a solid and flexible framework for machine learning operationalization (MLOps) is necessary, following the principles of DevOps methodology and utilizing machine learning technology. This ensures efficient end-to-end processes for deploying and managing machine learning models.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

summary: MLOps, or Machine Learning Operations, is a set of practices and rules that combine the DevOps methodology with machine learning technology. It involves a flexible framework that allows for end-to-end production of machine learning models. MLOps requires a combination of technical expertise, such as data science and engineering, as well as a culture that promotes collaboration and adaptability. It is essential for successful implementation of machine learning projects in large organizations.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda
title: AI Show | High Level MLOps with Microsoft Data Scientists | Episode 33
summary: Interoperability between different roles is crucial for successful operational projects. Four key principles of MLOps in delivery include change management, ensuring the end-user can effectively use the solution without fear of job replacement, establishing a unified development environment for data scientists, and implementing comprehensive logging to track and troubleshoot model performance. These technical aspects are often underestimated but are essential for efficient collaboration and problem-solving.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda

summary: Logging is crucial for monitoring and fixing issues in machine learning models. It requires a framework and methodology to ensure proper logging and easy searchability. Deploying the architecture in different environments consistently is also important. Additionally, integrating data pre-processing with model training is essential for effective MLOps. These practices improve experimentation velocity, solution flexibility, and overall model performance.

speaker: Seth welcomes Microsoft Data Scientist, Spyros Marketos, ML Engineer, Davide Fornelli and Data Engineer, Samarendra Panda
title: AI Show | High Level MLOps with Microsoft Data Scientists | Episode 33
summary: Invest time in the beginning to set clear expectations and explain that machine learning is a scientific experiment. Avoid relying on a solo superstar and instead build a task force of experts to cover all necessary areas. Clearly articulate possible outcomes to stakeholders, including the potential for success, failure, or anything in between. Avoid overinflating expectations and staff projects properly. When designing a solution, consider the model life cycle and avoid rushing into coding.

Lukawiecki demonstrates how to set up a reproducible workflow using modern notebook environments like Azure ML Compute Instances.

speaker: Rafal Lukawiecki
title: Reproducible Data Science with Machine Learning
summary: Modeling in machine learning is more like research than software development. Traditional development environments like Visual Code or Visual Studio are designed to hide mistakes and errors, but in machine learning, these trials and errors are valuable. Notebooks provide an interactive console where code can be surrounded by explanations and thinking. They allow for documenting the entire process of experimentation, making it easier for others to understand the thinking behind the final results.

speaker: Rafal Lukawiecki
title: Reproducible Data Science with Machine Learning

However, for production deployment, a more traditional IDE-based approach is recommended. This separation between research and software engineering phases allows for easier maintenance and debugging. In larger companies, a separate team may handle model deployment.

speaker: Rafal Lukawiecki

Overall, using notebooks in R programming offers advantages in terms of auditability and explainability.

Studies show that participants rate the neural TTS higher than traditional TTS or hybrid systems, approaching the quality of human recordings.

title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Vijai Kannan discusses data labeling in Azure ML. Data labeling involves detecting and annotating data with labels, such as images, text, video, audio, lidar files, or radar. The process involves creating a labeling project, generating tasks for human labelers, and exporting the labeled dataset. The labeled data is then used to train machine learning models.

speaker: Ayşegül Yönet, Bea Stollnitz, Vijai Kannan
title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: The video discusses the benefits of clustering and pre-labeling in the context of data labeling for machine learning. By grouping similar images together, labelers can more easily and quickly assign labels, reducing cognitive load and improving efficiency. The video also provides a demo of the Azure Machine Learning Studio, showcasing the process of creating a labeling project and the different types of labeling tasks supported, including image classification, object detection, and text labeling.

speaker: Ayşegül Yönet, Bea Stollnitz, Vijai Kannan
title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: Multi-labeling with Named Entity Recognition (NER) allows for assigning multiple labels to a document. This feature supports various text-related project types, with NER currently in private preview. Users can define labels and provide instructions for labeling data. ML-assisted labeling is also available, allowing users to choose whether to use ML assistance in their labeling project. The labeling experience includes machine-processed suggestions, improving efficiency.

speaker: Ayşegül Yönet, Bea Stollnitz, Vijai Kannan
title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: The video demonstrates a labeling service that uses ML-assisted capabilities to save time and improve accuracy. Users can adjust settings like zoom, brightness, and contrast, and have the option to skip images that don't fit any label class. Project managers can review and accept labels, and export the data to various formats. The ML model can be retrained during the labeling process, and the custom-trained model can be downloaded for further inferencing.

speaker: Ayşegül Yönet, Bea Stollnitz, Vijai Kannan
title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: The video discusses the possibility of outsourcing labeling to vendors in order to save time. Microsoft has identified two vendor companies that can provide labor force for labeling. Customers can connect with these vendors through the Azure marketplace. Additionally, there is a capability called labeled dataset import that allows users to import their already labeled data into the labeling tool. There are also plans to integrate with Cognitive Services Custom Vision.

speaker: Ayşegül Yönet, Bea Stollnitz, Vijai Kannan
title: The AI Show: Ep 48 | Fast-Track labeling with Data Labeling Services in Azure ML
summary: Azure ML offers integration with Cognitive Services Custom Vision, allowing users to label data in Azure ML and directly train models in Custom Vision, and vice versa. The integration is currently in preview and will be available in the coming weeks or months. Azure ML also supports labeling for healthcare-related images, starting with x-ray images. Additionally, Azure ML provides an incremental refresh feature that allows users to add new data to an existing labeling project. For more information, users can refer to the provided documentation and provide feedback to the Azure ML team.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Paige and Lo from PyMLadies discuss what data science is and what it means to be a data scientist. They explain that a data scientist is someone who can lead a research project, analyze and clean data, draw conclusions, and create predictive models. While a higher degree is not necessary, data scientists need to have a strong skillset in statistics, coding, and problem-solving. They also highlight the importance of systems thinking in data science.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Appreciation for the complexity of multivariate systems and the ability to collaborate with stakeholders or tackle research problems independently. They are skilled at using data to build predictive models and tell compelling stories. Data scientists must be creative and exploratory, able to identify relevant features and exclude unnecessary ones. They approach their work like detectives, hypothesizing about causes and outcomes and using higher-order thinking skills. Traits admired in data scientists include a healthy appreciation for complexity, collaboration, and the ability to tell compelling stories with data.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Great data scientists are respected for their appreciation of data cleaning and data visualization. They understand that starting with clean and reliable data is crucial for accurate results. They also possess the ability to effectively communicate their findings to stakeholders and the public. Additionally, they ask insightful and targeted questions when approached for their expertise, demonstrating their deep understanding of the subject matter.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Experienced data scientists ask targeted, constructive questions based on their intuition and understanding of the process. They appreciate that no model is perfect and that different interpretations can be valid. Asking the right questions is crucial, as incorrect assumptions can lead to financial losses in business or wasted time in science. Data science is an interdisciplinary field that requires communication and problem-solving skills.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Data science is not the only career path in the field of data. Data engineering and ETL engineering are also in high demand. A healthy data team should have multiple data engineers for every data scientist. Specializing in subfields of data science or specific aspects of machine learning can also be beneficial. It's important to find your niche and pursue what you're good at, rather than trying to be a jack-of-all-trades.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: When hiring for a data science position, it is important to look for candidates who have made contributions to the open source community, such as creating bug fixes or feature enhancements. Personal projects, like blogs or GitHub repositories, and involvement in outreach activities, such as presenting at conferences or founding community groups, are also valuable. Additionally, asking challenging questions during interviews can help assess how candidates handle difficult situations and whether they are willing to admit when they don't know something.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: Successful job candidates have a spark and excitement for the job, according to a Microsoft employee. While education is important, having a GitHub profile with production-level code or contributing to open-source projects can be just as valuable. The ability to handle rejection and setbacks is also crucial, as it demonstrates resilience and character. It's important not to let negative comments or questioning of intelligence affect you, as it often says more about the person making the comments than about you.

speaker: Paige, Lo
title: PyMLadies -- What is Data Science?
summary: The video discusses the importance of not letting negative comments or criticism discourage you in the field of data science. It emphasizes the need for effective communication, collaboration, and a positive attitude in order to thrive in the industry. The video encourages individuals to seek help, ask questions, and continue learning in order to become better and make a positive impact in the field.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Azure AI: Bringing artificial intelligence to every developer
summary: Eric Boyd, Corporate Vice President of Azure AI, delivers a keynote speech at the Global AI Community event. He highlights the ease of use and versatility of Azure AI for both developers and data scientists. Boyd shares an interesting behind-the-scenes story about the development of automated machine learning, which originated from a researcher's frustration with hyperparameter tuning. The collaboration between the research team and Azure AI resulted in a powerful and user-friendly tool.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Azure AI: Bringing artificial intelligence to every developer
summary: Microsoft's AI Assistant discusses the power of automated machine learning (ML) in saving time and making ML accessible to non-experts. They highlight the success of automated ML in achieving top performance in contests and matching data scientists' results. They also mention the new Azure AI service, Personalizer, which uses reinforcement learning to recommend personalized content based on individual user attributes. The focus is on simplicity and ML operations in the latest Azure AI updates.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Azure AI: Bringing artificial intelligence to every developer
summary: Reinforcement learning is a powerful tool in machine learning that allows models to learn and improve based on user responses. It works by predicting the content that will be most effective for a user and then reinforcing the model based on their interactions. This approach is being used by companies like MSN and Xbox, as well as the Women's Tennis Association. Getting started with machine learning can be made easier with resources like the Azure Machine Learning page.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: Rob Chambers, an architect on the speech team in the AI Division, discusses the updates to the Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK. The Cognitive Services Speech SDK is a client library that simplifies the integration of speech features into applications. It allows for interactive recognition with a microphone object, audio streaming, and supports multiple languages. Since Build, the team has been working on consolidating speech capabilities into one API that can be used across different platforms and programming languages.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: The video showcases a device development kit that allows developers to build their own devices with speech capabilities. The demo focuses on interactive applications and demonstrates how to use the code in C++. The video emphasizes the importance of providing intermediate results to users during speech recognition. It also mentions the use of other cognitive services, such as Language Understanding Intelligence Service (LUIS), to understand user intent. The code is simplified and includes creating a SpeechFactory object and a speech recognizer.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: The video demonstrates an intent recognizer that can identify different kinds of explosives. It showcases two interaction modes: a push and talk mode where the recognizer listens for a single command, and a continuous mode where it listens to the user for an extended period. The code for both modes is similar, with the addition of an intermediate result handler for continuous mode. The recognizer is optimized for speed and efficiency, providing accurate results with minimal processing power.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: The video discusses how to optimize speech recognition using the Language Understanding Service (LUIS) in real time. By sending audio to the LUIS service and specifying the LUIS model, the system can better understand user intent. This approach improves application reliability, performance, and ease of programming. The video also demonstrates how LUIS can accurately interpret user input even when the speech is not precise, by extracting intent and entities. The code examples show how to create an intent recognizer and specify the LUIS model.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: Developers can now utilize Keyword Spotting, a technology used in Cortana, to build their own models locally. By downloading the model and integrating it with the Cognitive Services SDK, developers can create their own keywords without relying on cloud services. The code required for this integration is simple and straightforward, making it accessible for developers of all levels. This allows for more advanced speech recognition capabilities and improved user experiences.

speaker: Rob Chambers
title: What’s New with Cognitive Services Speech SDK and Speech Devices SDK
summary: Developers can now perform various operations using the Cognitive Services SDK, such as speech-to-text, command and control, intent recognition, and keyword spotting. The SDK is available on multiple platforms, including Windows, Linux, and Android. The SDK also includes features like noise cancellation and directional beam forming for improved speech recognition. Additionally, the SDK has integrated translation capabilities, allowing developers to build applications that can translate speech into different languages.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Luis Cabrera, the Group Program Manager for Azure Cognitive Search, discusses the new semantic search capability in Azure Cognitive Search. He explains how this feature uses Bing AI models to enable users to find the most relevant information by understanding the meaning of words, not just syntax. The episode includes a demo and provides information on how to enable semantic search for your service.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the challenges of search queries that are complex or don't use exact keywords. They introduce the concept of a lexical ranker, which is commonly used in search services. They also mention the addition of a spell corrector to improve search accuracy. The speaker demonstrates the use of a lexical ranker with a query about the start date of Walmart.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Running a lexical ranker alone may not always yield the most relevant results. To address this, Microsoft has partnered with Bing to develop deep neural network models. They use a passage extraction model to identify representative passages from top documents, and then a semantic ranking model to score the relevance of these passages to the query. This approach improves the accuracy of search results by understanding the meaning behind the query.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Bing has developed a search engine that uses semantic understanding to rank and retrieve information from personal databases and documents. This innovation allows users to find content faster within their own data, such as human resources applications or support ticket databases. Additionally, the search engine can extract passages that not only relate to the content but also provide answers to specific questions, enhancing the search experience.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video showcases the capabilities of Bing's AI-powered search engine, which can extract relevant information from documents and provide captions for each document. The example used is searching for COVID-19 symptoms, where the search engine retrieves research papers and public data to find the answer. The video demonstrates the impact of features like spelling correction, semantic ranking, and answer captions in improving search results.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The World Health Organization has identified common symptoms of COVID-19, including fever, tiredness, and dry cough. Other symptoms such as shortness of breath, aches and pains, and sore throat are also possible indicators. However, it is important to note that ibuprofen, commonly used for sore throat relief, may not be recommended for COVID-19. Semantic search technology is being used to quickly triage relevant documents and provide accurate answers to user queries.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Semantic search is a powerful tool that allows users to query a service using a REST API. With the help of an extension like the VS Code extension for Azure Cognitive Search, users can easily make queries and retrieve relevant results. By specifying search fields, language, speller, and other parameters, users can refine their queries and obtain more accurate and meaningful results. Additionally, the introduction of the search.answers component enhances the user experience by providing informative answers to queries.

speaker: Luis Cabrera
title: Find meaningful insights using semantic capabilities in Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Azure Cognitive Search now offers semantic search capabilities, allowing users to find meaningful insights from their indexed documents without the need for re-indexing or re-reading. By simply changing a few lines of code, users can enable semantic answers, captions, and ranking in real-time. The feature is currently in preview and interested users can fill out a form to join the preview program. More information can be found at aka.ms/semanticpreview.

speaker: Saurya Das
title: Run Azure Machine Learning anywhere
summary: Saurya Das, a Product Manager in Azure Machine Learning, discusses running Azure Machine Learning anywhere using Azure Arc and Kubernetes. This integration allows data scientists to utilize existing Kubernetes infrastructure on-premises or in multicloud environments for machine learning. Azure Arc enables running Azure Machine Learning jobs on platforms like GKE, Amazon, and even on-premises. By standardizing on Kubernetes and leveraging Azure Arc, users can have a consistent experience across different environments.

speaker: Saurya Das
title: Run Azure Machine Learning anywhere
summary: Azure Portal allows users to track and manage on-premises and cloud clusters in a single interface. The portal provides centralized governance, policy application, monitoring, and security hazard visibility. Users can customize the portal to display specific information. The Kubernetes services section shows different types of Kubernetes assets, including Azure's managed service (Azure Kubernetes Service) and clusters brought to Azure using Azure Arc. Data scientists can access these clusters without needing to know about Kubernetes, as IT operators can set up the clusters and enable Azure Machine Learning.

speaker: Saurya Das
title: Run Azure Machine Learning anywhere
summary: To set up a cluster for data scientists, an IT admin needs to install Azure Arc and Azure Machine Learning bits. Once set up, data scientists can access the cluster through the Azure Machine Learning Studio. They can choose from Managed Compute or Attached Compute, which integrates with Kubernetes. Data scientists can select a Kubernetes cluster and attach it as a target for running training jobs. They can also specify a namespace for deployment. This process can also be done by the ID operator.

speaker: Saurya Das
title: Run Azure Machine Learning anywhere
summary: Azure Machine Learning now allows users to leverage their existing on-premises Kubernetes clusters for machine learning tasks. This means that data scientists and developers can take advantage of Azure Machine Learning's features, such as dashboards and logging, without having to migrate their clusters to the cloud. By simply changing the compute target in their notebooks, users can seamlessly utilize the excess capacity of their on-premises clusters. For more information, visit the Azure Machine Learning GitHub page.

speaker: Sethu Raman, Seth
title: Managed Endpoints
summary: Sethu Raman, a Product Manager in Azure ML, discusses Managed Endpoints in Azure Machine Learning in this episode of The AI Show. Managed Endpoints provides users with the ability to deploy and operationalize models with out-of-the-box capabilities. Sethu demonstrates how to deploy and score a GPU model, highlighting the development experience with CLI and local deployment, as well as how to perform a safe rollout using metrics and log analytics integration. Managed Endpoints simplifies software deployments for machine learning and offers managed infrastructure, ops support, and debuggability features.

speaker: Sethu Raman, Seth
title: Managed Endpoints
summary: Rolling out software safely can be challenging, but using Machine Learning can make it easier. In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to deploy a Machine Learning model on GPU servers in Azure. They show the necessary files and configurations, and then run the commands to create the endpoint. They also demonstrate how to retrieve the endpoint details and test the model. This video provides a step-by-step guide for deploying and debugging models in the cloud.

speaker: Sethu Raman, Seth
title: Managed Endpoints
summary: Users can debug and deploy models locally using the concept of local deployments. By adding the flag "--local" to commands like "azml endpoint create", users can execute commands and debug locally in a Docker container. Additionally, users can perform a safe roll out by updating the YAML file and using the "azml endpoint Update" command. Azure Monitor integration allows users to monitor the traffic split between different deployments.

speaker: Sethu Raman, Seth
title: Managed Endpoints
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates the process of deploying and updating machine learning models using Managed Endpoints. They show how to monitor metrics, identify and fix errors, and perform safe rollouts. The presenter emphasizes the benefits of Managed Endpoints in managing deployments and ensuring efficient model performance. Viewers are directed to a link for a hands-on exercise to further explore the topic.

speaker: Shivani Santosh Sambare
title: The AI Show: Ep 47 | High-performance serving with Triton Inference Server in AzureML
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Shivani Santosh Sambare demonstrates high-performance serving with Triton Inference Server in AzureML. Model deployment and serving can be challenging, but AzureML offers managed online endpoints that provide infrastructure maintenance, safe rollout, security, and monitoring. Triton Inference Server supports multiple frameworks and runs models concurrently on GPUs for maximum throughput. With AzureML, users can focus on their machine learning models and deployment.

speaker: Shivani Santosh Sambare
title: The AI Show: Ep 47 | High-performance serving with Triton Inference Server in AzureML
summary: The video discusses the deployment of multiple models to a single endpoint using Azure Machine Learning. The deployment YAML file is used to specify the endpoint and its deployments. The models are passed to the endpoint in the Triton model repository format, eliminating the need for a scoring script. The deployment process takes under 10 minutes, and the outcome is demonstrated in the video.

speaker: Shivani Santosh Sambare
title: The AI Show: Ep 47 | High-performance serving with Triton Inference Server in AzureML
summary: In this video, the speaker demonstrates how to deploy models using Azure Machine Learning Studio and the Triton Inference Server. They explain that the environment is pre-built and pulls the necessary image from the Triton server. They also show how to call the endpoint and score against different models. The speaker emphasizes that using Triton makes high-performance inferencing on GPUs and deploying models easy. They provide links to documentation, samples, and a blog for further information.

speaker: Satya Mallick, Ye Lu, Him Wai Ng, Seth
title: AI Show | 2021 OpenCV AI Competition | Grand Prize Winners | Cortic Tigers | Episode 32
summary: Satya Mallick from OpenCV introduces the grand prize winners of the 2021 OpenCV AI Competition, Ye Lu and Him Wai Ng from Team Cortic Tigers. The winners included projects for neonatal care and an autonomous wheelchair.

speaker: Satya Mallick, Ye Lu, Him Wai Ng, Seth
title: AI Show | 2021 OpenCV AI Competition | Grand Prize Winners | Cortic Tigers | Episode 32
summary: Ye Lu and Michael, from team Cortic Tigers, have developed an open-source software project called the Cortex Edge Platform (CEP). It offers a visual programming interface for beginners, with functions such as computer vision and speech recognition. As users progress, they can convert their visual programs into Python code for more advanced editing. The software also supports distributed AI computation using the OAK-D Lite device.

speaker: Satya Mallick, Ye Lu, Him Wai Ng, Seth
title: AI Show | 2021 OpenCV AI Competition | Grand Prize Winners | Cortic Tigers | Episode 32
summary: want to build your own robot, control your smart home, or distribute AI computation across multiple devices, the OAK-D and its software tools make it easy. speaker: Satya Mallick, Ye Lu, Him Wai Ng, Seth
title: AI Show | 2021 OpenCV AI Competition | Grand Prize Winners | Cortic Tigers | Episode 32

Charlie, a LEGO robot, serves as a prototype for an in-home assistant, showcasing the possibilities of AI.

speaker: Satya Mallick, Ye Lu, Him Wai Ng, Seth
title: AI Show | 2021 OpenCV AI Competition | Grand Prize Winners | Cortic Tigers | Episode 32
summary: The 2021 OpenCV AI competition showcased innovative projects, including a backpack for blind assistance and the OAK-D-Lite camera. The OAK-D-Lite is a compact and affordable camera that can run neural networks and perform depth estimation at 200 frames per second. Priced at $79, it is a powerful tool for AI enthusiasts and a great gift for kids. The competition's success has led to plans for future competitions and community collaborations.

speaker: Salil Vadhan
title: The Science Behind WhiteNoise: Differential Privacy
summary: Salil Vadhan, leader of the Privacy Tools Project at Harvard University, discusses the concept of differential privacy and its importance in protecting sensitive data. He explains how the publication of seemingly innocuous aggregate statistics can pose privacy risks and highlights the need for careful handling of such data. Vadhan also shares examples of vulnerabilities in different domains, emphasizing the significance of differential privacy in safeguarding personal information.

speaker: Salil Vadhan
title: The Science Behind WhiteNoise: Differential Privacy
summary: Differential privacy is a quantitative theory that aims to protect individual level data while allowing for statistical analysis. It achieves this by injecting random noise into computations, obscuring the effect of each individual while still allowing useful statistical signal. This theory offers a level of privacy protection that can be quantified using a privacy loss parameter. Many data analysis tasks can be done in a differentially private manner, with minimal cost and the possibility of generating synthetic data.

speaker: Salil Vadhan
title: The Science Behind WhiteNoise: Differential Privacy
summary: The video discusses the concept of rich synthetic data with differential privacy, which involves publishing a dataset that preserves statistical properties of the original data while protecting individual privacy. The video highlights the challenges in making this concept practical and mentions the use of differential privacy by organizations like the US Census Bureau and large tech companies. The goal is to enable wider adoption of differential privacy through initiatives like the White Noise system and the OpenDP open source software project. The video also emphasizes the importance of incorporating differential privacy into data repositories to enable wider sharing of sensitive data while maintaining privacy protections.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: Miguel Fierro joins Seth on the AI Show to discuss building recommender systems. They cover the creation of Recommenders, the top open-source repository on GitHub, and how customers are utilizing it. Miguel explains the importance of personalized experiences and how recommendation systems can scale to thousands of customers. While not as good as a real person, recommendation systems offer a middle ground between uniformity and personalized service.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: AI can provide two major opportunities for businesses. Firstly, it can enhance customer experience by understanding and meeting their unmet needs. Secondly, it can contribute to economic growth by either increasing revenue or reducing costs. Recommendation systems, for example, have proven to be effective in boosting revenue for e-commerce and media companies. However, creating scalable recommendation systems can be challenging. Microsoft has developed an open-source repository called Microsoft recommenders to assist businesses in building recommendation systems on Azure.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: Microsoft has developed an open-source repository called Microsoft recommenders to help people build recommendation systems on Azure. The repository consists of three main components: the library, examples, and a comprehensive test infrastructure. The test infrastructure includes various categories of tests, such as unit tests, data validation, functionality, integration, performance, responsibility, fairness, transparency, explainability, and security. Currently, the repository runs around 900 tests per day to ensure the library's robustness and adherence to Microsoft's standards.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: The video discusses different versions of Python and an interesting recent development in scaling tests using Azure ML. The video also introduces the library called "percent" which aims to simplify the usage of recommendation systems. It covers various components such as datasets, evaluation metrics, and machine learning models. The video concludes by highlighting the examples provided in Jupyter notebooks, which are useful for learning and building recommendation systems.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: The Microsoft Recommenders library is a popular open-source machine learning library for building recommendation systems. It provides a simple and effective way to train, predict, and compute metrics using various models. The library has gained popularity and is now the top-rated machine learning library at Microsoft on GitHub. Many internal and external teams at Microsoft are already using it, and it is a valuable resource for those looking to build recommendation systems.

speaker: Miguel Fierro, Seth
title: Building Recommender Systems
summary: If you want to get started with recommenders, the best strategy is to start with something that already works. Instead of creating something from scratch, find a simple example and make sure it runs on your computer. Then, replace the example dataset with your own and build from there. This approach will give you access to around 20 different algorithms to try. Additionally, there are examples available for deploying your machine learning model on Azure.

speaker: Robbie
title: Bing Visual Search
summary: Robbie discusses Bing Visual Search, which allows users to identify objects and text within images. The Bing Visual Search API provides developers with access to intelligent visual search capabilities, enabling them to build image applications and smarter imaging devices. Additionally, developers can extend visual search capabilities by building skills and enriching Microsoft's products and services. The Visual Search Developer Platform allows developers to create new scenarios by providing new knowledge or actions.

speaker: Robbie
title: Bing Visual Search
summary: Developers can leverage the Bing Visual Search API to create skills that provide information based on images. For example, a skill can identify a fruit and suggest recipes, or recognize a landmark and provide relevant information. Developers can set up their skills by defining visual intents, which determine when the skill should be triggered based on the content of the image. They can also choose what data to receive, such as annotations, raw images, object detection, or OCR.

speaker: Robbie
title: Bing Visual Search
summary: In this video, Robbie from Bing Visual Search explains how to build skills on top of Bing Visual Search. He demonstrates how to create a skill that recognizes food items in images and provides relevant information and search results. He also showcases a fun skill called "hotdog-or-not" that determines whether an image contains a hotdog. Robbie encourages viewers to visit bingvisualsearch.com for more information and documentation on building skills with Bing Visual Search.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki
title: How to Test Models for Fairness with Fairlearn Deep-Dive
summary: Mehrnoosh Sameki, Senior Product Manager at Azure AI, introduces Fairlearn, an open-source machine learning fairness toolkit. Fairlearn allows developers to assess and mitigate fairness issues in their AI systems, focusing on negative impacts for groups defined by race, gender, age, or disability status. The toolkit includes an assessment dashboard and strategies for mitigating fairness issues, empowering data scientists and business leaders to navigate trade-offs between fairness and performance.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki
title: How to Test Models for Fairness with Fairlearn Deep-Dive
summary: Fairlearn is a tool that helps assess and mitigate fairness issues in machine learning models. It consists of an assessment dashboard that provides high-level and detailed views of fairness impacts on different groups, and a set of algorithms for mitigating these issues. Fairlearn supports various fairness definitions and can be easily integrated into existing machine learning pipelines. It is now being integrated into Azure Machine Learning for easy access. A demo showcases how Fairlearn can be used to assess and mitigate fairness issues in a binary classification problem.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki
title: How to Test Models for Fairness with Fairlearn Deep-Dive
summary: The video discusses the use of Fairlearn's mitigation algorithm, GridSearch, to address unfairness in loan approval decisions. The speaker analyzes the accuracy rates and disparities across genders in the model's predictions. They also examine false positive and false negative rates, as well as the disparity in selection rates. GridSearch is described as a state-of-the-art algorithm that minimizes classification errors while adhering to user-defined fairness constraints. The speaker demonstrates how to implement GridSearch and fit it to the training data.

speaker: Mehrnoosh Sameki
title: How to Test Models for Fairness with Fairlearn Deep-Dive
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Fairlearn, an open-source Python package, to assess and mitigate bias in machine learning models. It shows how to navigate a dashboard that allows users to compare the accuracy and fairness of different models, and make informed decisions about which model to deploy based on their specific context and requirements. Fairlearn is also being integrated into Azure Machine Learning, providing a similar dashboard experience within the platform.

speaker: Jingya Huang, Cassie Breviu
title: Easier, Faster Training for your Hugging Face models
summary: Jingya Huang from Hugging Face joins Cassie Breviu to discuss how to use Optimum + ONNX Runtime to accelerate the training of Hugging Face models. They demonstrate how to fine-tune the DeBERTa model with Trainer and showcase the performance gains achieved by leveraging the ONNX Runtime backend. Optimum is an extension of the Transformers Library that provides performance optimization tools for training and running models efficiently on targeted devices. ONNX Runtime is a module within Optimum that offers training and inference APIs for accelerated performance.

speaker: Jingya Huang, Cassie Breviu
title: Easier, Faster Training for your Hugging Face models
summary: The video discusses the training API integrations in the Optimum runtime and the Hugging Face ecosystem. The Optimum runtime utilizes optimization techniques such as computation graph optimization, memory planning, and kernel optimization to accelerate training. The video also highlights the integration of the fuse add-on optimizer and the support for efficient mix precision training. speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: Emma, a Senior Program Manager at Microsoft, introduces the ONNX Runtime, a high-performance inferencing and training engine for machine learning models. ONNX Runtime has been adopted by various Microsoft products, achieving an average of 2.9x inference speedup. The video discusses ONNX Runtime quantization and ONNX Runtime mobile, which further accelerate model inference with smaller model and runtime sizes. The ONNX Runtime is evolving for both cloud-based and on-device inference.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: ONNX Runtime, a high-performance inference engine, is being used by a variety of popular frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Keras. It offers APIs in multiple languages and is compatible with Windows and Mac. ONNX Runtime allows users to easily plug it into their existing server pipeline and provides an open and extensible architecture for optimizing and accelerating machine learning inference.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: ONNX Runtime, integrated into various platforms including Azure ML and Oracle, is used by millions of devices and processes billions of requests daily. It powers flagship products like Office and offers improved performance compared to previous solutions. The newest feature, INT8 quantization, enables on-device inference by reducing model size and accelerating performance. While quantization may introduce accuracy loss, ONNX Runtime's INT8 quantization reduces storage by four times and offers more efficient computation.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: ONNX Runtime quantization to significantly improve performance and reduce model size. By applying ONNX Runtime INT8 quantization on transformer models, researchers observed promising results in both performance and model size. On a large machine, ONNX Runtime INT8 quantization accelerated inference performance by about three times, while on a smaller machine, it improved performance by around 60%. Additionally, the model size was reduced by almost four times compared to the original PyTorch model. Accuracy was also maintained, making this approach a valuable optimization technique for NLP tasks.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: The video demonstrates the end-to-end workflow of ONNX Runtime INT8 quantization. It shows how to convert a model from FP32 format to ONNX format using PyTorch or TensorFlow, and then quantize it from FP32 to INT8 using the provided quantization tool. The quantized model can be used for inference in ONNX Runtime. The video also showcases the different quantization modes available and provides performance and accuracy results for a quantized PyTorch model.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: The video discusses the process of ONNX Runtime quantization, which involves optimizing and quantizing models to improve performance and reduce model size. The optimization step is performed before quantization, and is only necessary for transformer models. The quantization step can be done using the ONNX Runtime quantization API, resulting in a model that is approximately a quarter of the original size. The performance and accuracy of the quantized model using ONNX Runtime is comparable to the original model.

speaker: Emma
title: Faster and Lighter Model Inference with ONNX Runtime from Cloud to Client
summary: The ONNX Runtime offers a new feature called ONNX Runtime Mobile, which focuses on reducing the size of the runtime package for on-device inference on smartphones and edge devices. This feature includes an optimized format called ONNX Runtime format and the ability to build the runtime with only the necessary operators for a specific model, further reducing the runtime size. The benchmark results show that the core ONNX Runtime mobile package can achieve a size of less than 300 kilobytes on both Android and iOS platforms, making on-device inference more feasible. The ONNX Runtime is an open-source project, and tutorials and examples can be found on the GitHub repository.

speaker: Parashar

speaker: Parashar

speaker: Parashar

speaker: Parashar
