summary: Andreas Kopp and Harmke Alkemade join Seth Juarez to discuss Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning. They explain that Federated Learning is a privacy-preserving technology that allows multiple organizations to collaboratively train a model without sharing their training data. They highlight the importance of protecting privacy and intellectual property in cross-organizational machine learning scenarios. The video includes a demo of a Global Federated Learning setup using Azure ML and NVIDIA FLare.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: Federated learning is a technology that allows multiple organizations to collaboratively train a machine learning model without sharing any training data. The process involves a central server hosting a global model, which is distributed to all participants. Each organization trains the model using their local data and sends back the trained weights to the central server for aggregation. This approach preserves data privacy while benefiting from the collective knowledge. It is similar to parallelizing large machine learning algorithms but focuses on preserving data privacy.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: Federated learning allows for model deployment and inferencing while maintaining data privacy. Only the model weights are shared and aggregated, making it ideal for healthcare settings and IP protection. A demo setup using Azure Machine Learning and Nvidia Flare shows how a global setting can be deployed in 30 minutes. Flare handles the distribution of training assets and can be integrated with existing training code in PyTorch or TensorFlow. Additional privacy measures like homomorphic encryption or differential privacy can be easily added.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video demonstrates the deployment of a Federated Learning solution for medical imaging on Azure. The repository contains configuration files for NVIDIA Flare and two applications for pneumonia detection using chest x-ray images. GitHub workflows are provided to set up the infrastructure and prepare the dataset. The solution allows for the simulation of multiple clients and a Federated server to enable distributed learning across different locations.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video explains how to set up a Federated Learning solution using a science virtual machine as a Federated server and three different workspaces as clients. Each workspace represents a different hospital in a different region, with its own private dataset. The server communicates with the clients using Nvidia Flare, and the overall solution is configured using a project.yaml file. Startup packages are generated to initiate the communication between the server and clients before training begins.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video discusses the setup and communication process for federated learning using Nvidia Flare. The communication is established between the Nvidia Flare controller and the compute instances within each workspace. The local clients perform the training on their machines with private data and send the trained models back to the Federated Server. The server then aggregates the local models into a global model. The communication setup is done using the Nvidia Flare SDK. The video also briefly showcases the training script for a PyTorch model using the Nvidia Flare Python SDK.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video discusses how to train models using the NVIDIA Fleet Command SDK. The training script for data scientists remains familiar, with some specific instructions for aggregating different models. The process involves setting up a data science virtual machine, connecting to the NVIDIA Fleet admin client, verifying client connections, submitting training jobs, and monitoring their progress. The notebook runs on the controlling compute instance in the workspace, while the clients run in the workspace.

speaker: Andreas Kopp, Harmke Alkemade, Seth Juarez
title: Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning
summary: In this video, the presenter discusses the use of Federated Learning with Azure Machine Learning. They demonstrate how to use a data science virtual machine to control the training process across multiple hospitals while keeping the data local. They also highlight the use of a central workspace to track metrics from the local experiments. The presenter provides links to a repository and a Towards Data Science article for further information.

speaker: Anna Roth
title: AI Show | What's New With Form Recognizer
summary: Anna Roth, a Program Manager on the Cognitive Services Team, introduces the latest updates in Azure Form Recognizer. Form Recognizer is a Cognitive Service that allows users to extract text, key/value pairs, and table data from documents. Users can train custom models to extract structured data from their forms and documents. The updates include version 2.1 Preview, new SDKs, enhancements to table extraction and detection, support for global currencies, Azure Gov, and enhanced security features.

speaker: Anna Roth
title: AI Show | What's New With Form Recognizer
summary: The video discusses the new features of Form Recognizer v2.1, including language support for Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish, as well as support for Chinese in layout extraction. The update also includes support for checkboxes and selection marks, recognition of printed and handwritten text, model composition for calling multiple models with a single ID, friendly model names, a new pre-built model for business cards, new locales for pre-built receipts, and overall quality improvements.

speaker: Anna Roth
title: AI Show | What's New With Form Recognizer
summary: Model Compose is designed to solve the problem of recognizing different form layouts. With Form Recognizer, you can train custom models for each template or layout. However, if you have multiple forms and don't know which one you'll receive, Model Compose allows you to send all the forms together and it will classify and provide key-value pairs for the specific form. It uses a classification algorithm to determine which model to use.

speaker: Anna Roth
title: AI Show | What's New With Form Recognizer
summary: The video demonstrates how to train a custom model using Form Recognizer. The presenter labels key-value pairs in a form and trains a model with just five examples. They then compose this model with another template, allowing the model to extract content from either form. The video also mentions that up to 100 models can be composed together.

speaker: Anna Roth
title: AI Show | What's New With Form Recognizer
summary: Form Recognizer V2 and 2.1 preview introduces Model Compose, a feature that allows users to combine multiple models into a single composed model. This video demonstrates how to use the tool to extract key-value pairs and table structures from forms, including PDFs and image files. The video also provides information on where to find resources and documentation for Form Recognizer.

speaker: Christina
title: Cognitive Services
summary: Christina, a Program Manager on the Cognitive Services platform Teams, discusses how the Metropolitan Museum of Arts used Cognitive Services and Spark to enhance their open access initiative. By applying intelligent annotations through Computer Vision and Text Analytics, the museum made their collection more searchable and accessible. This allowed users to explore the art pieces in a more interactive and engaging way. The integration of Cognitive Services with Spark enabled the museum to enrich their dataset and provide a unique experience for visitors.

speaker: Christina
title: Cognitive Services
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (MET) used Computer Vision, Cognitive Services, and Apache Spark to create an accessible search engine called Art Explorer. By applying intelligent annotations to the images, users can search for specific categories, such as images of people or outdoor scenes. The MET also used Text Analytics to connect the images to curated descriptions and external references, allowing users to learn more about the artwork. The project was completed in a three-day hackathon and the code is available on GitHub.

speaker: Micheline harris
title: When And When Not To Use Deep Learning
summary: Micheline Harris, a software engineer at Microsoft, discusses when to use deep learning versus classical machine learning in this episode of the AI Show. She emphasizes that while deep learning can be powerful for tasks with large amounts of data or insufficient accuracy with other methods, it is often overused. Harris suggests using classical machine learning for straightforward feature engineering or when there is a need for varied algorithm choices. She also clarifies the difference between training and test data sets.

speaker: Micheline harris
title: When And When Not To Use Deep Learning
summary: Classical machine learning is preferred over deep learning when there is a need for varied algorithm choices, limited compute resources, simplicity and explainability, fast prototyping, and acceptable accuracy on test data. On the other hand, deep learning is more suitable for complex feature engineering tasks, such as object detection in color images or classifying symphony music with multiple objects and complex features.

speaker: Micheline harris
title: When And When Not To Use Deep Learning
summary: The video discusses the use of deep learning in computer vision tasks, particularly for large and complex images. It highlights the benefits of deep learning, such as improved accuracy with large datasets, and the use of data augmentation techniques. The video also provides an overview of various Python packages for deep learning, ranging from low-level frameworks like TensorFlow to higher-level libraries like Keras and PyTorch. It concludes by summarizing the landscape of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning.

speaker: Tracy Chen, Bea Stollnitz
title: AI Show: Live | Dec 3 | Azure Machine Learning Batch Endpoints | Episode 42
summary: Tracy Chen, a product manager for Azure Machine Learning Batch, discusses batch endpoints in this episode of the AI Show. Batch endpoints allow users to deploy models for batch inference, where latency is not critical and results are obtained in minutes, hours, or days. In contrast, online endpoints are for real-time inference with low latency requirements. Batch endpoints manage computer resources, automatically bringing up a cluster for batch inference jobs and storing the results in cloud storage. Users only pay for the resources used.

speaker: Tracy Chen, Bea Stollnitz
title: AI Show: Live | Dec 3 | Azure Machine Learning Batch Endpoints | Episode 42
summary: Latency is the key difference between online and batch endpoints. If latency requirements are relaxed and cost is a concern, batch endpoints can be a good choice. Batch endpoints allow for accumulation of data and can be invoked on a schedule, resulting in cost savings. Batch endpoints provide a more intuitive and easier-to-use command line interface-based experience compared to parallel run step. The v2 CLI, REST, and UI can be used to interact with batch endpoints.

speaker: Tracy Chen, Bea Stollnitz
title: AI Show: Live | Dec 3 | Azure Machine Learning Batch Endpoints | Episode 42
summary: To use a v2 COI for batch inference using batch endpoints, first create a batch endpoint with a unique name. Then, create a batch deployment under the endpoint using a YAML file to define the deployment. Add the set default parameter to make the deployment the default one under the endpoint. Finally, invoke the batch endpoint with a data reference pointing to the input data.

speaker: Tracy Chen, Bea Stollnitz
title: AI Show: Live | Dec 3 | Azure Machine Learning Batch Endpoints | Episode 42
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to use a command-line interface to set up a CI/CD pipeline for training and deploying machine learning models. They show how to create a batch endpoint, invoke the endpoint, and switch between different model versions. The video also covers using GitHub Actions to automate the development process. Useful links are provided for further information on batch endpoints, deployments, and CI/CD pipelines.

speaker: Wenxin Wei and Lifeng Wei
title: The AI Show: Ep 54 | Building NLP models with Azure ML AutoML
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Wenxin Wei and Lifeng Wei demonstrate how to build NLP models using Azure ML AutoML. They discuss text classification, multi-class and multi-label tasks, and text named entity recognition (NER), highlighting the support for 104 languages. They also mention the benefits of distributed training, seamless integration with the Azure Data Labeling service, and ML Ops capabilities.

speaker: Wenxin Wei and Lifeng Wei
title: The AI Show: Ep 54 | Building NLP models with Azure ML AutoML
summary: Autumn NLP offers NLP training and ML ops capabilities with multi-language support. They have experimented with different models for various languages and provide the best models for different scenarios. Users can specify the language code and Autumn NLP will choose the appropriate model. The user experience involves creating an experiment in an existing workspace, preparing labeled and pre-processed data, and using a GPU cluster for accelerated training. The example shown involves categorizing academic papers into specific categories based on their text.

speaker: Wenxin Wei and Lifeng Wei
title: The AI Show: Ep 54 | Building NLP models with Azure ML AutoML
summary: To enable distributed training for NLP tasks, you can use the AutoML feature in Azure. By setting a few lines of code, you can run multiple algorithms on multiple machines, allowing for parallel training. This approach supports both multi-nodes and multi-GPU setups. The system ensures that all machines collaborate and provide update information to accelerate the training process.

speaker: Wenxin Wei and Lifeng Wei
title: The AI Show: Ep 54 | Building NLP models with Azure ML AutoML
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of building natural language processing (NLP) models using Azure ML AutoML. They explain how to set up distributed training, select the text for training, and configure the AutoML settings. They also mention that AutoML trains only one model and does not require ranking or optimization. The speaker highlights the benefits of multilingual support and the improved performance of the fine-tuned models. They provide a link to the official documentation for more information.

speaker: Shivani Patel
title: MLOps feature dive: Manage your assets, artifacts and code
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Shivani Patel, a program manager on the Azure Machine Learning platform team, discusses the importance of managing assets, artifacts, and code in MLOps workflows. She demonstrates how to track and visualize datasets, experiments, and models using Azure Machine Learning Studio. Versioning and registering these components allows teams to collaborate, reproduce models, and identify biases in datasets.

speaker: Shivani Patel
title: MLOps feature dive: Manage your assets, artifacts and code
summary: In this video, the importance of managing code, datasets, experiments, and models in the context of MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) is discussed. The video emphasizes the need for proper tracking and documentation of these components to save time, effort, and ensure reproducibility. It also highlights the benefits of using Azure Machine Learning Services to manage and track datasets, code, and experiments, providing a centralized and validated environment for data scientists to collaborate effectively.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Building awesome experiences in Microsoft Teams (Part 1 of 3)
summary: Gary Pretty, a senior engineer on the Bot Framework SDK Team, discusses how the Bot Framework makes it easier to develop engaging experiences in Microsoft Teams. He demonstrates a conversational bot in Teams using the TeamsActivityHandler class and explores the available Bot Framework samples for Teams bot development. He also showcases how to build a bot for a Teams Search Extension using a sample from the GitHub repository.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Building awesome experiences in Microsoft Teams (Part 1 of 3)
summary: The Teams Activity handler in Microsoft Teams allows developers to easily build conversational experiences. It extends the number of methods available for Team-specific actions, such as joining a conversation or reacting to a message. The handler eliminates the need for manual parsing of incoming events and simplifies the process of sending messages back. Developers can find examples and samples in the Bot Builder Samples repository on GitHub.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Building awesome experiences in Microsoft Teams (Part 1 of 3)
summary: In this video, the speaker demonstrates how to use Teams Messaging Extensions in the Microsoft Bot Framework. They show an example of a search Messaging Extension and explain that Teams Apps can have both Extensions and bot interaction. The speaker highlights the ease of building these experiences with only a few lines of code. They also mention the ability to react to various events in Teams and integrate with third-party services.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: Gary Pretty, a Program Manager on the conversational AI team, demonstrates how to build bots with Azure Bot Service. He showcases the latest features and provides a step-by-step guide on building and deploying a bot using Azure Bot Service and Bot Framework Composer. The goal is to make the process of building conversational apps faster and more collaborative. The video also highlights the new applied AI services in Azure that aim to provide a seamless and productive experience for developers.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: The Bot Framework Composer now includes a New Rocket Shipman menu that guides users through the necessary steps to create and enhance their bots. It provides links to Microsoft Learn and Microsoft Docs for easy access to relevant information. Additionally, the new authoring editor allows users to build multimodal conversations with text, speech, suggested actions, and attachments, including adaptive cards. The editor simplifies the process of writing complex responses, making it more intuitive for users.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: The latest version of Composer offers a more intuitive and user-friendly experience for building bots. It includes enhanced testing and debugging tools, integrated web chat for real-time interaction with the bot, and a fully-featured developer IDE. The new component model allows for easy extension of Composer and bot customization. These updates make it easier for both beginners and experienced developers to create sophisticated bot experiences.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: Microsoft Teams developers now have access to a new package manager that allows them to easily build teams-based bots. This package manager provides a range of components and features, including message extensions, team and channel information, and the ability to add new actions to the canvas. Developers can also create and share their own packages, making specialized functionality accessible to anyone. Additionally, the package manager enables one-click publishing to Azure and simplifies the configuration of channels via the Connections tab.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: Microsoft Teams has made it easier for users to configure channels and install apps. With a single click, users can enable Microsoft Teams on their Azure resource and receive instructions on how to install it into Teams. Additionally, users can now find and install packages for platforms like Google, Twilio, Slack, Facebook, WebEx, and Alexa. This new feature was announced at Build and is part of Composer version 2.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Learn how to build bots with Azure Bot Service's comprehensive development experience
summary: Microsoft has released Composer version 2, a major step forward in building bots with Azure Bot Service. The update includes pre-built experiences and templates that incorporate best practices and customer feedback. Composer now supports C# and Node in preview, and integrates with Microsoft Graph for calendar and people search capabilities. Additionally, Composer can be used in conjunction with Power Virtual Agents, allowing for easy collaboration and customization.

speaker: Anna Thomas
title: LearnAI: LUIS – Notes from the Field
summary: Anna Thomas, an applied data scientist at Microsoft, discusses the challenges of deploying enterprise-ready LUIS (Language Understanding Intelligent Service) models at scale. She emphasizes the importance of finding a balance between the number of intents and options within each intent to ensure optimal performance. Thomas also suggests breaking down large intents into smaller sub-intents to improve accuracy.

speaker: Anna Thomas
title: LearnAI: LUIS – Notes from the Field
summary: Having too many intents or overlapping intents can cause issues in a conversational AI model. Finding a balance is important. Versioning allows for cloning the model at different stages to try out different approaches. Collaboration tools enable multiple collaborators to work on the same model. Patterns, introduced in May 2018, are a tool to generalize common utterances and increase intent accuracy without adding extra utterances.

speaker: Anna Thomas
title: LearnAI: LUIS – Notes from the Field
summary: The video discusses different entity types in Microsoft's Language Understanding Intelligent Service (LUIS) and provides guidance on when to use each type. The speaker recommends using simple entities for extracting single concepts that are not well-formatted, and list entities for values that match exactly to a predefined list. The video also suggests using hierarchical entities for managing complex and varied lists. Additionally, the speaker mentions using post-processing techniques, such as hash lookups, to refine entity names after extraction.

speaker: Anna Thomas
title: LearnAI: LUIS – Notes from the Field
summary: The video discusses various entity types and their uses in post-processing. It explains the similarities and differences between hierarchical entities and roles, highlighting that the only distinction is the use of patterns. The video also mentions the benefits of pre-built entities, specifically the key phrase entity for extracting important information from conversations. Additionally, it introduces the person name and geography v2 entities. Lastly, it discusses the pattern dot any entity, which is useful for detecting entities with unclear beginnings and endings, such as book titles.

speaker: Anna Thomas
title: LearnAI: LUIS – Notes from the Field
summary: Improving entity detection is crucial for enhancing pattern detection and overall app performance. The Team Data Science Process (TDS) provides a framework for developing effective models. It involves three datasets: labeled data for training, a validation dataset for model selection, and a testing dataset for evaluating performance. Batch testing and active learning can be used to iteratively improve models. Dispatch is a tool that helps with routing and model performance analysis. Various resources and tutorials are available for creating enterprise-grade Louis models.

speaker: Neta Haiby
title: Extracting Data From Documents and Forms with OCR and Form Recognizer
summary: Neta Haiby, Principal Program Manager on the Microsoft Azure Cognitive Services Team, demonstrates how to extract data from documents and forms using OCR and form recognizer. OCR can extract text from documents and images, while form recognizer can extract structured text, key-value pairs, and tables from forms. This technology automates the process of data extraction, eliminating the need for manual processing. The demo showcases the extraction of data from a multi-page PDF using form recognizer's layout API.

speaker: Neta Haiby
title: Extracting Data From Documents and Forms with OCR and Form Recognizer
summary: In this demo, the video showcases how to use layout extraction to extract data from a document. The document used is a news release of unemployment insurance weekly claims with multiple pages containing text and tables. The layout API is called to analyze the document and extract the text and tables. The output is a JSON file that includes the extracted data, including information about row and column indices and whether a cell spans multiple rows or columns.

speaker: Neta Haiby
title: Extracting Data From Documents and Forms with OCR and Form Recognizer
summary: Form Recognizer is a tool that allows companies to train models to automatically extract data from various types of forms. It offers two options for training models: one without labels, which is useful for quickly training models for different form types, and one with labels, which requires human input to extract specific values. With just a handful of sample documents, companies can train models and continuously improve their accuracy over time. This video demonstrates how to train and analyze a document using Form Recognizer's custom service.

speaker: Neta Haiby
title: Extracting Data From Documents and Forms with OCR and Form Recognizer
summary: The sample labeling tool for form recognition is available as an open source and can be accessed through a tryout site or deployed locally on Azure Cloud. The tool allows users to label various form elements such as names, social security numbers, signatures, addresses, and more. Once labeled, the tool can train a model with an accuracy of up to 95%. The trained model can then be used to analyze and extract information from new documents.

speaker: Neta Haiby
title: Extracting Data From Documents and Forms with OCR and Form Recognizer
summary: Form Recognizer is a powerful tool that can extract text, tables, and key-value pairs from various types of documents. It offers the ability to train custom models tailored to specific forms, as well as prebuilt models for common document types like receipts. Customers and partners, such as Automation Anywhere, have successfully used Form Recognizer to automate processes and streamline operations, resulting in improved efficiency and faster data processing.

speaker: Ana Thomas, Holly
title: LearnAI-Bootcamp for Emerging AI Developers: Integrating Services with BotBuilder SDK v4 Part 2
summary: In this episode of the LearnAI-Bootcamp for Emerging AI Developers series, Ana Thomas and Holly from Microsoft's cloud and AI team discuss integrating multiple services into a bot using the BotBuilder SDK v4. They start by creating an Azure Search service and then integrate Azure Search, LUIS, and Regex into the bot. The video provides a demo and also directs viewers to the GitHub page for the lab materials.

speaker: Ana Thomas, Holly
title: LearnAI-Bootcamp for Emerging AI Developers: Integrating Services with BotBuilder SDK v4 Part 2
summary: The video provides a step-by-step guide on building a hello world bot using the v4 SDK. It covers topics such as configuring services, adding middleware, and optimizing bots using middleware. The video also demonstrates how to handle different topics and responses using the SDK's topic interface. The tutorial aims to help developers understand the new features and capabilities of the v4 SDK for building more advanced bots.

speaker: Ana Thomas, Holly
title: LearnAI-Bootcamp for Emerging AI Developers: Integrating Services with BotBuilder SDK v4 Part 2
summary: The video discusses the implementation of regex (regular expressions) in a new SDK for a chatbot. The use of regex allows for specific matching of user inputs, optimizing calls to the service. The video demonstrates how regex is used to handle different user intents, such as searching for pictures or requesting help. The next step in the lab is to address the error in the search topic by filling it out.

speaker: Ana Thomas, Holly
title: LearnAI-Bootcamp for Emerging AI Developers: Integrating Services with BotBuilder SDK v4 Part 2
summary: The video discusses the implementation of a search feature in a bot using the Microsoft Bot Framework SDK v4. It covers the use of regular expressions (regex) and the Language Understanding Intelligent Service (LUIS) to handle user input and guide the conversation. The video also mentions the option to add buttons for a more guided user experience and the process of publishing the bot. The code for the implementation is available on GitHub.

speaker: Rajesh
title: Powered by Azure Machine Learning service: Optimize Bing Ad campaigns
summary: Rajesh, a Senior Product Manager in Azure ML, discusses how Bing Ads uses AI to optimize ad campaigns. By applying machine learning techniques, Bing Ads helps advertisers maximize their digital marketing budget by recommending keywords and ad placements that are more likely to generate clicks and conversions. The system analyzes data from similar advertisers and provides personalized recommendations to improve ad performance.

speaker: Rajesh
title: Powered by Azure Machine Learning service: Optimize Bing Ad campaigns
summary: Advertisers can optimize their ads by strategically positioning them, running them on certain days, and adding new keywords. Azure Machine Learning Service helps advertisers by providing inferencing capabilities, allowing them to scale up and down on-demand, and easily deploy their models in a Kubernetes cluster. Model management in Azure Machine Learning Service enables versioning, performance monitoring, and quick debugging of models. This helps advertisers make informed decisions and quickly correct any issues that may arise.

speaker: Rajesh
title: Powered by Azure Machine Learning service: Optimize Bing Ad campaigns
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of deploying machine learning models using Azure Machine Learning Service. They explain that the deployment process is simple and requires just a few lines of code. Azure takes care of scaling the model and handling the infrastructure, allowing developers and data scientists to focus on business results. The speaker also mentions that there are resources available on the Azure website for further learning and encourages viewers to try it out and provide feedback.

speaker: Kelly
title: Vision Cognitive Services Updates
summary: Kelly from Cognitive Services discusses the new updates for Vision Cognitive Services in this video. The updates include improvements in computer vision, such as image tagging, captioning, and OCR, with a new version of OCR that is significantly better. They have also expanded the languages available for captioning. Kelly demonstrates the improved OCR capabilities, showcasing how the new model accurately captures text from images.

speaker: Kelly
title: Vision Cognitive Services Updates
summary: Custom Vision is a tool that allows users to build image classification models quickly and easily with minimal data. It now includes object detection, providing bounding boxes and identifying objects within an image. Users can upload images, tag them with bounding boxes, and train the model. The tool offers suggested bounding boxes and makes it easier to tag images, improving the accuracy of the model. The more images and tags provided, the better the model's performance.

speaker: Kelly
title: Vision Cognitive Services Updates
summary: The video discusses the topic of customization in computer vision and custom vision models. It recommends having at least 15 images for training, but the number may vary depending on the objects being detected. The video also mentions that one bounding box per image is recommended, but more can be used for better accuracy. The API returns bounding box coordinates and tags, and the mean average precision (MAP) score is used to evaluate object detection performance. The video also mentions new export capabilities for classification models, including support for ONNX, Windows ML, and Docker files. The object detection feature is not yet available for Edge devices.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Seth welcomes Mehrnoosh Sameki and Besmira Nushi to discuss the Responsible AI (RAI) integration effort. They introduce the RAI toolkit, which combines open-source tools for error analysis, interpretability, fairness, counterfactual analysis, and causal decision making. The toolkit aims to simplify the process of responsible development and assessment of machine learning models and data-driven decision making. The episode includes a demo showcasing model debugging and responsible decision-making.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video discusses a dashboard that integrates model debugging, fairness analysis, counterfactual analysis, and responsible decision-making for data exploration and model interpretability. It emphasizes the importance of taking responsible decisions based on mature tools like econ ml, rather than relying on spurious correlations. The dashboard allows users to identify model errors, analyze error rates for different cohorts, and make informed decisions to avoid financial loss and limitations in accessing finances.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video discusses the importance of diagnosing and understanding errors in data analysis models. It emphasizes the need to go beyond identifying errors and move towards diagnosing them in order to develop targeted mitigation strategies. The video showcases various capabilities of a dashboard, such as data exploration and model interpretability, that can help in understanding why errors occur and how to address them effectively.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video discusses the analysis of prediction probabilities for selling prices of old and new houses. It highlights that the model's accuracy is higher for newer houses compared to older ones. The need for more representation of expensive old houses in the training data is emphasized. The video also mentions the use of box plots to visualize the distribution of prediction probabilities. Additionally, it suggests exploring how the model makes its predictions and emphasizes the importance of collecting more data for a better balance.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video provides an explanation of how a model makes predictions for different data cohorts and highlights the importance of certain factors in the prediction process. It demonstrates how the model uses features such as overall finish quality and year built to make predictions. The video also discusses the importance of investigating fairness issues and spurious correlations in the model's predictions. Additionally, it showcases the ability to analyze individual data points and perform counterfactual analysis for diagnosis purposes.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video discusses the use of counterfactuals in analyzing and debugging machine learning models. Counterfactuals are used to identify the minimum changes needed to predict the opposite outcome for a specific data point. This tool is useful for detecting fairness issues and providing actionable insights for decision-making. The video also mentions the use of causal inferencing capabilities in the dashboard for business stakeholders to provide actionable insights to customers.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: Individual house owners can now access actionable insights on how to effectively change the price of their house in the market. By analyzing historic data and conducting causal analysis, owners can determine the impact of specific features, such as increasing the number of garages or improving the finish quality, on the housing price. This analysis is based on statistics and utilizes an open-source package called econ ml. The dashboard also provides ideal policies for house builders looking to optimize their properties.

speaker: Seth, Mehrnoosh Sameki, Besmira Nushi
title: AI Show: Live Responsible AI Dashboard: One-stop shop for operationalizing RAI in practice | 43
summary: The video discusses the use of a responsible AI dashboard, which helps in operationalizing responsible AI practices. The dashboard provides various features such as error analysis, interpretability, fairness assessment, and mitigation. It is open-source and modular, allowing users to customize and co-create components. The dashboard is part of a larger effort called the Responsible AI Toolbox, which aims to provide a comprehensive set of tools for responsible AI implementation. Viewers are encouraged to visit responsiblytoolbox.ai for more information.

speaker: Seth Juarez, Sonya captive
title: Overview of the Microsoft AI School
summary: Seth Juarez and Sonya Captive discuss the Microsoft AI School, a platform that provides developers and data scientists with resources to learn about the Microsoft AI platform and deep learning. The AI School offers a variety of content, including videos, tutorials, code samples, and documentation. Users can navigate through the platform by searching for specific topics or using filters. Feedback and suggestions can be sent to AskAISchool@microsoft.com.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, a core contributor for PyTorch, provides an introductory hands-on tutorial for building a fashion recognizer using PyTorch. He covers core functionality, network architecture, loss function and optimizer, and setting up TensorBoard. PyTorch is an open-source machine learning framework that accelerates the path from research to production deployment. The tutorial showcases the ease of use and interoperability of PyTorch with other libraries like NumPy.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: The video discusses the PyTorch library, which is a tensor library that interoperates with NumPy. It allows for accelerated operations on CPUs, GPUs, and other devices. PyTorch can be used as a drop-in replacement for the tensor library and has high compatibility with NumPy APIs. The video also demonstrates using PyTorch for deep learning tasks, specifically for image recognition using the FashionMNIST dataset. PyTorch provides libraries for data reading and preparation, as well as bindings to common datasets.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: To initialize a dataset, the AI assistant fetches data from the internet and applies transformations to prepare the images. The dataset is then loaded into a data loader, which converts the data into tensors and creates an iterator for easy access. Torchvision provides pre-built datasets, but users can also create their own datasets using Python classes. Transformers are used to modify the data during loading. The data loader, dataset, and transformer each have distinct roles in the data loading process.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the difference between a data set and a transformer in the context of machine learning. They explain that a data set is like a dictionary of semantics, while a data loader is a multi-threaded worker that samples items from the data set, shuffles them, and groups them into batches. They also touch on network architecture, specifically using fully connected linear layers for a simple multi-layer perceptron. The speaker clarifies that the init function stores the model parameters, while the forward function runs the functional operations, including activation functions.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: The video discusses the storage and usage of model parameters in deep learning models. It explains that parameters, such as activation functions and weights, are stored in the model's state. This allows for parameter sharing and easy movement of the model to different devices, such as GPUs. The video also demonstrates how to visualize and compute gradients for the parameters using autograd.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: The video demonstrates how to train a machine learning model using TensorFlow. It covers topics such as computing gradients, visualizing graphs with TensorBoard, and building a custom training loop. The presenter also mentions higher-level frameworks like PyTorch Lightning and Python Ignite that can simplify the training process. The video provides a step-by-step guide for training a model and evaluating its performance.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: The video demonstrates how to train a simple model using a multi-layer perceptron. The training loop involves calling the model, calculating the loss, and optimizing the model parameters using the optimizer. The optimizer.step() function subtracts the scaled gradients of the model parameters to update them. The test part does not require gradient calculations, so the no_grad() function is used. The video emphasizes the importance of clearing gradients and the use of explicit conventions in neural network training.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: Disabling the tracking of autograd during the backward pass can have a small performance benefit as it eliminates the need to remember which operations occurred during the forward pass. However, even without disabling it, the model would still work fine. Setting the model to eval mode instead of train mode is useful for modules like dropout or batch norm, but in this case, it is not necessary. Tensorboard is a great tool for visualizing training statistics and model graphs.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: The video discusses how to save and deploy Python models using PyTorch. The presenter demonstrates how to save the parameters of a model using a dictionary and explains that the source code of the model is still required for later use. They also introduce TorchScript, a part of PyTorch that allows for packaging both the model and source code into a self-contained package, making it possible to deploy the model without relying on Python. This is useful for deployment in environments without Python, such as mobile phones or embedded applications.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov
title: Intro to PyTorch Tutorial: Building fashion recognizer
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the benefits of using Python and PyTorch for deploying machine learning models. They highlight how the state dictionary in PyTorch allows for easy transfer learning and fine-tuning of models. The speaker also emphasizes the flexibility and power of PyTorch as a pluggable library within the Python ecosystem. They mention that PyTorch can be integrated with other libraries and domains, such as deployment and scientific computing. The video concludes by mentioning the ability to save and load models using the state dictionary, and the availability of tutorials and resources on python.org.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Luis from the Azure Cognitive Search team discusses how to add custom skills to a skillset in Azure Cognitive Search. He explains the process of enriching content in the ingestion pipeline and demonstrates how to create custom skills. Luis also introduces power skills as a way to leverage existing skills. Azure Cognitive Search is a Platform as a Service component that enables powerful search experiences in applications.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Azure Cognitive Search supports an extensible skill set, allowing users to add their own custom skills to the enrichment process. These custom skills can be created using custom code and can perform various tasks, such as connecting to a database or using custom models. The input-output interface for these custom skills is a simple HTTPS call, where data is passed as a property bag. As long as the input-output interface is followed, users can use any code or language for their custom skills.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video demonstrates how to create a custom skill using the Microsoft Power Skills repository. The repository provides pre-built skill templates that can be customized. The video shows an example of modifying the "Hello World" skill to create a new skill called "get-file-type". The skill takes an input parameter called "name" and outputs a greeting using the input. The process is shown using Visual Studio and Azure Functions.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video demonstrates how to create a custom skill in Azure Functions to determine the file type based on its extension. By using the filename input, the function checks for the extension and categorizes it as an image or a specific file type. This custom skill can be valuable for filtering search results or performing specific actions based on file types. The video also shows how to test the function using Postman.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video demonstrates how to connect an Azure Function to the rest of a pipeline for consuming data. The Azure Function is a custom skill that takes input from an indexer and returns output that the indexer can read. The video shows how to modify the index to include an extra field, and how to modify the skill set to include the custom skill. The custom skill is then connected to the rest of the pipeline for further processing.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: The video discusses how to add custom skills to an array of built-in skills. It explains that a template is available for each skill, allowing users to easily copy and paste the necessary elements. The video also emphasizes the importance of understanding the context of a custom skill, as it determines the level at which information is enriched. The source of the file name is obtained from the metadata storage name during the document-cracking stage.

speaker: Luis, Seth
title: AI Show Custom Skills In Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this video, the speaker explains how to use custom skills in Azure Cognitive Search. They demonstrate how to extract file types from documents using an Azure Function and map the extracted data to the index. The speaker also discusses the ability to use complex structures in the index and highlights the power of custom skills in enhancing search capabilities.

speaker: Shenee Winon
title: New Azure Machine Learning Basic and Enterprise Editions
summary: Shenee Winon, a program manager on the Azure Machine Learning platform team, introduces the new Azure Machine Learning Basic and Enterprise Editions. The Basic edition is designed for open source developers and data scientists who prefer a code-first experience, while the Enterprise edition offers no-code machine learning tools for all skill levels and is tailored for enterprises. The Enterprise edition includes enhanced security, collaboration, manageability, and governance features, as well as new UI capabilities and improved MLOps capabilities.

speaker: Shenee Winon
title: New Azure Machine Learning Basic and Enterprise Editions
summary: Azure Machine Learning has introduced a new studio experience with automated machine learning and designer tools. The automated machine learning feature allows users to select different types of models for training, compare models, and perform model interoperability and explainability. The designer tool enables users to create and visualize machine learning pipelines, including data preparation, model training, and deployments. Users can access these new capabilities by upgrading to the enterprise workspace in Azure Machine Learning. There are differences in costs between the basic and enterprise skews, with a surcharge on compute targets for the enterprise skew. More information can be found in the technical documentation and the Azure Machine Learning studio.

speaker: Lauren Tran, Alexandra
title: Approaches for Sequence Classification on Financial Time Series Data
summary: Lauren Tran, a machine learning engineer at Microsoft, discusses sequence classification on financial time series data at the Women in Machine Learning and Data Science meetup. She explores the use of LSTM, CNN, and SVM algorithms for sequence labeling tasks and demonstrates their application in detecting signs of financial distress and predicting insolvency using financial transaction data. This talk provides insights into commercial software engineering and the importance of proactive intervention in financial default prediction.

speaker: Lauren Tran, Alexandra
title: Approaches for Sequence Classification on Financial Time Series Data
summary: The video discusses the development of a binary classifier to predict whether members will default on their financial transactions. The approach involved using traditional machine learning methods such as support vector machines, as well as deep learning methods like LSTM and CNN. The data used included transaction history and spending categories. Feature engineering was done to incorporate the notion of time by aggregating transaction activity on a monthly, weekly, and daily basis.

speaker: Lauren Tran, Alexandra
title: Approaches for Sequence Classification on Financial Time Series Data
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of using traditional machine learning, specifically support vector machines (SVM), to educate and help partners, startups, and customers understand the machine learning process. They demonstrate the use of a tool called Machine Learning Studio to prototype and evaluate the data, ensuring that the engineered features are effective. The speaker emphasizes the importance of understanding the process before transitioning to coding with libraries like scikit-learn.

speaker: Lauren Tran, Alexandra
title: Approaches for Sequence Classification on Financial Time Series Data
summary: The video discusses the implementation of machine learning algorithms using scikit-learn and deep learning approaches using LSTM networks. It explains how to transform data into a 3D matrix representation for LSTM input. The video also provides code examples using Azure Machine Learning Workbench for building LSTM layers and dense layers for classification.

speaker: Lauren Tran, Alexandra
title: Approaches for Sequence Classification on Financial Time Series Data
summary: The video discusses the use of dense layers and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for classification tasks. Dense layers are fully connected parts of neural networks that use sigmoid activation for binary classification. CNNs, typically used for image tasks, are also effective for sequence labeling due to their spatial reasoning capabilities. The video demonstrates the implementation of CNNs using 1D filters for non-image data. Additionally, the video explores the use of individual transactions for pattern detection and classification, achieving 75% validation accuracy.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: Phani Mutyala, Senior Program Manager on the Azure Cognitive Services team, discusses Cognitive Services containers and how they can be used at the Edge. The session covers the flexibility and availability of the APIs, the four product families of Cognitive Services (Vision, Speech, Language, and Decision), and the ability for customers to deploy Cognitive Services in their own terms, either on the Cloud or at the Edge.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: Customers who are unable to upload all their data to the cloud due to security and privacy concerns, low bandwidth, or intermittent connection can benefit from Cognitive Services running at the Edge. By providing APIs in the form of Docker containers, customers have full control over their data and can meet regulatory requirements. Use cases include robotic process automation, intelligent customer support, document understanding, sentiment analysis, and face detection. Containers are an extended feature of existing Cognitive Services, offering flexibility for customers.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: A strategic Microsoft partner, Wilson Allen, is using Docker containers to bring form-based data into the firm data ecosystem and create metadata from text-based data. They use the Form Recognizer container to extract historic HR PDF forms and ingest the output resource into a database for master data and analytics purposes. Insight, a global payments technology company, uses Azure IoT Edge and Azure Cognitive Services to provide a self-service kiosk with face recognition, speech-to-text, and language understanding capabilities. This solution integrates with customers' digital issuance technology, reducing wait times and improving customer satisfaction. TIBCO, a data science team member, uses the TIBCO Connected Intelligence platform to unlock the potential of real-time data for faster and smarter decision-making.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: The video discusses TIBCO's Predict pillar, which focuses on anomaly detection in various industries such as manufacturing, energy, finance, and healthcare. TIBCO utilizes Microsoft services, including Azure Anomaly Detection and Cognitive Services, along with their own platforms, TIBCO Data Science and Spotfire, to analyze data, identify root causes, and generate recommended actions. The solution is developed in two phases, with a central data science team using TIBCO Data Science to detect anomalies on historical data from multiple sites.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: The TIBCO Data Science platform is used to detect anomalies in historical data from multiple sites. The visual-backed data science workflow creates infrastructure for maintenance engineers to use at remote sites. Containerized services, known as Python Data functions in TIBCO Spotfire, are used to detect anomalies and perform root cause analysis. Key drivers are identified and further processing is done to determine recommended actions. The TIBCO analytics stack, along with containerized services from Microsoft, is used for this analysis.

speaker: Phani Mutyala
title: Bringing AI to the Edge
summary: In this video, we learn about the second phase of the maintenance process, where the engineer performs anomaly detection at the Edge. The engineer uses the equipment maintenance dashboard to detect anomalies in production per minute. The anomalies are displayed as red markers on the dashboard. The engineer can then select a specific time window and perform root cause analysis to identify the key driving factors for the anomalies. The engineer can also use the Key Phrase Extraction Container to generate key phrases and make maintenance recommendations based on the data.

speaker: Rob, Ivor Berry
title: Microsoft Learn | Developing solutions with Azure OpenAI
summary: Rob Ivor Berry discusses the Microsoft Learn learning path on developing solutions with Azure OpenAI. The learning path explores how to create your own Azure OpenAI deployment, use it in apps, and utilize more advanced features in development. The module focuses on grounding your Azure Open AI Service in your own data, allowing you to upload company data and use Azure Open AI to provide answers.

speaker: Rob, Ivor Berry
title: Microsoft Learn | Developing solutions with Azure OpenAI
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to add your own data to an AI model using Azure Open AI. They use the example of a travel agency called Margie's Travel, which has pamphlets about different cities and hotels. By connecting their data to an Azure search resource, they are able to provide personalized responses to questions about where to stay and information about the cities. The video also mentions that users can access the Azure AI Studio for further interaction with AI models.

speaker: Marco Ribeiro
title: The Science Behind InterpretML: LIME
summary: Marco Ribeiro, Senior Researcher at Microsoft Research, discusses the importance of interpretability in machine learning models. He shares his experience of discovering that his model had learned a shortcut instead of picking up on the intended patterns, highlighting the limitations of cross-validation accuracy. Ribeiro introduces LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations), a research paper he wrote during his PhD, as a solution to understanding how models make predictions.

speaker: Marco Ribeiro
title: The Science Behind InterpretML: LIME
summary: Interpretability in machine learning is crucial for understanding how models make predictions and improving their performance. By understanding the inner workings of a model, one can identify and rectify issues such as overfitting and spurious correlations. Interpretability also enables non-experts to make informed decisions about model selection and feature engineering. LIME, a technique discussed in the video, focuses on explaining specific aspects of a model's behavior rather than attempting to explain everything at once. Overall, interpretability is a valuable tool for developers and users of machine learning models.

speaker: Marco Ribeiro
title: The Science Behind InterpretML: LIME
summary: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) is a tool that aims to explain the predictions made by complex machine learning models. It treats the model as a black box and perturbs the example to understand how the model behaves. By changing different features and observing the changes in the prediction, LIME learns a simple explanation that describes the model's behavior in a specific region or neighborhood. LIME is a useful tool for interpretability in machine learning.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Global AI Bootcamp Keynote
summary: Eric Boyd, Corporate Vice President of Azure AI, delivers the keynote speech at the Global AI Bootcamp. He discusses Azure AI's strategy and focus for the future, emphasizing the ease of building ML models for users of all skill levels. Boyd also highlights the heavy investments made based on customer demand. The event, hosted in over 120 locations worldwide, aims to inspire attendees with the latest AI technologies, tools, and trends.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Global AI Bootcamp Keynote
summary: Azure offers a comprehensive range of AI solutions, from Azure machine learning to cognitive services, catering to all skill levels and business needs. For beginners, there are simplified options like automated machine learning and a drag-and-drop designer. Advanced users can utilize code-first experiences with integrated notebooks. Azure also focuses on enterprise-level management with ml Ops, making it easier to deploy and manage multiple models. Additionally, Azure supports enhancing existing applications with AI through its suite of cognitive services, including personalized recommendations and custom speech models.

speaker: Eric Boyd
title: Global AI Bootcamp Keynote
summary: Microsoft has announced new features for its AI services. Users can now build custom speech models based on their organization's Office 365 data, allowing for more accurate speech-to-text translations. Additionally, Microsoft has introduced custom neural voice, which enables users to create synthesized voices based on their company's mascot. The company has also released Bot Composer, a low-code tool for creating bots, and is focusing on knowledge mining to help customers extract insights from their data using AI. Microsoft is excited about the growth of the global AI community and has announced the upcoming Global AI Tour, a series of events taking place from March to May 2020.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Machine Learning Models
summary: In this episode of the AI show, Seth Juarez explains machine learning models and how they work. He starts by comparing the traditional programming approach to solving problems with the machine learning approach. Instead of writing a function, machine learning involves giving the computer input and answers, and it learns to create a function. Juarez explains that a machine learning model is essentially a function written in a different way, and he demonstrates this concept using a simple classification problem.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Machine Learning Models
summary: In machine learning, converting input data into numbers is crucial for classification tasks. This can be done using techniques like bag-of-words models for text or fast Fourier transforms for sound. Once the data is converted, a function or model needs to be defined for the machine learning algorithm to learn from. Frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn provide options for selecting the function shape. The model is then optimized using a cost/loss function and an optimizer. Finally, the trained model can be used to make predictions.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Machine Learning Models
summary: To train a machine learning model using TensorFlow, you need to define the model function, cost and loss function, and an optimizer. The model function represents the desired output based on the input data. The cost and loss function measures how well the model performs compared to the actual output. The optimizer minimizes the loss function to improve the model. Once trained, the model can be used to make predictions. TensorFlow provides various options for optimizers and loss functions, allowing flexibility in model design.

speaker: Seth Juarez
title: Machine Learning Models
summary: In this video, the presenter discusses loss functions, function shapes, and optimizers in the context of data science. They explain that choosing the right function shape, loss function, and optimizer is crucial for model accuracy. The presenter demonstrates a model implementation using a Convolutional Neural Network and shows how to optimize the model using the fit function. They emphasize the iterative nature of the data science process and the importance of analyzing results to improve model performance.

speaker: Neha Rajput
title: Introducing QnA Maker managed: Now in public preview
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Neha Rajput, Program Manager at QnA Maker, introduces QnA Maker Managed, which is now in public preview. QnA Maker is a tool that creates a bot to answer frequently asked questions. The new features of QnA Maker Managed include simplified resource management, end-to-end region support, and the ability to add personality to the bot. The service supports multiple languages and is easy to scale.

speaker: Neha Rajput
title: Introducing QnA Maker managed: Now in public preview
summary: The QnA Maker service is undergoing several updates. Firstly, there will be support for deep learning ranking models, which will improve the relevance of query results across all languages. Additionally, a new feature called MRC (Machine Reading Comprehension) based on suspended action will allow for precise answers to be returned instead of entire passages. The service will also be consolidated into two services, QnA Maker and Azure Search, making it easier for customers to access the latest models and scale up or down as needed.

speaker: Neha Rajput
title: Introducing QnA Maker managed: Now in public preview
summary: The video demonstrates how to create and manage resources in QnA Maker. It highlights the option to select the Azure search location and the creation of various resources. The video also showcases features such as customer-managed keys for encryption, private endpoint support, and the ability to create multilingual knowledge bases. The presenter uses a public URL to upload data for the demonstration.

speaker: Neha Rajput
title: Introducing QnA Maker managed: Now in public preview
summary: QnA Maker, a knowledge base management and authoring service, allows users to create and modify question and answer pairs with various formatting options. It also features MRC-based answer span detection for short and precise answers. The service improves relevance across languages and provides endpoints for deployment. QnA Maker simplifies the process of creating bots and saves time by automatically generating links and tags. More information can be found in the upcoming public blog and documentation.

title: Understanding Text using Cognitive Services
summary: In this video, viewers will learn how to analyze text using Cognitive Services. The video covers topics such as signing up for a cognitive service, and the capabilities of Text Analytics, Entity Linking, and Bing Entity Search. The speaker explains that cognitive services are a variety of services that use machine learning, and developers can easily consume these services by calling the API. The video focuses on services related to language and demonstrates how to create a subscription for the Text Analytics API.

title: Understanding Text using Cognitive Services
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to get started with Microsoft's cognitive services. They show how to navigate to the services and provide a developer key to access them. The presenter then showcases the capabilities of the Text Analytics service, such as sentiment analysis and language identification. They also discuss the importance of using these services to understand customer feedback and prioritize support tickets. Finally, they mention the possibility of combining different services for more advanced applications.

title: Understanding Text using Cognitive Services
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses text analytics and entity linking, two components of an application that analyzes text. Text analytics identifies key phrases in a piece of text, while entity linking identifies specific entities mentioned in the text. The speaker demonstrates how these components work using examples. The video also mentions the use of entity search to find additional metadata about identified entities. The goal is to automate the process of analyzing text and extracting relevant information. Viewers are directed to Microsoft's cognitive services website for more information.

speaker: Mahesh, Maya
title: Build a Customized Site Search Instance using Bing Custom Search API
summary: Mahesh from the Bing API team explains how to build a customized site search instance using Bing Custom Search API. This ad-free search tool allows users to create a search experience on their own site or across selected websites. Users can control ranking specifics and customize responses. Mahesh demonstrates how easy it is to set up a site search experience using the admin portal. Bing Custom Search API offers 1,000 free queries for developers to try it out.

speaker: Mahesh, Maya
title: Build a Customized Site Search Instance using Bing Custom Search API
summary: To enable a site search experience for users, you can use a custom search instance. This allows you to surface results from specific sites and block certain results if desired. You can add up to 400 sites to your custom search instance and use bulk upload functionality for convenience. Additionally, you can use pinning to prioritize certain sites and ensure relevant results are shown at the top. Blocking and pinning are useful features for customizing search results for your users.

speaker: Mahesh, Maya
title: Build a Customized Site Search Instance using Bing Custom Search API
summary: Pinning is a useful feature in custom search API that allows users to customize search results by prioritizing certain products or information. Users can also customize the layout and appearance of the search results using the hosted UI option. The API provides a JSON response that can be used to create a custom presentation layer. Both startups and enterprise-level companies can benefit from this versatile product.

speaker: Mahesh, Maya
title: Build a Customized Site Search Instance using Bing Custom Search API
summary: The video demonstrates how to set up a customized site search experience using Bing Custom Search. Users can choose the number of results per page, add a logo, and customize the toolbar theme. The search experience can be embedded using a JavaScript snippet or HTML endpoint. Bing Custom Search is an ad-free product, allowing users to customize their search results. The service is currently free to sign up, with a charge of $4 per thousand transactions. Additional functionalities will be launched in the coming months.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: Moon King, a program manager at Microsoft, discusses intelligent recommendations and how to build a proof of concept in one day. He explains that intelligent recommendations use AI and machine learning to improve discovery by finding the right content or products for users based on their interests and tastes. This can drive engagement, conversion, revenue, and CTR for businesses. Moon King also highlights various scenarios where recommendations can be applied, beyond just streaming platforms like Netflix.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: The video discusses the use of machine learning in driving personalized recommendations and connections in various scenarios. The focus is on democratizing AI/ML by providing a turnkey solution that can be easily integrated into existing systems. The system utilizes behavioral information, such as customer purchases, to generate recommendations. It also adapts to different types of behavior, allowing for personalized suggestions based on user history. The service is available on Azure and has shown significant impacts on revenue and click-through rates.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: Intelligent recommendation systems can personalize user experiences based on historical information and session-based interactions. This is particularly useful for engaging anonymous visitors in online retail scenarios. Usage information can also be used to suggest complementary items or actions based on what others have done. These recommendations can be applied to various types of items, such as documents, support tickets, videos, and more. Setting up such a system is made simple and accessible for users. Additionally, visual cognition can be used to suggest similar looks or descriptions without relying on collaborative filtering.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: The video showcases the power of visual search technology in finding similar products based on images rather than relying on keywords. The AI system uses advanced NLP technology to analyze product descriptions and find close matches, making it useful for various industries such as fashion, furniture, and food. The system can reason over intrinsic nouns and semantics to provide accurate recommendations. The video also demonstrates how the technology successfully recommends similar products based on a customer's description, even when specific keywords are not mentioned.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: The video demonstrates a feature called "try with your own data" that allows users to upload their own files and quickly see results. The video also mentions a quick start guide that provides information on the required data format. By following the provided format and including at least interactions and an image, users can obtain immediate results. The video showcases an example of analyzing popular brussels sprouts.

speaker: Moon King
title: Intelligent Recommendations
summary: Moon King discusses the benefits of using intelligent recommendations to enhance the user experience on websites. By implementing this feature, businesses have seen significant increases in engagement and revenue. Microsoft documents is one example of a company that has experienced a 600% growth in interaction month over month. Intelligent recommendations make it easier for users to find products they didn't even know they were looking for, improving the overall shopping experience. To learn more, visit intelligent-recommendations.microsoft.com.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: In this episode of The AI Show, Serge Retkowsky from Microsoft France demonstrates how audio processing can be used to extract audio signal information into spectrograms, which are images representing the spectrum of frequencies over time. He shows how these spectrograms can be used to build a custom vision model with Azure Automated ML for audio classification. By converting audio into images, computer vision techniques can be applied to audio analysis.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: The video explains the concept of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), which is a method to convert a signal from the time domain to the frequency domain. By analyzing the frequency components of a sound wave, we can visualize and understand its characteristics. The spectrogram, a graphical representation of the spectrum of frequencies over time, allows us to identify anomalies or issues in equipment by analyzing the sound samples and saving them as spectrograms.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: In this video, the concept of using spectrograms to classify audio files is explored. By converting audio signals into images, computer vision techniques can be applied to predict anomalies in machinery or classify music genres. The video also discusses the process of converting audio to spectrograms and provides a Python code example for building a classification model.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: The video explains the process of using Fourier transformation to switch from time to frequency domain, and how it can be used to analyze audio signals. It introduces the concept of a spectrogram, which combines frequencies and time in one graph to describe a song. The video also highlights the limitations of human hearing and the need for different scales to accurately differentiate between frequencies.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: The video discusses the concept of spectrograms and how they can be used to visualize audio data. The speaker explains the difference between linear and logarithmic scales and demonstrates how to generate spectrograms using a Python function. They also mention the possibility of using AutoML for image classification using the spectrogram images.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: The video showcases the process of building and training a model using Azure Machine Learning. The presenter demonstrates how to create a GPU compute cluster, load and automate images, and deploy the model on Azure Kubernetes Services. They then test the model using an open-source classical song from YouTube. The video highlights the ease and efficiency of using Azure Machine Learning for model development and deployment.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: The video demonstrates how a model can predict the genre of a song by analyzing its audio waveform. The model accurately identifies classical, blues, jazz, and even metal songs with high confidence levels. The process involves converting audio to visual representations and using machine learning algorithms for prediction. The results show the versatility of the model in classifying different genres. The video also mentions that the code and notebook used in the demonstration will be shared for further exploration.

speaker: Serge Retkowsky
title: The AI Show: Ep 55 | Audio analytics with Azure Automated ML
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the use of sound for predictive maintenance and anomaly detection. They demonstrate how to transform sound into images using spectrograms and build a classification model. They showcase an example with a washing machine, detecting a sound anomaly and sending a notification. The speaker emphasizes the potential of sound analytics for various applications, such as predictive maintenance and smarter cities. The video also provides links to related resources and mentions that all the materials will be available for replay.

speaker: Qun Ying
title: Inside Anomaly Detector
summary: Qun Ying, Senior Program Manager on the Microsoft Azure Cognitive Services Team, demonstrates how to use the Anomaly Detector API with simple REST API calls. Anomaly Detector is an AI-powered service that can detect anomalies in time series data. It requires no knowledge of AI and only involves calling the APIs with an array of data points. The APIs will respond with which data points are anomalous and which ones are change points. No training or model selection is needed.

speaker: Qun Ying
title: Inside Anomaly Detector
summary: The video demonstrates anomaly detection for streaming data and change point detection using code examples.
