The code includes functions for posting data to an API endpoint, loading JSON data, and drawing charts based on the API results. Different sensitivity levels are shown to detect anomalies, and a second Jupyter Notebook showcases point anomaly detection using a sliding window approach. The video emphasizes the importance of replacing the API key and endpoint in the code before running it.

speaker: Qun Ying
title: Inside Anomaly Detector
summary: The video demonstrates the usage of the Anomaly Detector API for monitoring streaming data and detecting anomalies. It showcases a demo web app and Jupyter Notebooks for sliding window and change point detection examples. The video also briefly mentions the usage of the Anomaly Detector API with Docker containers. The speaker emphasizes the importance of detecting anomalies and encourages viewers to try out the Anomaly Detector API.

speaker: AI Show
title: Setting Up Azure ML Services and Data Wrangling Using Azure ML Services [Part 2/4]
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, the speaker discusses setting up Azure ML Services and data wrangling using Azure ML Services. The Azure Machine Learning Services provide an integrated, end-to-end data science experience, allowing data scientists to prepare data, develop experiments, and deploy models at cloud scale. The speaker explains how to set up an Experimentation account, a Model Management account, and AML Workbench, and highlights the features of Azure ML Workbench that can speed up data wrangling.

speaker: AI Show
title: Setting Up Azure ML Services and Data Wrangling Using Azure ML Services [Part 2/4]
summary: The video demonstrates how to use a data preparation tool in Azure to clean and analyze data. It shows how to load data from Azure Blob storage, select a sample dataset, identify missing or erroneous data, analyze data patterns and distributions, and perform transformations without writing code. The tool helps data scientists save time and streamline the data cleaning process.

speaker: AI Show
title: Setting Up Azure ML Services and Data Wrangling Using Azure ML Services [Part 2/4]
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of data preparation using a Data Preparation Package. They explain that the package allows for transformations and cleaning of large datasets, and demonstrate how to perform transformations on a specific column, such as binning age values. The speaker also mentions the option to use Jupyter notebooks for data analysis and reporting. The video concludes by mentioning that the next episode will cover training and operationalizing models.

speaker: Kenji Kanazawa
title: Get started with Reinforcement Learning on Azure Machine Learning
summary: Kenji Kanazawa, a Principal Program Manager in Azure Machine Learning, discusses reinforcement learning in this episode of The AI Show. Reinforcement learning is a type of AI that involves a system interacting with the world, making decisions, and observing the results. Unlike computer vision, which is a one-step process, reinforcement learning takes multiple steps and continuously interacts with the world. Kanazawa explains how reinforcement learning algorithms, such as PPO (proximal policy optimization), work to optimize decision-making. He also demonstrates how to use reinforcement learning on Azure Machine Learning.

speaker: Kenji Kanazawa
title: Get started with Reinforcement Learning on Azure Machine Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning is a machine learning technique where an agent learns to make decisions by interacting with its environment. In this video, the speaker explains the concept of reinforcement learning and demonstrates how Azure Machine Learning can be used to train a reinforcement learning agent. The speaker also introduces the reinforcement learning estimator, a specific tool in Azure Machine Learning that is designed for reinforcement learning tasks.

speaker: Kenji Kanazawa
title: Get started with Reinforcement Learning on Azure Machine Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning is a key aspect of machine learning that requires optimization and distributed computing. Azure Machine Learning Estimator simplifies this process by automatically packaging and distributing code to multiple machines for effective training. It also manages compute resources, spinning them up when needed and shutting them down when training is complete. This technology is being used in various domains, including gaming and enterprise applications such as manufacturing and logistics optimization.

speaker: Mike Tholfsen
title: Inside Immersive Reader
summary: Mike Tholfsen, Microsoft Education Program Manager, discusses how Immersive Reader can be used to embed text reading and comprehension capabilities into applications. Originally designed to assist people with dyslexia, Immersive Reader has proven to be helpful for a wide range of users, including those with ADHD, non-native speakers, and individuals with visual impairments. Integrating Immersive Reader can benefit partners by promoting equity and inclusion, reaching non-native speakers, and providing access to top assistive and accessible technology.

speaker: Mike Tholfsen
title: Inside Immersive Reader
summary: The Immersive Reader is a powerful tool that can be integrated into various platforms, such as learning management systems like Canvas. It offers features like focus mode, high-grade neural text-to-speech, customizable text preferences, grammar options, reading preferences, and the ability to click on words to see pictures. These capabilities make reading more accessible and beneficial for individuals with different needs, such as those with vision impairments, dyslexia, or language difficulties.

speaker: Mike Tholfsen
title: Inside Immersive Reader
summary: Microsoft's Immersive Reader, a tool that helps improve reading comprehension, is now available in over 80 partner apps. The tool allows users to click on words to see pictures and offers translation in over 67 languages. Immersive Reader has won several awards and is based on research and science. It will be part of Microsoft's Cognitive Services and will have a usage-based pricing model. The tool is easy to integrate and is currently free until general availability in the summer.

speaker: Sethu Raman
title: Build Recap | Managed online endpoints GA
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Sethu Raman discusses the general availability of Managed Online Endpoints announced at Microsoft Build 2022. Managed Online Endpoints provide a turnkey solution for deploying ML models at scale in production without worrying about underlying infrastructure. Sethu demonstrates how users can scale to 100,000 queries per second using GitHub-friendly APIs. This feature is beneficial for large customers concerned about scale.

speaker: Sethu Raman
title: Build Recap | Managed online endpoints GA
summary: The video demonstrates how to scale up a cluster to achieve high throughput and QPS (queries per second) using F-series machines and instances. By increasing the number of nodes and adjusting the worker count, the test achieves a QPS of 100,000. However, this comes with a trade-off of increased tail latencies. Overall, high-skilled customers can now easily self-serve and achieve high QPS.

speaker: Sethu Raman
title: Build Recap | Managed online endpoints GA
summary: Customers can now self-serve their way to hundreds of thousands of queries per second (qps) in under seven minutes. Tail latencies, such as p90 or p99, are important to measure user experience. Increasing worker and node counts can cause issues due to increased context switching and additional latency. Microsoft Build has announced two new features for management endpoints based on customer feedback.

speaker: Sethu Raman
title: Build Recap | Managed online endpoints GA
summary: Microsoft is introducing two new features for managed online endpoints. The first feature is mirror traffic, which allows users to divert a percentage of live traffic to a new model for testing without affecting the overall response to clients. The second feature is network isolation support, which simplifies the setup process by securing both ingress and egress communication through private endpoints. Users can find more information and tutorials on these features through the provided link.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: Ailsa Leen, a design program manager on the Azure AI team, discusses the use of AI for accessibility and inclusive design. She emphasizes the importance of ensuring equal access to technology for people with disabilities and highlights the role of accessible design in improving experiences for everyone. Leen also shares common use cases of Azure AI for accessibility and emphasizes the need for inclusive innovation.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: The video discusses the concept of accessibility as a spectrum that applies to everyone, not just individuals with disabilities. It highlights the different types of disabilities, including permanent, temporary, and situational, and emphasizes the importance of making software and websites accessible to all. The video also mentions that there are hidden disabilities that may not be immediately apparent. Overall, accessibility is presented as a universal need that benefits everyone.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: The video discusses the importance of accessibility for individuals with disabilities, including visible and invisible disabilities. It highlights the need for inclusive design in everyday objects, such as curb cuts, which benefit not only wheelchair users but also individuals with strollers or carts. The video then transitions to discussing the relevance of accessibility in software and AI. It explains how AI tools, such as vision recognition and speech-to-text capabilities, can address mismatches between individuals and the systems they use, making software more accessible for everyone.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: AI-driven accessibility technologies are revolutionizing the way people interact with software. For example, speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities allow users to input information more easily. Additionally, AI can enhance efficiency by assisting users in typing or predicting text, as seen with Stephen Hawking's use of predictive text AI. These technologies not only address mismatches between humans and computers but also benefit developers and users alike. Numerous companies, including Microsoft, utilize AI for accessibility purposes, such as live captions for the deaf and hard of hearing.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: Captions are not only important for the deaf and hard of hearing, but also helpful for neurodiverse individuals and those without headphones. Content reading, such as read aloud features, can assist with comprehension and accessibility for people with vision disabilities. Other accessibility tools include translation, voice control, and describing images. These tools are becoming increasingly advanced and can greatly enhance accessibility for all individuals.

speaker: Ailsa Leen, L Celine
title: Using AI to Make Experiences Accessible and Inclusive
summary: In this video, Elsa discusses the importance of accessibility and inclusion in technology, specifically focusing on the use of AI. She demonstrates how AI can be used to provide captions and translations in PowerPoint presentations, and emphasizes the need to consult and involve the communities that will be affected by these solutions. Elsa also mentions the Speech Accessibility Project and encourages viewers to check out the Ability Summit, a virtual event focused on disability inclusion and technology.

title: Experimentation Using Notebooks in Azure ML with Remote Compute [Part 3/4]
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, the focus is on using Notebooks in Azure ML with remote GPU compute. The video provides an overview of Azure ML Services and how it enables data scientists to prepare data, develop experiments, and deploy models at cloud scale. The video also demonstrates how to train a machine learning model using Pandas and Scikit-Learn, and how to attach a remote machine to the Notebook server.

title: Experimentation Using Notebooks in Azure ML with Remote Compute [Part 3/4]
summary: The video discusses how to set up and use the Azure Machine Learning Workbench. It explains that the Workbench is based on Docker and allows users to create and manage Docker containers for running machine learning experiments. The video also demonstrates how to configure the Workbench to include custom libraries and how to start a Notebook Server to run experiments on a remote machine. It concludes by mentioning that the Workbench supports different kernels and can be used with other computing resources like HDInsight Spark.

title: Experimentation Using Notebooks in Azure ML with Remote Compute [Part 3/4]
summary: The video provides a demonstration of how to set up and use the Azure Machine Learning service. It covers initializing the azureml_logger, importing libraries and data, visualizing and transforming the data, mapping strings to numbers, handling null values, creating features, and visualizing the data again. The video emphasizes the ability to log and track changes made during experimentation and highlights the convenience of using the Azure Machine Learning service.

title: Experimentation Using Notebooks in Azure ML with Remote Compute [Part 3/4]
summary: The video discusses the process of building and optimizing machine learning models using logistic regression and random forest classifier. The presenter demonstrates how to import libraries, train the models, and evaluate their accuracy. The video also highlights the use of Azure ML Logger to track experiment runs and compare different models. The next video will cover packaging and deploying the model for use.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: In this episode of the AI show, Chris Laurie demonstrates how to deploy machine learning models using Visual Studio Code Tools for AI extension and Azure Machine Learning service. He explains the process of taking the output of a machine learning program and making it useful by deploying it as a REST API in the cloud using microservices and Docker containers. Chris also shows how to create a cluster and deploy the model with just a few clicks.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: The video demonstrates how to deploy a machine learning model to the cloud using Azure. The process involves registering the model, adding tags and descriptions, and creating versions. Once the model is registered, it can be deployed using a Docker container. The video also mentions the option of using Azure Kubernetes cluster for production environments, but focuses on spinning up an Azure container instance for testing purposes.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to spin up an Azure Container Instance, which is a lightweight option for testing. They explain that creating an Azure Kubernetes Cluster is also easy, and show how to deploy a service from a registered model. They discuss the importance of having a scoring file and explain how to specify the environment using a Conda file. Optional steps such as providing a Docker file and schema are also mentioned.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: The video explains how to create an image and a service using Azure Machine Learning. The scoring file is shown, which uses TensorFlow to load and run the model. The YAML file is also discussed, which specifies the dependencies and configurations for the project. The video mentions the use of containers, Docker files, and Azure Container Instances, which are created in the Azure Machine Learning workspace. The service deployment process is explained, including the generation of a Docker image.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: The video demonstrates how to deploy a Docker image to Azure Container Instances using Azure Machine Learning. It explains that this method allows for quick deployment without fine-grained control, but if more control is desired, a compute target like Kubernetes can be used. The video also shows how the Docker image is uploaded to Azure Container Registry and discusses the potential use of Azure DevOps pipelines. The deployment process typically takes around 5 to 8 minutes.

speaker: Chris Laurie, Seth
title: Learn How to Deploy Machine Learning Models!
summary: In this video, the host demonstrates how to deploy a machine learning model into a production environment using Azure. They show how to create a Docker image, deploy it to an Azure Container Instance, and access the scoring URI for making predictions. They also discuss the option of deploying the model to a Kubernetes cluster. Overall, the video provides a step-by-step guide for taking machine learning models to the last mile of deployment.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: Micheleen Harris, a software engineer at Microsoft, provides an introduction to deep learning and computer vision. She covers concepts such as CNNs, deep learning, and transfer learning, explaining commonly used terms and popular approaches to solving computer vision challenges. Harris also discusses the differences between traditional supervised machine learning and deep learning, highlighting the role of domain experts and the extraction of important features.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: In this video, the concept of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in deep learning for computer vision is explained. CNNs use different layers to extract and classify features in images, without human involvement. The first layers focus on low-level features like edges and colors, while subsequent layers identify higher-level features like shapes and objects. The final layers bring all the information together to solve complex problems. The video also showcases an example of a deep neural network for computer vision.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are used to analyze complex objects in images, such as people, animals, and beaches. Transfer learning is a concept where a pre-trained CNN is used as a starting point for solving a different problem, like identifying deer instead of dogs. This approach allows models to achieve accurate results with fewer labeled images. Custom Vision AI is an example of a service built on transfer learning.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: The video discusses the concept of retraining neural networks for specific problem spaces. It explains that base models trained on specific datasets can offer better results for similar problems. The video also mentions ImageNet, a large collection of labeled images used for image classification. It highlights the yearly competition called the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge, where universities and companies compete to improve performance on the dataset. The video concludes by mentioning the advancements in deep neural networks, such as AlexNet, VGG, GoogleNet, and ResNet.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: In the field of computer vision, researchers have made significant advancements in image recognition through the use of deep neural networks. In 2015, a team in China developed a 152-layer Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) called ResNet, which challenged the common belief that neural networks couldn't go too deep. This breakthrough became the new benchmark for image recognition. Since then, there has been a shift towards using ensembles of multiple neural networks to further improve performance.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: Transfer learning was used in the Kaggle Data Science Bowl 2017 to determine if a patient had lung cancer or not. The winning solution used the Microsoft ResNet CNN, retrained with the Microsoft Cognitive Toolkit and LightGBM. This approach took only 53 minutes and showcased the power of transfer learning in computer vision tasks. CNNs are also used in other domains, such as sound analysis and natural language processing.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: Custom Vision AI is a cloud-based solution that allows users to retrain a custom vision model without needing extensive experience in computer vision or deep learning. It is important to properly prepare image data by using consistently sized and normalized images to ensure the effectiveness of the model. While deep learning is a powerful tool, traditional approaches such as OpenCV or SVM classifiers can still be relevant for certain problems.

speaker: Micheleen Harris
title: Demystifying AI
summary: The video discusses the process of creating a neural network with feature extraction layers and increasing depth by adding hidden layers and neurons. It demonstrates how the network learns and adapts to solve a specific problem. Different activation functions, such as Tanh, ReLu, and Sigmoid, are mentioned, as well as the importance of the learning rate in determining the speed and accuracy of learning. The video also touches on the concept of weight calculation and the ability to manually adjust weights to influence the network's decision-making process.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: Mehrnoosh Sameki and Besmira Nushi discuss the Error Analysis toolkit, an open-source tool that helps machine learning practitioners identify and diagnose errors in AI models. They emphasize the importance of understanding model errors and their root causes in order to build responsible and reliable AI solutions. The toolkit provides interpretability and fairness features, as well as debugging capabilities through global and local explanations.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The focus of machine learning evaluation should go beyond just accuracy and consider aspects like interpretability, fairness, and reliability. Errors in machine learning models can have various impacts, such as safety issues or fairness concerns if certain demographic groups are disproportionately affected. Additionally, errors can erode user trust in the system, leading to a loss of confidence in machine learning as a whole. Fairness and interpretability are subsets of the broader concept of general errors in machine learning.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The video showcases a toolkit called Responsible AI Widgets, which allows users to analyze and diagnose errors in machine learning models. The toolkit includes interpretability techniques such as SHAP and global surrogate models, which help explain the factors influencing predictions. Users can generate global and local explanations and pass them to the error analysis dashboard for further analysis. The toolkit is open source and can be easily installed using pip.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The error analysis dashboard is a tool that helps identify and understand errors in data predictions. It uses a TreeMap to cluster data into interpretable subgroups based on error rates. By clicking on different cohorts, users can see the proportion of errors and characteristics of the individuals within that cohort. This tool allows for a deeper understanding of where errors are occurring and how they are distributed across different groups.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The video showcases a tool that helps analyze errors in machine learning models. It allows users to identify cohorts where errors are concentrated and investigate the factors contributing to those errors. Users can also unselect certain features and retrain the model accordingly. The tool provides a heat map view to analyze error rates in sub-cohorts based on selected features. Overall, it offers adaptability and insights for improving model performance.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The video discusses the increase in error rates based on education levels and gender. It highlights a pattern of error rates increasing as education levels get higher. Additionally, there is a discrepancy between error rates for males and females within each education group, with males having a higher error rate. The video also mentions the exploration phase, which includes data exploration, global explanation, local explanations, and what-if scenarios to diagnose and mitigate errors.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: The video discusses the challenges of distinguishing between income groups in a machine learning model due to imbalanced training data. The speaker suggests augmenting the data to include more labels and examples of both income groups to improve the model's performance. They emphasize the importance of understanding the data and debugging the model's predictions, highlighting the similarities between responsible AI engineering and traditional software development practices.

speaker: Mehrnoosh, Besmira
title: Build Responsible AI using Error Analysis toolkit
summary: Automated machine learning techniques can now build multiple models simultaneously, but relying solely on aggregate metrics like accuracy or error rate may not be sufficient. The Error Analysis Toolkit, combined with the InterpretML Toolkit, offers global and local explanations for model predictions. It allows users to understand which factors are most influential for different groups and perform what-if analyses to debug and improve models. For more information, visit erroranalysis.ai.

speaker: Luis
title: AIShow | Azure Cognitive Search Overview
summary: Luis, a Program Manager in the Azure Cognitive Search team, provides an overview of Azure Cognitive Search in this episode of the AI Show. Azure Cognitive Search is a platform as a service that allows users to create search-enabled applications for web, mobile, and line of business. It offers a range of capabilities, including autocomplete, synonyms, suggestions, filters, and more, to enhance the search experience. The video highlights how Azure Cognitive Search provides these capabilities even for users who are not search experts.

speaker: Luis
title: AIShow | Azure Cognitive Search Overview
summary: Azure Cognitive Search is a powerful tool that can connect to both structured and unstructured data sources. It uses document cracking skills to extract content from various file formats, such as PDFs and PowerPoint files, and enriches the information using AI and machine learning algorithms. With Azure Cognitive Search, you can easily index and search through structured and unstructured content without writing any code.

speaker: Luis
title: AIShow | Azure Cognitive Search Overview
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Azure Cognitive Search to extract and index data from unstructured content without writing code. The presenter shows how to connect to Azure Blob Storage, define enrichment steps, and apply cognitive services to extract information from files such as PDFs. Built-in skills can be selected to perform various tasks, including OCR and translation. The video emphasizes the importance of creating a cognitive services resource in the same region as Azure Cognitive Search for optimal performance.

speaker: Luis
title: AIShow | Azure Cognitive Search Overview
summary: In this video, the speaker explains how to customize the search index and define index properties. They demonstrate how to select attributes for fields, such as making them retrievable or searchable. They also discuss the use of analyzers to handle language intricacies and improve search results. The video shows the process of creating an index set and setting up indexers to extract information from documents.

speaker: Luis
title: AIShow | Azure Cognitive Search Overview
summary: Document cracking is the process of extracting text and other information from various types of documents, such as PDFs, Word documents, and HTML files. This information can then be indexed and searched using Azure Cognitive Search. The video demonstrates how the indexer cracks open the documents, extracts the relevant information, and stores it in an index. Users can then search for specific documents or information within the documents using the search capabilities provided by Azure Cognitive Search.

speaker: Micheline Harris
title: The Simplest Machine Learning
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Micheline Harris introduces the simplest machine learning algorithm, linear regression, and explains its terminology. She then moves on to discuss the perceptron, the simplest neural network, and introduces the concept of an activation function. This episode provides a clear and concise explanation of these fundamental machine learning concepts in under 10 minutes.

speaker: Micheline Harris
title: The Simplest Machine Learning
summary: Neural networks are a type of design used in deep learning, which implements algorithms. Activation functions play a crucial role in neural networks by applying a threshold to the output of an optimized equation. Multiple neurons can be stacked together in hidden layers to create more complex neural networks. These networks are particularly effective in computer vision, speech recognition, natural language processing, robotics, and recommender systems.

speaker: Nilesh Acharya
title: Automation to accelerate apply and outperform your machine learning models
summary: Nilesh Acharya, a Senior Program Manager at Microsoft, explains how automated machine learning (AutoML) can help accelerate the process of building machine learning models. AutoML simplifies the iterative process of data preparation, model training, and hyperparameter selection by automating these steps. It uses machine learning techniques to recommend pipelines and optimize model accuracy, saving time, money, and resources. AutoML is a powerful tool for data scientists, analysts, and developers looking to build ML models with greater speed and efficiency.

speaker: Vishwac Sena Kannan, Neha Rajput
title: Author rich content in QnA Maker knowledge base and enable role based sharing
summary: Vishwac Sena Kannan, a Program Manager on the Bot Framework Team, discusses the advanced understanding and language generation capabilities offered by the Bot Framework Composer in this special Build edition of the AI Show. Neha Rajput, a product manager in QnA Maker, highlights the new features coming to QnA Maker, including Rich Text Authoring and Role Based Access Control. She demonstrates how these features enhance the authoring experience and showcases how QnA Maker is being used to provide information about COVID-19.

speaker: Vishwac Sena Kannan, Neha Rajput
title: Author rich content in QnA Maker knowledge base and enable role based sharing
summary: The video demonstrates the use of Rich Text Authoring in creating Q&A pairs for a bot. It shows how to add hyperlinks, emojis, and formatting to the text. The video also introduces the Gembed feature, which allows for better control and collaboration among content authors by providing editor and reader roles within the QnA Maker service. This eliminates the need for workarounds like sharing access or using separate services for testing and production.

speaker: Vishwac Sena Kannan, Neha Rajput
title: Author rich content in QnA Maker knowledge base and enable role based sharing
summary: The video explains the different roles and permissions in QnA Maker, a service that allows users to create and manage knowledge bases. The roles include the editor, who can create and update content but not publish it, the reader, who can only read and test the service, and the publisher, who has full permissions including publishing and deleting knowledge bases. The video demonstrates how to assign roles to users in the Azure portal.

speaker: Vishwac Sena Kannan, Neha Rajput
title: Author rich content in QnA Maker knowledge base and enable role based sharing
summary: The video discusses the differences between the editor and reader roles in QnA Maker, a tool used to create and manage knowledge bases. The editor role allows for creating and updating knowledge bases but not publishing them, while the reader role only allows for reading and testing knowledge bases. The video also highlights how QnA Maker is being used to provide information about COVID-19, with examples of healthcare bots and awareness bots created using the tool.

speaker: Vishwac Sena Kannan, Neha Rajput
title: Author rich content in QnA Maker knowledge base and enable role based sharing
summary: The video showcases the QnA Maker V2, a tool that allows users to create FAQ bots easily. It highlights the benefits of using QnA Maker, such as low effort and time required for bot creation. The new version offers a self-hosted architecture and seamless scaling. It also introduces a deep-learnt ranking model and Machine Reading Comprehension for more precise answers. Viewers are encouraged to sign up for the QnA Maker V2 private preview.

speaker: Seth, Seth Juarez
title: An Intuitive Approach to Machine Learning Models (Part 1 of 4)
summary: Seth Juarez presents an introduction to deep learning in this four-part series. In part one, he discusses the differences between AI, machine learning, and deep learning, when machine learning is an appropriate tool, and what a machine learning model is. Seth aims to provide a clear understanding of these concepts and their internal workings. The series offers valuable insights for both practitioners and beginners in the field.

speaker: Seth, Seth Juarez
title: An Intuitive Approach to Machine Learning Models (Part 1 of 4)
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are often misunderstood concepts. AI can be thought of as a search problem, while ML involves generating algorithms based on examples. Neural networks are considered ML, but when they have a large number of layers, they are referred to as deep learning. The decision of when to use AI or ML depends on the specific problem at hand. An example of using ML is detecting if a check image is upside down by sampling pixels at the top.

speaker: Seth, Seth Juarez
title: An Intuitive Approach to Machine Learning Models (Part 1 of 4)
summary: Machine learning fills the gap between a programmer's intuition and the ability to solve complex problems. While programmers can write code to address specific scenarios, machine learning allows for the creation of models that can handle any situation. By providing examples and data, machine learning algorithms can predict outcomes and provide solutions. This different way of thinking about programming can be challenging for those unfamiliar with the field, but it ultimately enhances problem-solving capabilities.

speaker: Seth, Seth Juarez
title: An Intuitive Approach to Machine Learning Models (Part 1 of 4)
summary: In this video, the speaker explains the concept of building convolutional neural networks (CNNs) from the bottom-up. They use the example of predicting whether images are darker at the top or bottom. The speaker discusses different approaches, such as comparing the average values and using magic weights (W) to multiply the input values. The video encourages viewer interaction and prompts them to identify any missing information.

speaker: Seth, Seth Juarez
title: An Intuitive Approach to Machine Learning Models (Part 1 of 4)
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the concept of bias in machine learning models. They explain that bias is a way to influence the output of a model by adding a positive or negative number. The speaker demonstrates this concept using a simple perceptron algorithm. They then expand on this idea, showing how it can be applied to more complex models, such as predicting top, middle, or bottom. The speaker also mentions that this approach can be used for digit recognition, achieving 92% accuracy on the MNIST dataset.

speaker: Dennis Eikelenboom
title: Data to ML Tracking with Azure Machine Learning
summary: Dennis Eikelenboom, Program Manager on the Azure Machine Learning team, discusses the importance of tracking in Azure Machine Learning. He demonstrates how Azure Machine Learning enables organizations to keep track of assets such as code, data, and models throughout the machine learning lifecycle. Using the example of an analytics company called Contoso, he shows how tracking helps with experiment reproducibility, operational efficiency, and compliance with legislative requirements.

speaker: Dennis Eikelenboom
title: Data to ML Tracking with Azure Machine Learning
summary: This video discusses the importance of tracking and managing assets in Azure Machine Learning. It highlights the benefits of keeping track of datasets, experiment runs, and model versions, such as reproducibility, building on existing work, compliance with legal requirements, and identifying issues in production. Azure Machine Learning provides tracking capabilities to simplify this process and allows users to trace back to specific experiments and dataset versions.

speaker: Maksim Luciana
title: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance
summary: Maksim Luciana, a program manager on the Azure Machine Learning team, introduces Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance in this episode of the AI Show. Compute Instance is a managed virtual machine in the cloud that supports various open-source projects like R, TensorFlow, and Jupyter notebooks. It is pre-configured for machine learning tasks, eliminating setup time for data scientists. Compute Instance aims to bridge the gap between data scientists and IT professionals, providing a secure and compliant environment for ML development.

speaker: Maksim Luciana
title: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance
summary: In this video, the speaker introduces a new feature called Compute Instance in the machine learning studio UI. This feature allows data scientists to have secure and flexible access to a virtual machine, eliminating the need for additional steps like logging into a separate machine. The Compute Instance is fully integrated into the workspace, enabling collaboration with other users. The speaker also demonstrates customization by installing a popular visualization library and using it within the studio UI.

speaker: Maksim Luciana
title: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance
summary: The video showcases the integration of Jupyter notebooks into the Azure machine learning workspace. Users can easily create and manage notebook VMs, selecting GPU or CPU machines and customizing security options. The notebook VMs are managed and shared within the workspace, providing a secure and efficient environment for data scientists and IT professionals in enterprise settings.

speaker: Maksim Luciana
title: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance
summary: The video discusses the features of a computing platform that offers infrastructure-as-a-service virtual machines (VMs). Users have access to the VMs through secure controls provided by the platform. One notable feature is the ability to stop the VMs at any time while preserving customizations, allowing users to save on compute costs. The platform also supports collaboration by allowing multiple VMs to mount the same file share. Additionally, the video demonstrates the integration of the platform with a machine learning service.

speaker: Maksim Luciana
title: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance
summary: Azure Machine Learning Compute Instance allows data scientists to collaborate and share their work seamlessly. By connecting to the machine learning service, the notebook enables distributed machine learning jobs and integrated authentication. The workspace provides widgets to show progress, and metrics can be displayed in a way that is integrated with the compute instance. Collaboration features allow for easy sharing and editing of notebooks, making it convenient for data scientists to work together.

speaker: Francesca Lazzeri
title: AI Show - Deep Learning vs. Machine Learning
summary: Francesca Lazzeri explains the difference between machine learning and deep learning in this episode of the AI Show. Machine learning is a portfolio of algorithms that use data to learn and provide results, while deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks. AI, on the other hand, is about consuming machine learning models to build intelligent applications. Francesca also discusses how deep learning can be applied to real-world scenarios.

speaker: Francesca Lazzeri
title: AI Show - Deep Learning vs. Machine Learning
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the differences between artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning. They explain the various types of neural networks used in deep learning, such as convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks. They also mention the importance of hardware dependencies and the featurization process. The video concludes by mentioning a helpful document that provides more information on deep learning and how to implement it on Azure.

speaker: Santos Pulay
title: Azure Machine Learning Pipelines
summary: Santos Pulay, a Program Manager in the Azure Machine Learning Team, discusses Azure Machine Learning Pipelines in this episode of the AI Show. He explains that a typical machine learning workflow consists of three phases: data preparation, training, and deployment. Santos highlights the advantages of using pipelines, such as reusability of steps and significant cost savings in compute resources. By breaking down the workflow into modular steps, data and computations can be easily reused, improving efficiency and reducing the risk of starting over from scratch.

speaker: Santos Pulay
title: Azure Machine Learning Pipelines
summary: Azure Machine Learning Service allows users to easily set up and run machine learning pipelines. These pipelines consist of discrete steps that can be packaged into a single Python file. The steps can be stitched together using data dependencies, where one step produces data that is used by the subsequent step. The pipelines can be published as REST endpoints, allowing authorized users to call them and change parameters, with only the necessary steps being rerun.

speaker: Santos Pulay
title: Azure Machine Learning Pipelines
summary: In this video, the host discusses the capabilities of Azure Machine Learning Service pipelines. The pipelines allow for parallel or sequential execution of tasks, and can be used for a variety of computations, including training and generation. The video also explains the different types of steps in a pipeline, such as data sources, modules, and compute options. The ability to store and reuse data outputs is highlighted as a key feature, along with the collaboration and cost-saving benefits of using pipelines in the machine learning workflow.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: Panos Periorellis, Principal Program Manager for Azure Cognitive Services, discusses call center transcription analytics in this special edition of the AI Show. He demonstrates how to onboard onto speech services and quickly gain insights from phone calls. Periorellis also highlights new features, such as bulk transcriptions, model swapping, and language identification. For audio customization, he recommends visiting speech.Microsoft.com to explore the improvements made on the Speech Studio.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: Microsoft has made improvements to their Speech Studio, including updating their models with telephony data to provide more accurate transcriptions. While customization or adaptation is still important, they now offer high accuracy interpretation with out-of-the-box base models for customers who may not be able to adapt the model immediately. In a demo, they show how a phone call conversation is analyzed using cognitive services, with files produced for transcription and analytics.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: The video demonstrates how an end-to-end application can be created using Azure Speech services. It showcases a demo where a bot handles a call and transfers it to a human agent. The video also highlights the analytics capabilities of the platform, including sentiment analysis, talk to silence ratio, and text analytics. It emphasizes the customization options available for creating tailored analytics for real conversations.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to create an end-to-end application using telephony and Azure AI. They also showcase the use of ARM templates, which are portable configuration files that automate the setup of resources in Azure. The templates allow for customization of parameters such as storage account name, call transfer numbers, bot settings, speech recognition parameters, and virtual machine credentials. Once the parameters are set, the infrastructure is automatically created.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: The video demonstrates how to set up an ARM template to automatically transcribe and analyze audio files stored in a storage account. Parameters such as storage account name, Speech Services subscription key, region, profanity filtering, and sentiment analysis can be customized. The ARM template creates functions for audio file retrieval and transcription, a virtual machine, a Key Vault for storing credentials, a SQL database for storing transcription information, and an AudioCodes resource for bridging Azure and telephony.

speaker: Panos Periorellis
title: Improve Customer Service with Call Center Analytics
summary: AudioCodes serves as a bridge between Azure and telephony, allowing for parallel call processing and call recording. The recorded calls can be sent to a storage account for further analysis. The demos showcased the use of online contact centers, cognitive services, and transcription analytics to reduce customer friction, lower costs, understand customer behavior, evaluate agent performance, ensure compliance, and monitor sentiment. Microsoft continues to deliver innovative solutions for call center businesses.

speaker: Hi, everyone. In this video, we are going to talk about time series forecasting with Azure Machine Learning.
title: Time Series Forecasting with Azure Machine Learning
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses time series forecasting with Azure Machine Learning. They demonstrate how to build, train, and deploy a time series forecasting solution using Azure Machine Learning. The video covers topics such as setting up the development environment, accessing and examining the data, training with Automated Machine Learning, exploring the results, and accessing the forecasting model through the Azure portal.

speaker: Hi, everyone. In this video, we are going to talk about time series forecasting with Azure Machine Learning.
title: Time Series Forecasting with Azure Machine Learning
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Azure Machine Learning service for time series forecasting. It covers steps such as ingesting and previewing data, splitting data for training and validation, configuring AutoML experiments, selecting the best model, testing the model, and deploying it. The video also mentions the availability of documentation and the option to create a free Azure subscription for getting started with Azure Machine Learning service.

speaker: Hazem El-Hammamy
title: AI Show | Nov 5 | Ignite Recap | Language Services
summary: Hazem El-Hammamy discusses the announcement made at Ignite regarding Language Services. Text Analytics, QnA Maker, and Language Understanding (LUIS) are now unified under Language Services. The video provides an overview of the challenges that Language Cognitive Services address and showcases the new features and capabilities of the unified service. The goal is to make it easier to automate processes involving text analysis and natural language processing.

speaker: Hazem El-Hammamy
title: AI Show | Nov 5 | Ignite Recap | Language Services
summary: Microsoft has unified its language services into one powerful and user-friendly platform called Language Studio. Developers can now access a range of features and capabilities, including text classification, information extraction, and conversation understanding. The platform also offers custom capabilities, such as creating custom classifiers and entities. Language Studio can be accessed through the language.cognitive.azure.com portal, allowing users to try out pre-built and custom capabilities without writing code.

speaker: Hazem El-Hammamy
title: AI Show | Nov 5 | Ignite Recap | Language Services
summary: The video showcases the capabilities of a video AI assistant, allowing users to easily extract health information from text and analyze it. The pre-built capability enables users to extract dosages and medication names, while also visualizing the relationship between them. The JSON response provides all the extracted information and links to known data sources. Additionally, the video demonstrates a custom capability called conversational language understanding, which allows users to create their own projects.

speaker: Hazem El-Hammamy
title: AI Show | Nov 5 | Ignite Recap | Language Services
summary: To create a custom project in Conversational Language Understanding, you have two options: Conversation Project or Orchestration Workflow Project. The Conversation Project allows you to create custom classifiers and entity extractors, while the Orchestration Workflow Project lets you connect multiple conversation projects or question answering knowledge bases. After creating a project, you can define intents and entities, provide training data, train a model, and deploy it. All these actions can be done directly in the Language Studio.

speaker: Hazem El-Hammamy
title: AI Show | Nov 5 | Ignite Recap | Language Services
summary: The video showcases the new features and capabilities of the unified language services, including conversational language understanding, custom-named entity recognition, and custom text classification. It also highlights the multilingual capabilities of the CustomService, demonstrating how it can accurately predict intents and extract information in different languages, even with minimal training data. The video concludes by providing links for further exploration and learning.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: Moritz Steller and Setu Chokshi discuss MLOps (v2) and its importance in unifying MLOps at Microsoft. They cover the fundamentals, approach, architectures, and demo the new features. MLOps is defined as a process that combines platform, people, and processes to operationalize machine learning models. The solution accelerator they present aims to solve the challenges in this field and enable MLOps at scale in a modular and secure way.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the concept of MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) and its importance in the overall pipeline of deploying and monitoring machine learning models. It highlights that while modeling is an exciting part, the majority of the work lies in operationalization, standards, and solutioning. The term "MLOps v2" refers to Microsoft's approach to MLOps, which takes into account the variations in technology stacks and AI workloads to provide tailored solutions for different industries and customers.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the challenges of implementing MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) and introduces MLOps v2 as a solution. MLOps v2 aims to automate and simplify the process of deploying AI models into production. It addresses challenges related to roles and skills within an enterprise, as well as the variation of tools and technologies used in different departments. The goal is to streamline the process and make it easier for data scientists and product managers to deliver AI solutions efficiently.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: Implementing an effective MLOps system can be challenging due to various factors. Different departments may use different tools, making it difficult to standardize processes. Artifacts and versioning can pose challenges in terms of model registries and metadata. Development and production can get stuck in experimentation, hindering the ability to move quickly to product. To address these challenges, an MLOps system should be inclusive of people, processes, and platforms, allowing for flexibility and scalability within an enterprise.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: MLOps v2 focuses on five technical pillars to provide a simple, secure, fast, scalable, and modular solution for AI workloads. The goal is to allow data scientists to focus on their projects without worrying about repetitive maintenance tasks. The solution offers native security measures, enables fast product development, provides a stack of technologies for different AI workloads, and allows for customization and automation through templates and reusability.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses a concept called "spa's checkout" which is an SH script that defines variables for different ML and CI/CD tools. There are three repositories: one for infrastructure templates, one for project code, and one for demos. The system is highly repeatable and can be applied to different personas in MLOps. The architecture includes a data estate, infrastructure setup, and a secure workspace for model development. The video recommends exploring the Solution Accelerator for more details.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the process of building and deploying machine learning models using Azure Machine Learning. It covers the inner loop, where models are developed and trained, and the outer loop, where models are tested and deployed. The video also highlights the importance of model and data monitoring, particularly in complex scenarios such as image or natural language data.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the challenges of implementing machine learning models in the fields of NLP and computer vision. It emphasizes the need for human involvement in tasks such as data labeling and model retraining to ensure ethical and responsible AI practices. The video highlights the complexity of computer vision and the potential bias in language, emphasizing the importance of human oversight in these areas.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the importance of human involvement in MLOps systems to address potential bias implications of models, particularly in the transformer space. The speakers introduce a GitHub repository called Azure MLOpsv2, which provides a blueprint for implementing MLOps architecture. The repository includes documentation, high-quality architectures, and code that can be modified and deployed using various tools such as terraform, Bicep, CLI, or SDK. Users can choose their preferred deployment method and customize the script accordingly.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: To deploy your code using sparse checkout in Git, update your Git version to the latest one. Configure your script to create custom code and push it to your code repository. Set up your infrastructure using the provided architecture and different environments. Configure unique names for namespaces and post spaces. Set up service principles for pipeline deployment and create service connections. Add a new pipeline using your GitHub connection.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video demonstrates setting up a new pipeline for MLOps using GitHub and Azure DevOps. It explains how to choose existing pipelines and customize them for different environments. The video also highlights the use of reusable templates to avoid errors caused by copy-pasting. The setup includes infrastructure deployment, model training, online deployment, and batch deployment. The video provides a deeper understanding of MLOps model execution.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video demonstrates how to set up and run a machine learning pipeline using Azure Machine Learning. The process involves preparing and cleaning data, training a model, and creating a pipeline. The video also discusses the option to reuse components in different projects and the ability to run the pipeline without blocking other MLOps runners. The overall goal is to streamline the machine learning workflow and improve efficiency.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the evaluation process for machine learning models in the context of taxi fare prediction. The evaluation involves comparing the performance of the new model with previously registered models. Only the best-performing model is registered and deployed. Additionally, the evaluation includes assessing fairness using the responsibly AI toolkit to ensure the model is unbiased towards different vendors.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses the importance of model fairness evaluation and how it can be incorporated into the model evaluation process. The speaker demonstrates how to set up fairness metrics and evaluate models for bias. They also highlight the use of model explanations to ensure that the models are performing as intended. The video emphasizes the convenience of integrating these steps into the existing workflow.

speaker: Moritz Steller, Setu Chokshi
title: MLOps (v2) - Unifying MLOps at Microsoft
summary: The video discusses MLOps v2, a unified approach to machine learning operations at Microsoft. It highlights the use of MLflow for model deployment and showcases online and batch deployment pipelines. The video emphasizes the collaborative nature of the project and encourages community engagement. Overall, MLOps v2 aims to streamline the machine learning process and provide a standardized framework for successful implementation.

speaker: Wenxin Wei
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 1
summary: Wenxin Wei introduces the Responsible AI dashboard for text models, which includes tools for model interpretability, unfairness assessment, error analysis, and model performance analysis. The dashboard provides a holistic assessment and debugging experience for text models, allowing users to make informed business decisions. Wenxin demonstrates how the dashboard works and shares customer-use highlights. This is part one of a two-part series on responsible AI support for images and text models.

speaker: Wenxin Wei
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 1
summary: The video showcases a demo of an RAI text insight component that uses an ESG text classification model. The component includes an error analysis feature to identify model mistakes and blindspots, a model overview to assess performance, a confusion matrix to analyze misclassifications, and a data analysis component with table and chart views to examine patterns and distributions. The demo highlights the model's strong performance in environmental topics but lower accuracy in non-ESG classifications.

speaker: Wenxin Wei
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 1
summary: The video discusses the use of scatter plots and feature importance dashboards to analyze and understand the performance of a classification model. By visualizing the error distribution and examining the top important words, patterns and insights can be gained. The video emphasizes the importance of consistency between predictions and context, and highlights the need for data investigation to identify and address model errors.

speaker: Wenxin Wei
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 1
summary: The video discusses the use of the RAI Text Insights component in Azure Machine Learning to generate a Responsible AI dashboard for text classification models. The dashboard provides various capabilities such as error analysis, model overview, confusion matrix, and data analysis to help diagnose and enhance the model. The video also mentions future support for question answering and large language models.

speaker: Nilesh Acharya
title: How to Configure Automated ML Experiments
summary: Nilesh Acharya, Senior Program Manager, discusses the common configuration settings for automating machine learning experiments using the Python SDK. He covers topics such as where the training will occur (locally or remotely), defining max cores per iteration and max concurrent iterations for remote compute, and the recommended data formats for machine learning. Examples are provided for importing numpy arrays and pandas data frames.

speaker: Nilesh Acharya
title: How to Configure Automated ML Experiments
summary: To efficiently train a machine learning experiment, it is important to consider the data format and location. Using the data fetch method, data can be imported from various sources such as numpy arrays or pandas data frames. Validation and testing can be done using k-fold, Monte Carlo, or custom splits. The X and Y values represent the training features and labels, respectively. By properly defining the validation method, accurate results can be obtained.

speaker: Nilesh Acharya
title: How to Configure Automated ML Experiments
summary: When working with a custom or mannequin validation data set, it's important to define the training data and validation splits. Pre-processing techniques such as dropping high cardinality or no variance features, imputing missing values, generating additional features, and transforming encoding can be used to cleanse and enhance the data. Additionally, you can choose the models or algorithms to train your data against, either by allowing or denying specific algorithms or using an automated machine learning approach.

speaker: Nilesh Acharya
title: How to Configure Automated ML Experiments
summary: The video discusses the various settings and options available in automated machine learning. It covers topics such as model performance, auto deny/auto blacklist, primary metric selection, and exit criteria. The video emphasizes the importance of defining these settings to optimize the training and selection of machine learning models. It also provides examples and instructions on how to use these settings effectively.

speaker: Adina Trufinescu
title: Computer Vision for Spatial Analysis
summary: Adina Trufinescu, a Program Manager for computer vision at Azure Cognitive Service, discusses the new feature called spatial analysis. This feature allows computer vision AI to analyze video streams, enabling scenarios such as people counting, social distancing monitoring, and tracking entry and exit in physical spaces. Industries such as retail, manufacturing, and real estate management can benefit from this technology to optimize store layouts and improve customer experiences.

speaker: Adina Trufinescu
title: Computer Vision for Spatial Analysis
summary: Spatial analysis technology is being used in various industries, including retail, manufacturing, and real estate management. It helps businesses modify store layouts, monitor safety in restricted areas, and ensure social distancing and maximum occupancy. To address privacy concerns, the technology is deployed as a Docker container at the edge, giving customers control over their data. Additionally, responsible AI guidance is provided to ensure ethical and responsible use of the technology.

speaker: Adina Trufinescu
title: Computer Vision for Spatial Analysis
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the responsible use of AI in spatial analysis. They demonstrate various use cases, such as people counting, social distancing, and entry-exit monitoring in retail spaces. The speaker emphasizes the importance of upholding the dignity of end users while utilizing this technology. They also briefly mention how this can be implemented in Azure through an IoT Hub service.

speaker: Adina Trufinescu
title: Computer Vision for Spatial Analysis
summary: Azure IoT Hub and Azure IoT Edge devices are required to deploy the spatial analysis container. The device should have an NVIDIA T4 GPU, and Azure Stack Edge with GPU is recommended. The spatial analysis container is deployed as an Azure IoT Hub, and the configuration for the operation is passed through the Module Identity Twin. Customers, such as ANC in India, are already using this technology for pandemic compliance and real estate management. For more information, visit aka.msspatialanalysis.

speaker: Manash Goswami
title: ONNX Runtime
summary: Manash Goswami, Principal Program Manager for AI Frameworks at Microsoft, discusses the integration of ONNX Runtime with Xilinx's FPGA solution. ONNX Runtime is an open-source inference engine that allows for the execution of ML models in various hardware environments. The integration with Xilinx's U250 FPGAs enables the execution of ONNX models. This collaboration between Microsoft and Xilinx provides data science teams with flexibility in model development and deployment while optimizing neural network computations.

speaker: Manash Goswami
title: ONNX Runtime
summary: The ONNX Runtime Inference Engine version 1.3 has been released, with support for ONNX spec version 1.7. The update includes the general availability of the direct ML execution provider on Windows, providing acceleration for ONNX model inference across different platforms on Windows devices. Additionally, a new partner, Xilinx, has joined the hardware ecosystem for ONNX Runtime, building the execution provider for the Vitis AI software library, allowing developers to execute ONNX models on the Xilinx U250 FPGA platform.

speaker: Manash Goswami
title: ONNX Runtime
summary: The collaboration between Xilinx, Microsoft, and Peakspeed has resulted in the development of the Azure NP Series VMs, which leverage FPGA technology for high-performance computing. Peakspeed has successfully deployed their geospatial imaging solutions on the Azure NP VMs, achieving significant performance improvements compared to CPU and GPU instances. The integration of ONNX Runtime and the Vitis AI stack allows developers to accelerate their applications on FPGA endpoints in Azure and on-premises using Xilinx U250 hardware. Xilinx will soon release a pre-built VM image in the Azure Marketplace for easy deployment.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Chris Wendt, the Group Program Manager for Microsoft Translation Service, discusses the Translator API and cognitive services. The translation service translates between natural language, speech, and text, with the goal of breaking down language barriers. While automated translation is cheaper and faster than human translation, the quality may not be as good, especially for less commonly translated languages.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: Machine translation has been around since the 1950s and has steadily improved over the years. The latest advancements, such as neural networks and transformer models, have significantly increased translation quality. Users can further enhance translation quality by utilizing features like Custom Translator, which allows them to upload previously translated documents. The goal is to achieve human parity in translation quality. In certain domains, such as Chinese to English news, machine translation has already reached this level. However, more complex and informal language poses challenges for achieving perfect translations.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: The video discusses the usage of a translation API for text. The API allows users to translate text between 1 and 70 languages, without the need to specify the source language. The API also provides a function to detect languages and a function for transliteration, which converts text between different scripts. The video emphasizes the accuracy of the language detection feature, except for closely related languages.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: The video discusses the language detection and sentence breaking functionalities of the translation API. Language detection helps identify the language of a text, while sentence breaking is important for translating longer documents without producing bad translations. The video also mentions sample code on GitHub for translating longer documents and mentions the upcoming document translation API. The video then transitions to discussing the speech translation functionality, which combines speech recognition and translation services to provide accurate translations.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: To embark on translating speech, a client-side SDK is offered. While translating text is simple, speech requires a streaming protocol that can be difficult to manage manually. The SDK is available for major operating systems and programming languages. An example code is provided, where the source and target languages are specified, and the recognizer provides the translation result. Real-time actions can be performed before the end of the speech. Multiple languages can be translated simultaneously, and audio of one language is provided for free.

speaker: Chris Wendt
title: Translator API – What’s New
summary: The video showcases the real-time conversation capabilities of the Microsoft Translator API. It demonstrates how the API can translate speech in multiple languages and enable bidirectional conversations. The video also highlights the upcoming feature of a cloud-based conversation system that allows multiple participants speaking different languages to communicate with each other. Viewers are invited to visit Microsoft.com/translator for more information and to participate in the private preview of the functionality.

speaker: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink
title: Nuance: Developing a Clinical Research Search tool with Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink from Nuance discuss how they used Azure Cognitive Search to develop a clinical research search tool. The tool helps clinical researchers in pathology and radiology find patients that match specific criteria and analyze patterns in recent diagnoses. Nuance's solution has been cited in over 200 academic articles and has seen significant performance improvements since migrating to Cognitive Search.

speaker: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink
title: Nuance: Developing a Clinical Research Search tool with Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the challenges of analyzing unstructured healthcare data and introduces a product called Empower Clinical Analytics. The product allows users to search for specific keywords in various types of medical data, such as radiology reports, pathology reports, and clinical notes. The speaker demonstrates how the product can be used to search for reports containing the keyword "pneumonia" and filter out irrelevant or negative findings. Empower Clinical Analytics aims to provide key clinical insights and improve patient outcomes.

speaker: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink
title: Nuance: Developing a Clinical Research Search tool with Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Empower is a powerful clinical data analysis tool that allows users to answer complex clinical questions and perform in-depth analysis. With features like maximizing positive findings, sequential searches, and creating alerts, Empower provides healthcare professionals with the ability to efficiently analyze patient data. The tool has gained recognition in the industry, with over 200 research articles citing its use. Empower has scaled and grown significantly, indexing approximately 1.2 billion reports.

speaker: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink
title: Nuance: Developing a Clinical Research Search tool with Azure Cognitive Search
summary: Empower, a company that has been scaling rapidly in the past four years, faced challenges with their old index solution when it came to handling large data sets. They turned to Azure cognitive search, a platform that offers a hosted product with improved performance and accuracy. By leveraging the search syntax and customizing the solution, Empower was able to empower clinicians by helping them find the right information at the right time.

speaker: Derek Legenzoff and Jamin Wunderink
title: Nuance: Developing a Clinical Research Search tool with Azure Cognitive Search
summary: In this video, the presenters demonstrate how to use Azure Cognitive Search to build a clinical research search tool called Empower. They show how to perform fielded searches, use proximity search to find specific terms within a certain distance of each other, and use facets to analyze data and gain insights. They also provide links for further information on Azure Cognitive Search and Empower.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging

summary: Qinying Liao and Ashley Bailey from Veritone introduce Custom Neural Voice "Lite," a new feature in public preview that allows users to clone their voice by recording just 5 minutes of speech data. The feature also reduces training data and time to market for customers.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging
title: The AI Show: Ep 56 | Create a Custom Neural Voice "Lite" for Brands and Characters with Veritone
summary: The video showcases a voice conversion technology that can convert any text into spoken language that sounds human, in the voice that represents the customer's brand. It also highlights the cross lingual adaptation capability, which allows the model to speak multiple languages without the need for additional training data. The technology can maintain voice characteristics and accents across different languages, making it suitable for reaching a diverse global audience.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging
title: The AI Show: Ep 56 | Create a Custom Neural Voice "Lite" for Brands and Characters with Veritone
summary: Veritone, an enterprise AI company, utilizes Microsoft's Custom Neural Voice to offer both stock and custom voices. This technology allows them to replicate someone's voice in multiple languages for various applications. Veritone Voice has gained traction in industries such as media and entertainment. The synthetic voices created using text-to-speech are so realistic that it's hard to tell the difference from the real voices. Veritone also offers speech-to-speech capabilities.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging
title: The AI Show: Ep 56 | Create a Custom Neural Voice "Lite" for Brands and Characters with Veritone
summary: Our AI technology allows brands to work with talent to create authorized and verified voice clones for advertisements and endorsements. This saves time for busy talent who may not be able to make it to the studio for recordings. The technology is also used for audiobooks, audio description for visually impaired individuals, financial earnings calls, weather reporting, news narration, localization, e-learning courses, training materials, and radio production. The use of voice clones creates a more authentic experience for listeners.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging
title: The AI Show: Ep 56 | Create a Custom Neural Voice "Lite" for Brands and Characters with Veritone
summary: The video discusses the use of AI in radio production, specifically in creating short liners, sweepers, and ads for radio personalities. It also presents a case study of localizing podcast content in different languages using AI translation and human review. The video emphasizes the importance of maintaining authenticity and adhering to ethical practices, particularly in relation to intellectual property and synthetic media. The company is actively involved in industry organizations to ensure best practices are followed.

speaker: Qinying Liao, Ashley Bailey, Shinging
title: The AI Show: Ep 56 | Create a Custom Neural Voice "Lite" for Brands and Characters with Veritone
summary: The video discusses the importance of responsible use of technology, specifically in the context of custom neural voice technology. It introduces a new feature called Custom Neural Voice Lite, which allows users to record their voice with just five minutes of speech data. speaker: Pawan Taparia, Darren Jefford
title: Use the Efficiency of Low-Code with the Extensibility to Azure to Design World-Class Chatbots
summary: The video showcases how a digital assistant can be built using Power Virtual Agents. The assistant can provide information about required trainings and perform directory searches for employees within an organization. It also highlights the simplicity of adding new shapes and accessing external resources within the design surface.

speaker: Pawan Taparia, Darren Jefford
