speaker: Minsoo Thigpen
title: How to Explain Text Models with IntepretML Deep Dive
summary: Minsoo Thigpen, Program Manager on the Azure Machine Learning Responsible AI team, introduces Interpret-Text, a new offering from InterpretML that provides explainers for NLP machine learning models like BERT and RNNs. Interpret-Text supports BERT, RNNs, and standard scikit-learn models, allowing users to understand the key phrases and words that contribute to text classifications. The toolkit includes a visualization dashboard and aims to make recent research developments in interpretability more accessible to data scientists.

speaker: Minsoo Thigpen
title: How to Explain Text Models with IntepretML Deep Dive
summary: In this video, a toolkit is introduced that provides accessible implementations of three explainers for data scientists. The first is a classical text explainer that can be used with various models. The second is a unified information explainer that works with DNN models and provides explanations at each layer. The third is an introspective rationale explainer that makes black-box models more interpretable. These explainers offer different methods for understanding and interpreting text data.

speaker: Minsoo Thigpen
title: How to Explain Text Models with IntepretML Deep Dive
summary: The video introduces a plugin called the introspective generator, which makes black-box models more interpretable. It splits text into rationales and anti-rationales, training the model on both and maximizing accuracy with rationales while minimizing it with anti-rationales. This approach provides strong guarantees about which phrases matter to the prediction. The video also recommends using the classical text explainer for classical ML models in NLP and the introspective rationale explainer for understanding neural networks. Sample notebooks for both explainers are available in the repo.

title: Intelligent Edge - How 3 lines of code & Windows ML empower devs to run AI locally on Win 10 devices
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Rosane and Wilson discuss Windows ML, a new machine learning API that allows developers to run AI locally on Windows 10 devices. They highlight the benefits of Windows ML, such as enabling scenarios with strict performance requirements and addressing concerns around user data privacy. They also mention that Windows ML supports the standard format for machine learning, ONNX, and can run on a variety of Windows devices.

speaker: Rosane, Wilson
title: Intelligent Edge - How 3 lines of code & Windows ML empower devs to run AI locally on Win 10 devices
summary: Developers can now easily accelerate their evaluations on any GPU without worrying about specific drivers. If a GPU is not available, the system will automatically fall back to using the CPU. With Windows ML, developers can simply input an onyx model and run it locally, making it accessible and convenient. Models are essentially sets of instructions that help make decisions, and developers can now easily incorporate them into their programs.

speaker: Rosane, Wilson
title: Intelligent Edge - How 3 lines of code & Windows ML empower devs to run AI locally on Win 10 devices
summary: The video demonstrates how to generate wrapper classes automatically using Windows ML. By loading the model, binding the values, and evaluating the model, developers can easily use the generated classes without needing intimate knowledge of the model's inner workings. This simplifies the development process and allows developers to focus on architecture, user experience, and code scalability. The video also showcases the Windows Machine Learning Explorer app for testing and exploring Windows ML functionality.

speaker: Rosane, Wilson
title: Intelligent Edge - How 3 lines of code & Windows ML empower devs to run AI locally on Win 10 devices
summary: The Windows Machine Learning Explorer app allows users to test and evaluate multiple machine learning models. It can detect lung diseases from chest x-ray pictures in real-time, and can be executed on both CPU and GPU. The app also supports the ability to load multiple models and switch between them easily. Documentation and sample apps are available on the Microsoft website for those interested in getting started with Windows ML.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, a core developer of PyTorch, discusses the basics of PyTorch, including its unique features and strong community. PyTorch embraces the idea that machine learning is programming and provides a set of libraries in Python, making it easy to get started and integrate with other parts of the workflow. While PyTorch is primarily focused on deep learning, it is also used in other scientific fields.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch is a versatile library that caters to both the deep learning and scientific communities. It provides a tensor library for efficient computation across various devices, such as CPUs and GPUs. PyTorch offers modular and pluggable sub-libraries for tasks like automatic differentiation, building neural networks, optimization, data reading, and model deployment. It embraces the Python ecosystem, making it easy to integrate with existing workflows. Data preparation is a crucial aspect, with PyTorch providing tools to handle data efficiently.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: To get started with PyTorch, you can use the Torch Data Loader, which provides abstractions for handling typical tasks in your workflow. It allows you to efficiently read data sets, perform preprocessing tasks like data augmentation and image resizing, and produce mini-batches of data for training. PyTorch is flexible and customizable, allowing you to structure your workflow according to your specific needs, whether it's reading data from a local file or a proprietary database. The modularity and customizability of PyTorch make it suitable for both research and production settings.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the flexibility and freedom provided by PyTorch when it comes to data loading and model building. They explain how PyTorch allows users to easily customize data loading processes, including the ability to transform data and connect to cloud providers for large-scale datasets. They also highlight the modular approach of PyTorch for building models, where users can decompose building blocks and have control over each component. The speaker emphasizes the pluggability and adaptability of PyTorch's Autograd feature for automatic differentiation and gradient computation.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: Python's Autograd feature allows for flexible and pluggable tensor operations, making it ideal for research purposes. PyTorch provides a standard library of neural network layers, allowing for easy construction of regular neural networks. These layers can be thought of as modules with state and a forward function. The ability to use arbitrary control flow and compute derivatives of parameters enables the construction of a complete training loop for neural networks.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch is a popular choice for researchers due to its flexibility and ease of use. It allows users to construct models using a hierarchy of modules and easily optimize them using standard libraries. The computational graph in PyTorch makes it simple to express complex structures and customize the training regime. The library torch.nn provides standard layers for building models, and PyTorch allows users to freely use Python functions and constructs within their models. This flexibility and simplicity make PyTorch a powerful tool for advanced use cases.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: The video discusses the flexibility and modularity of PyTorch, a popular deep learning library. It highlights how users can create their own layers by subclassing existing modules, allowing for customization and optimization of any mathematical optimization problem. The video also mentions the support for higher-order gradients, enabling the computation of second partial derivatives and facilitating second-order optimization methods. Overall, PyTorch's modularity enhances the user experience and expands the possibilities in deep learning research and applications.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch focuses on bringing research to production by providing tools for packaging and deploying machine learning models. It offers a project management ecosystem called the third CRF, developed in collaboration with partners like Amazon and Microsoft, which allows easy packaging of models and attaching REST APIs for deployment. Additionally, PyTorch supports deployment on server-side in the cloud as well as on embedded devices like mobile.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch offers Torchscript, a component of its ecosystem, which allows for the deployment of models without the need for the Python interpreter. This enables models to be packaged and deployed on embedded devices or mobile phones. Additionally, PyTorch provides techniques for optimizing model performance, such as quantization, pruning, and low precision implementation. The platform supports a wide range of devices, including CPUs, GPUs, and mobile CPUs like ARM CPUs.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch is a popular developer platform for deep learning due to its technical merits and strong community support. It offers tools like ONNX export and integration points for efficient deployment on various devices. The friendly and responsive PyTorch forums contribute to its popularity, along with the extensive ecosystem of projects built on top of PyTorch. It is widely used in various domains, from computer vision to biology.

speaker: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, Seth
title: Get Started with PyTorch
summary: PyTorch is a powerful deep learning framework that has gained popularity due to its strong community support and ecosystem. It offers a wide range of tools and models for various domains, from computer vision to biology. The community-driven nature of PyTorch allows for the development of innovative projects and the sharing of ideas. Learning resources can be found on the PyTorch website, including tutorials and documentation. Additionally, forums and websites like LinkedIn can provide support and guidance for users. Development of PyTorch happens on GitHub, making it accessible for contributions.

speaker: Erika

speaker: Liam, Cassie
title: Igniting Developer Innovation with Vector Search
summary: Liam, a PM for Azure Cognitive Search, discusses the exciting possibilities of vectors in Azure Cognitive Search (preview) and Azure OpenAI Service functions. He explains how vectors enhance search capabilities, enabling more accurate and relevant "hybrid search" and advanced natural language understanding and generation. This revolutionizes information retrieval and takes language-based applications to the next level within the Azure ecosystem.

summary: The video discusses the use of vectors in AI applications, specifically in the context of Azure Cognitive Search and Azure Open AI. speaker: Liam, Cassie
title: Igniting Developer Innovation with Vector Search
summary: The video discusses the use of vector databases, specifically Azure Cognitive Search, to efficiently search and analyze large amounts of text data. By converting words into numbers and creating embeddings, the system can identify semantically similar content and improve search results. This technology has various applications, including in the legal field where finding relevant content with different variations of words can be challenging.

speaker: Liam, Cassie

summary: The video demonstrates how to use Azure Cognitive Search to create a search index for recipe data. The index includes a vector field that allows for semantic search. speaker: Liam, Cassie

speaker: Liam, Cassie

speaker: Seth, Swati Gharse

summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Swati Gharse, a Product Manager on the Azure Machine Learning Team, discusses how to build computer vision models using AutoML for Images. speaker: Seth, Swati Gharse

summary: AutoML in Azure Machine Learning allows data scientists to easily build computer vision models without writing training code. Users can optimize model training by controlling hyperparameters and choose from a variety of state-of-the-art algorithms. The models can be deployed as web services or used for local inferencing. AutoML also integrates seamlessly with other Azure ML capabilities, such as data labeling and MLOps for operationalizing models at scale.

speaker: Seth, Swati Gharse
title: AI Show Live | Building computer vision models using AutoML for Images | Episode 35
summary: The video discusses the use of AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) to easily tune hyperparameters for model building. The video provides a demo of how AutoML can be used to build an object detection model, showcasing the process of setting up the workspace, bringing in training data, and configuring AutoML to try different hyperparameters.

speaker: Seth, Swati Gharse
title: AI Show Live | Building computer vision models using AutoML for Images | Episode 35
summary: AutoML for images allows users to easily tune hyperparameters and try different algorithms in a single run. Users can specify ranges for learning rates and model sizes, as well as different learning rates and optimizers for different algorithms. The parameter space can be set up to try multiple algorithms and hyperparameters, with options for sampling and early termination. The AutoML run is executed on a cloud compute target, saving users time and effort.

speaker: Seth, Swati Gharse
title: AI Show Live | Building computer vision models using AutoML for Images | Episode 35
summary: AutoML for images is a powerful tool that automates the process of building computer vision models. With AutoML, users can try different models and hyperparameter values, saving time and compute resources. AutoML for images offers flexibility and control while boosting productivity for data scientists.

speaker: Rami J.

summary: Rami J., a Program Manager in Azure Machine Learning Services, discusses the new ML assisted data labeling capability in Azure ML Studio. speaker: Rami J.

speaker: Rami J.

summary: The video discusses a labeling tool that allows users to add labels to images with more nuance. Users have the option to relabel existing images or start over. speaker: Rami J.

speaker: Rami J.

summary: The video demonstrates how to use a workspace portal to label data for object detection. It explains how to create teams and invite labelers to assist with the labeling process. speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: Gopi Krishna Kumar, a program manager in the cloud AI team at Microsoft, introduces the Data Science Virtual Machine (DSVM) in this episode of the AI Show. DSVM is a pre-configured Azure Virtual Machine image that includes popular tools for data analytics, machine learning, and AI development. It allows data scientists to quickly set up their environment without the need for software installation and configuration. The DSVM is available on the Azure marketplace and offers full control and customization options for users.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: Managing the infrastructure and software for data analytics can be a tedious task for data scientists. However, a solution is available that takes away the hassle of setting up and maintaining the necessary tools. By providing prepackaged software and compatibility testing, this solution allows data scientists to focus on their core work while ensuring a reliable and efficient infrastructure for their projects. This eliminates the need for data scientists to also act as IT and infrastructure support, leading to increased productivity and consistent results.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: Running analytics in the cloud offers several benefits, including repeatable infrastructure, closer proximity to data, enhanced security, and scalability. It is particularly useful for educational and training purposes, allowing instructors to focus on content rather than infrastructure. Additionally, cloud-based virtual machines can provide powerful GPU capabilities for deep learning algorithms, eliminating the need for dedicated GPU hardware.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: The Data Science Virtual Machine (DSVM) and Deep Learning Virtual Machine (DLVM) are both available on Azure. The DSVM is a template that provides a range of tools for data science, while the DLVM is a focused template for running deep learning workloads on GPU-based hardware. Both templates offer the option of running on either Windows or Linux. The DSVM and DLVM allow users to quickly set up and start working on their code without spending time on infrastructure setup.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: The video showcases the different machine learning products offered by Azure, including Windows Server 2016, Ubuntu, Windows Server 2012, and CentOS. It highlights the convenience of spinning up a virtual machine (VM) with these tools and demonstrates the user interface of the data science tool menu. The video emphasizes that setting up these VMs is no different from setting up any other VM on Azure.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: The video showcases the various tools and features available in the Visual Studio for AI, including the ability to manage infrastructure and submit jobs to remote data science virtual machines. It also highlights the use of Jupyter notebooks for quick experimentation and provides an example of running a machine learning model using Microsoft R Server. The video emphasizes the convenience and efficiency of using Visual Studio for AI development.

speaker: Gopi Krishna Kumar
title: Data Science Virtual Machine
summary: The Windows Data Science Virtual Machine provides a pre-configured environment for data scientists and AI developers to quickly get started with their projects. It includes popular frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch, as well as tools like Jupyter Notebooks and Visual Studio Code. The virtual machine also allows for easy integration with Azure data services and machine learning capabilities. Users can scale their projects from single-node development to large-scale clusters. For more information, visit the product page, documentation, or reach out to the Data Science Virtual Machine team on forums or Stack Overflow.

speaker: Manoj
title: Azure Open Datasets: ML-Ready Open Data on Azure
summary: Manoj, from the AI platform team, discusses Azure Open Datasets, a platform for hosting open data on Azure. The datasets cover various domains such as weather, socioeconomic statistics, machine learning samples, and more. Manoj explains how to explore and use these datasets in Azure services like Azure Machine Learning. The data comes from sources like government institutions and is made accessible through Azure infrastructure and services. This episode of the AI Show provides valuable insights on leveraging free data for machine learning workflows.

speaker: Manoj
title: Azure Open Datasets: ML-Ready Open Data on Azure
summary: The video discusses a platform called Open Datasets on Azure, which provides easily accessible and pre-processed data for machine learning projects. The platform hosts large datasets, including public data and satellite imagery, and allows users to enrich their own data with these factors to improve model accuracy. By hosting the datasets on Azure, users can save storage and data transfer costs. The video emphasizes the importance of using this platform for augmenting data and making predictions.

speaker: Manoj
title: Azure Open Datasets: ML-Ready Open Data on Azure
summary: The video demonstrates how to access and use open datasets in Azure Machine Learning. It shows how to import weather data using the Azure ML Python package, as well as how to access the data using the Azure storage SDK in different programming languages. The video also highlights the ability to submit and augment datasets, and showcases the dataset hub in Azure Machine Learning workspace.

speaker: Boris Ganesh Golsky
title: What's New in the Cognitive Services Face API
summary: Boris Ganesh Golsky from the Azure Cognitive Services Face API team discusses the latest innovations in the Face API. The Face API provides algorithms for detecting, recognizing, and analyzing human faces in images. It offers capabilities such as face detection, verification, and identification. Developers can easily integrate these functionalities into their applications by creating a Face API Resource in the Azure portal and using the provided SDKs and samples. The team has made significant investments in infrastructure and performance improvements based on customer feedback.

speaker: Boris Ganesh Golsky
title: What's New in the Cognitive Services Face API
summary: The video discusses updates and improvements to the infrastructure and AI capabilities of the Cognitive Services Face API. On the infrastructure side, the Face API has expanded regional coverage, added Azure Active Directory support, VNET support, and customer managed keys for encryption. On the AI side, the Face API now offers side-by-side support for detection and recognition models, a new detection model for non-frontal and small faces, and a new facial recognition model with improved accuracy. These updates give customers more control and enhance the security and functionality of the Face API.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Vinitra Swamy from the ONNX engineering team at Microsoft introduces the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) and ONNX Runtime. ONNX is a format for representing deep learning models that allows for easy translation between different frameworks. The benefit of using ONNX is that it enables graph optimizations and allows for the use of different runtime inference frameworks. The episode also includes a demo on converting a CoreML model to ONNX and a case study on ONNX Runtime accelerating Bing Semantic Precise Image Search.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: Converting models to the ONNX format is made easy with the use of converters in popular frameworks like PyTorch, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and Keras. The process involves simple conversion commands that convert the model into the ONNX format. For those who already have ONNX and want to experiment with conversion, an ONNX ecosystem Docker file is available, which includes all the necessary converters, frameworks, and the ONNX runtime. This Docker file allows for easy setup and experimentation with ONNX.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: The video discusses the ONNX Runtime, an open-source scoring engine for ONNX models. It is compatible with the most recent release of ONNX and offers high performance, often outperforming native runtimes. The ONNX Runtime is cross-platform and can be easily installed. The video also explains the difference between ONNX versions and operator sets, which are continually updated to include new functionalities contributed by industry partners.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: The Bing multimedia team has leveraged ONNX Runtime to improve image search. They faced the challenge of searching for images that are difficult to describe with words, such as pencil erasers that look like tools. By mapping these images to the same semantic embedding space as words, they were able to improve the accuracy of image search results. ONNX Runtime, included on every Windows machine, allows for faster model execution by leveraging speedups from execution providers like Intel's MKL-DNN and NVIDIA's TensorRT.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: The Bing multimedia team has developed Semantic Precise Image Search, a solution that allows images to be represented in the same vector space as queries. By embedding images into this space, Bing can accurately match images to user queries based on semantic similarities. To speed up the process, the team used ONNX Runtime, converting the model to the ONNX format and achieving a 50% reduction in latency on CPUs using Intel's MKL-DNN as an execution provider. This optimization has greatly enhanced Bing's image search capabilities.

speaker: Vinitra Swamy
title: ONNX Runtime speeds up Image Embedding model in Bing Semantic Precise Image Search
summary: Bing has improved its search capabilities by using two models simultaneously: one for saving images in the latent space and another for comparing queries with images in the latent space. This has resulted in a two times speedup and has been made possible by ONNX Runtime, which allows the deployment of pre-trained ONNX models for inference. Azure Machine Learning is a great platform to explore and deploy these models, and the ONNX Model Zoo provides a collection of state-of-the-art models for immediate use.

speaker: Noelle LaCharite
title: What’s New? A Single Key for Cognitive Services #TWiCognitive
summary: Noelle LaCharite discusses the simplification of using Cognitive Services in applications. Instead of managing multiple keys per service, there is now a single key that combines vision, language, and search services. This eliminates the need for copying and pasting multiple keys and streamlines the process. The single key can be created in the Azure Portal and provides access to various pre-built machine learning models.

speaker: Jacqueline Maureen

speaker: Jacqueline Maureen
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 2
summary: The video discusses the importance of evaluating model performance for different subgroups of data in responsible AI. It introduces a metrics visualization tool that allows users to compare performance metrics across dataset cohorts, helping to identify potential biases or unintended harms. The video also showcases a data explorer component that provides different views of the data, such as image explorer, table view, and class view, to further analyze and diagnose model discrepancies. Additionally, the video highlights the ability to access visual explanations for object detection models to debug and identify biases.

speaker: Jacqueline Maureen
title: Responsible AI Support for Image and Text Models | Part 2
summary: The video discusses the use of object detection models in the Responsible AI Support for Images and Text Models Part 2. The video also addresses potential biases in the model's predictions and suggests ways to mitigate them. The dashboard supports both AutoML and non-AutoML models, and the process for setting it up is similar to the text dashboard. Further information can be found in the technical documentation and blog provided.

speaker: Greg, Jim, Seth

The image API allows users to evaluate, find faces, and perform OCR on images, while the text API helps identify offensive or inappropriate content. They emphasize the importance of using human reviewers to ensure compliance with platform policies.

speaker: Greg, Jim, Seth

The evaluate feature allows users to submit images for review to ensure they comply with platform policies. The find faces feature is useful for businesses that want to detect and filter out images with faces, such as hotel booking platforms that want to avoid displaying personal information. The video provides examples of how to use these features and showcases their effectiveness.

speaker: Greg, Jim, Seth
title: Image and Text Moderation with Content Moderator
summary: The video discusses the capabilities of an API for image recognition and content moderation. It covers features such as face detection, image matching, and optical character recognition (OCR). The API can be used for various purposes, including blurring faces, detecting similar images, and filtering out inappropriate content. It also offers enhanced OCR capabilities to detect fraudulent activities.

speaker: Greg, Jim, Seth
title: Image and Text Moderation with Content Moderator

Greg also emphasizes the importance of human review in content moderation and showcases the profanity matching capability. Overall, OCR is a powerful tool that can be easily implemented with just a few API calls.

speaker: Shivani Patel

She shows how to automate the model training and deployment process using machine learning pipelines and GitHub Actions. The video provides a step-by-step walkthrough of the process, including how to trigger the pipeline and track the progress using GitHub Actions and Azure Machine Learning.

speaker: Shivani Patel
title: MLOps feature dive: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
summary: The video discusses the process of continuous integration (CI) in machine learning pipelines. It explains how code is run, files are updated, and models are registered. The importance of referencing the specific code and files used for scoring is emphasized.

speaker: Shivani Patel

speaker: Faith Xu
title: ONNX Runtime
summary: Faith Xu, a Program Manager at Microsoft, introduces ONNX Runtime, an open-source scoring engine for traditional and deep machine learning models. Microsoft is using ONNX Runtime to improve prediction latency and efficiency in various scenarios. The community of ONNX supporters is continuously growing, and contributions are encouraged.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: Christopher Whitten, Principal Software Engineer, introduces the Bot Framework Composer, a collaborative conversational AI development environment. The Composer provides developers and teams with a visual dialog editor, tools for language understanding and generation, and a bot runtime executable. It integrates with the Bot Framework SDK and allows for modeling dialogs, input recognition, and response generation. The session explores the features of the Composer and demonstrates its capabilities in creating sophisticated conversational applications.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: The video discusses the use of adaptive dialogs in Microsoft's Bot Framework Composer. It covers topics such as flow decomposition, dialog composition, and integration with Bot Framework Skills. The video also demonstrates the deployment of a Rolodex bot to the Azure Bot Service. The Composer's flow editor allows for visual layout of conversation nodes, while the form editor configures nodes based on the Bot Framework SDK interfaces. Triggers and Recognizers are used to produce flow based on events and define language understanding models for dialogs.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: The video demonstrates how to update content in a bot using the LG Syntax and syntax highlighting in the Composer design page. It shows how to start the bot, connect to the Bot Framework Emulator, and have conversations with the bot. The video also covers adding functionality to the bot using the adaptive dialog in the Bot Framework SDK, including adding a greeting and assigning a recognizer. It concludes with creating actions to collect information from the user.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: The video demonstrates the use of regular expression and LUIS (Language Understanding Intelligent Service) recognizers in a bot. Regular expression recognizer allows for pattern matching and extracting information from user input, while LUIS provides machine learning capabilities to understand user intent and extract entities. The video also shows how to publish the bot to LUIS for testing and validation.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Bot Framework Composer to create reusable dialogs and integrate Bot Framework Skills. Composer allows you to encapsulate bot logic into dialogs that can be invoked anywhere within your bot, promoting encapsulation and reuse. It also provides features to discover and manage skill endpoints, as well as call skills within your dialogs. Additionally, Composer allows you to generate a skill manifest for your own bot, making it available as a skill.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: The video demonstrates how to integrate a HelpDesk skill into a bot using Bot Framework Composer. By calling the skill dialog and forwarding the user's activity, the bot can interact with the skill seamlessly. The video also briefly discusses the Publish Profiles page in Composer, which allows for provisioning, deployment, and publishing of bots to various platforms, including Azure web apps.

speaker: Christopher Whitten, Chris
title: Bot Framework Composer: Bot Framework’s new collaborative Conversational AI development environment
summary: In this video, the presenter demonstrates how to create a new publishing profile in a Composer built bot using Azure Bot Service. They provision a web application and copy the resulting JSON payload to edit the existing publishing profile. After making changes and redeploying, they publish to the selected profile and test the bot. The video concludes with links to download Composer and access the Rolodex bot.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: Liam Cavanagh, Principal Program Manager on the Azure Cognitive Search team, demonstrates how AI can be used to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19. By applying machine learning techniques such as named entity recognition, semantic word similarity, contextual summarization, and knowledge graphs, first responders and medical professionals can better find and understand relevant research. The session provides an overview of the techniques used and includes code samples for developers interested in building a similar solution using Cognitive Search.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: Azure Cognitive Search is used to power a search experience that utilizes various technologies to enhance the search results. Open data sets from Semantic Scholar are used as a source of information, which is then enriched using Microsoft's TA for health technology to extract important medical entities. AI capabilities are used to provide semantic search and contextual summarization. Knowledge graphs are also utilized to visualize correlations between different entities. The application is continually updated based on new information and requirements.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: The video showcases how Azure Cognitive Search is used to enhance search capabilities for medical research. By leveraging AI technology, the search engine suggests relevant terms and prioritizes recent articles to provide up-to-date information. Additionally, the system utilizes semantic analysis to identify similar terms and variations, improving the accuracy and efficiency of search results. The integration of dates allows users to filter for the most relevant information.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: The video showcases a demonstration of a search application powered by AI capabilities and Cognitive Search. The application allows users to filter and search for relevant information using facets, dates, and visual graphs. The video also briefly explains the technical aspects of data preparation and ingestion using Azure Cognitive Search and Azure Blob storage.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: Azure Cognitive Search is used to parse and store content from various sources, such as PDFs and office documents. Custom skills are used to extract medical entities and refine the search index. A Data Science VM is used to analyze the content and create semantically similar terms. Multiple versions of the search index are created to enhance and support different requirements. Azure Cognitive Search provides title, abstract, and body information for search queries.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: The video showcases the setup of a search index using Semantic Scholar. It demonstrates how custom skills can be used to enrich and modify data within the index. The video also highlights the use of the Semantic Server to find semantically similar terms based on a search query. Overall, the video provides insights into the capabilities of cognitive search and its application in the medical field.

speaker: Liam Cavanagh
title: Using AI to mine unstructured research papers to fight COVID-19
summary: The video showcases the use of Azure Cognitive Search and custom skills to build a medical search application. It demonstrates how data is ingested and prepared using cognitive search, and how the search application is built using Azure App Service. The video also highlights the importance of user feedback and how it can be used to enhance the search index. The video provides links to access the online application, GitHub repo, and other relevant resources for further exploration.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: Sanjeev Jagtap, PM for Cognitive Services, discusses the use cases for using AI to moderate content. He highlights user-created assets, social sharing, conversational scenarios, and augmented reality as areas where content moderation is necessary. With the increasing scale of content creation, it is important to filter out potentially illegal and inappropriate content using tools like Content Moderator.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: Content moderation is a complex challenge due to factors such as geopolitical sensitivities, cultural nuances, evolving demographics, and the ever-changing nature of online content. The presence of bad actors posting illegal and offensive content poses a significant risk to brands and users, regardless of company size or application type. Traditional human moderation struggles to keep up, and implementing AI solutions requires substantial investment. Businesses must find scalable and effective approaches to address this problem and maximize their potential.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: As businesses grow and markets change, content moderation becomes a challenge. While there are technologies and products available, integrating them seamlessly and customizing them to fit specific needs can be difficult. Out-of-the-box AI models may not fully address the unique characteristics of the content. A good content moderation solution should be simple to understand and acquire, easy to integrate, customizable, and should augment human moderators rather than replacing them. Microsoft's Content Moderator platform offers REST APIs to scan for illegal and inappropriate content in images, text, and videos.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: Microsoft has developed technology called C Sam, which stands for child sexual abuse material, to scan for illegal, inappropriate, offensive, and explicit content in images, text, and videos. This technology can be easily integrated into applications, allowing companies worldwide to detect and moderate such content. The Review API acts as a bridge between the scanning models and human moderators, providing a seamless approach for content review. Microsoft believes that a combination of machine and human moderation yields the best results.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video demonstrates the use of an image and text moderation API. The API allows users to scan images and text for offensive or explicit content. The output is provided in JSON or text format, containing labels, scores, and other insights. The video includes a simple demo of the API in action, showcasing the moderation of images and text. The API can be easily integrated into applications for content moderation purposes.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video demonstrates a text moderation demo using an API. The output includes autocorrected text, potential personally identifiable information (PII) such as email addresses and phone numbers, and text classification based on explicitness, suggestiveness, and offensiveness. The demo also discusses the use of a default database for flagging terms across multiple languages and the need for human moderators to review borderline cases. The code for the demo is simple, involving API calls for text classification, PII detection, and autocorrection.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: Human moderation is an essential part of online safety. Whether using existing systems or homegrown tools, human moderators play a crucial role in reviewing and evaluating content. The review API offers an integrated solution, allowing customers to scan content, apply content policies, and create reviews or take other actions. The review tool, included in the content moderator subscription, provides a user-friendly interface for managing workflows and reviewing content.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the Content Moderator API to create a workflow for reviewing and flagging potentially inappropriate images. The workflow involves connecting to the Content Moderator, creating a review for each image, and highlighting the ones that are deemed racy. The video shows how to run the workflow and view the created reviews. It also explains how to modify the workflow to change the conditions for flagging images.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video demonstrates how to customize the workflow and policies of an image moderation system. By modifying the code, different results can be obtained, such as creating reviews only for images with a certain tag. The video also explains how to use the review operation to create reviews without moderating the images. Additionally, the video introduces the feature for custom image scanning, which allows users to upload their own custom images and match them against the moderation system's results.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video demonstrates how to use a list management API for images and text to upload custom content and match it with existing data. The workflow involves creating reviews based on matching criteria and highlighting matched items. The video showcases the process using code examples and explains the results obtained from custom image and text matching.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video discusses how custom matching for terms and lists can be combined with existing tools to enhance content moderation. It also explores the possibility of using the review tool in conjunction with other cognitive APIs and services, such as the custom vision service. This allows for the scanning and review of content using custom vision classifiers, with the ability to make human decisions and even initiate a training process based on those decisions.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the process of creating a custom classifier to detect soft toys from images using a toy marketplace as an example. They demonstrate how to call the custom vision service and extract the tags for the soft toys. The speaker also mentions the video moderation feature available, but does not provide a demo. Overall, the video showcases how multiple services can be combined for the review process.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: Video moderation is available as part of the review tool offered by the AI assistant. Users can try out image, text, and video moderation without writing any code. The video review experience includes options to view the video player or keyframes, along with a transcript synced with the video. The tool supports labeling at both the video and individual frame levels. To integrate video moderation, users can refer to the provided documentation and sample source code on GitHub.

speaker: Sanjeev Jagtap
title: Amplify Your Content Insights Across AI by filtering with Content Moderator
summary: The video provides a complete code sample on GitHub for moderating videos and creating video reviews using the .NET SDK of Content Moderator. It also mentions that the fastest way to get started with Content Moderator is through Flow, which offers pre-built templates. The video emphasizes the importance of content moderation for various scenarios and mentions that Content Moderator currently supports English only, but plans to support more languages in the future.

speaker: Abe Omorogbe
title: Scaling your AI/ML practices with MLOps and Azure Machine Learning | Part 1
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Abe Omorogbe discusses MLOps and how to leverage Azure Machine Learning capabilities to streamline the process of moving ML experiments from training to inference. He explains the importance of the MLOps process and introduces the three main pillars of MLOps: people, process, and platform. By implementing MLOps, organizations can achieve increased automation, collaboration, and reproducibility, resulting in faster and more secure ML model deployments.

speaker: Abe Omorogbe
title: Scaling your AI/ML practices with MLOps and Azure Machine Learning | Part 1
summary: ML Ops is a process that aims to increase automation, collaboration, and reproducibility in machine learning projects. It focuses on faster production and secure deployment, with a strong emphasis on auditability. While tools and platforms have improved, the success of ML Ops still relies on people buying into the process and following good practices. The ML Ops process differs from traditional DevOps, with three main pillars: prototyping, training, and operationalization. Monitoring and managing the deployed models are also crucial aspects of ML Ops.

speaker: Abe Omorogbe
title: Scaling your AI/ML practices with MLOps and Azure Machine Learning | Part 1
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the operationalization and deployment of machine learning models in a production environment. They emphasize the importance of monitoring and managing the model to ensure data security and performance. The speaker also highlights the iterative nature of the machine learning lifecycle and the need for retraining and adaptation over time. They provide a sneak peek of the upcoming parts, which will focus on scaling ML practices and provide resources for learning more about ML Ops.

speaker: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, Ashish Bhatia
title: AI Builder | A World of AI at Your Fingertips
summary: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, and Ashish Bhatia discuss AI Builder, a low-code, no-code solution for AI. They explain how AI has transformed data processing, making tasks easier and more automated. They demonstrate how AI Builder works and its applications in intelligent document processing. The video also discusses the growing trend of low-code and no-code development and how AI Builder fits into the Power Platform ecosystem.

speaker: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, Ashish Bhatia
title: AI Builder | A World of AI at Your Fingertips
summary: Microsoft offers a range of low-code and no-code tools for business analytics, application development, website development, workflow automation, and chatbot development. These tools are built on a common fabric called Dataverse, with a low-code programming language called PowerFX. AI Builder is a part of the Power Platform and is gradually being integrated into all of these tools. It provides a no-code approach to AI development, while Azure Machine Learning and Azure AI Services are more suitable for pro data scientists and developers who require more control and customization.

speaker: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, Ashish Bhatia
title: AI Builder | A World of AI at Your Fingertips
summary: The video showcases the AI Builder in action, demonstrating how it can be used to create a simple power app that extracts key information from a receipt and automatically generates an expense report. The AI Builder utilizes pre-built AI models and allows for fine-tuning, providing admins with model governance and control. The demo highlights the speed and accuracy of the AI Builder in identifying and populating relevant fields from the receipt.

speaker: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, Ashish Bhatia
title: AI Builder | A World of AI at Your Fingertips
summary: The video showcases a pre-built AI model that can extract information from scanned images of receipts. The model is integrated into a form that submits the extracted data to a SharePoint list. Another demo demonstrates a custom machine learning model that extracts information from uploaded invoices and triggers an automated workflow for approval. Both examples highlight the capabilities of AI in processing expense reports and improving efficiency.

speaker: Rob Nunez, Albert Dankwa, Ashish Bhatia
title: AI Builder | A World of AI at Your Fingertips
summary: Microsoft has developed a drawing bot that uses a technology called Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate images from text descriptions. The GAN consists of two machine learning models, one that generates images and another that judges the authenticity of the generated images. The models work together, with the generator trying to fool the discriminator. The drawing bot can create new and novel pictures of birds based on textual descriptions, using an attentional model to map words to specific regions in the images.

speaker: Chen
title: Bring Anomaly Detector on-premise with containers support
summary: Chen from the AI platform team introduces the Anomaly Detector, a hosted API service on the cloud. However, there are challenges with running it as a service, such as data latency and the need to keep data on-premises for regulatory compliance. To address these challenges, the Anomaly Detector is now available as a containerized service, allowing users to deploy the API service close to their data. This enables the reuse of the same application across both the cloud and on-premises environments.

speaker: Chen
title: Bring Anomaly Detector on-premise with containers support
summary: Microsoft has introduced Anomaly Detector containers, which allow users to run the Anomaly Detector service without the need for a connection to the cloud. The containers can be run on various infrastructures, including Azure Stack, Kubernetes, and even on personal laptops. The containers offer the same functionality as the cloud-based service and provide a consistent code running experience. Users can create an Anomaly Detector resource on the cloud to get started with using the containers.

speaker: Chen
title: Bring Anomaly Detector on-premise with containers support
summary: To create an Anomaly Detector resource on the Cloud, you need to obtain an API key and API endpoint. The API key is used for container usage and the endpoint is where billing telemetry is sent. The container image is currently hosted in a private Azure Container Registry, and you can apply for credentials to access it. Once you have the credentials, you can run the container locally using the key and endpoint. It functions the same way as the cloud service, with the endpoint changed to localhost.

speaker: Chen
title: Bring Anomaly Detector on-premise with containers support
summary: In this video, the speaker explains how to use Docker login and pull images from the Azure Container Registry. They demonstrate the standard Docker commands required and highlight the three unique parameters needed to run the container images. They also discuss the billing endpoint and the importance of specifying the key. The video concludes with information on where to find more resources and documentation on Anomaly detector.

speaker: Seth Juarez, PSI
title: Simplifying Machine Learning with Automated ML
summary: In this episode of the AI Show, Seth Juarez, a Program Manager in the Azure Machine Learning Team, discusses automated machine learning (ML). Automated ML simplifies the ML workflow by automating tasks such as data cleansing, feature engineering, algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and deployment. It democratizes machine learning, allowing business domain experts to leverage ML without coding and optimizing data scientists' work. The video also demonstrates how to start an automated ML experiment, analyze experiment outputs, and deploy a recommended model.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: Paul DeCarlo and Alvin Clark discuss the partnership between Microsoft and NVIDIA in developing NVIDIA DeepStream with Microsoft Azure. This collaboration aims to guide developers in creating Intelligent Video Applications (IVAs) using optimized audio and computer vision AI models. The DeepStream Graph Composer development environment allows developers to build cross-platform container workloads that can be deployed to server or edge hardware. The video provides an overview of NVIDIA DeepStream SDK and showcases a demo of the DeepStream Graph Composer.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: The video discusses the importance of utilizing hardware acceleration, specifically GPUs, for efficient video processing. It emphasizes the need to offload tasks such as decoding, scaling, and color space conversion to the GPU to optimize performance. DeepStream is highlighted as a solution that ensures efficient processing of AI inference models and video analytics, minimizing latency and maximizing throughput. The video also mentions the versatility of DeepStream, allowing the same application to run on different hardware platforms without the need for recoding.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: The video discusses the use of the NVIDIA DeepStream SDK for building video processing pipelines. The SDK provides hardware-accelerated deep stream plug-ins that can be used in both Python and C++. The latest version, DeepStream 6.0, introduces a visual programming method called Graph Composer, allowing users to visually create and customize video pipelines. The pipelines can be deployed using container builder and can be sent to various platforms, including the cloud.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the NVIDIA DeepStream Graph Composer IDE to build an application for object detection. The IDE comes with a collection of extensions containing components that can be dragged and dropped onto the canvas. The video shows how to connect video inputs, apply an object detection algorithm, draw bounding boxes, and render the results. The IDE allows for quick iterations and modifications to the pipeline.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: The video demonstrates how the NVIDIA DeepStream Graph Composer makes it easy to modify pipelines and add new features. It showcases the NVDS Msg Conv Broker, which allows connection to an MQTT input/output channel and compatibility with Azure IoT Edge. The video also highlights the Container Builder feature for building containers that can run on different platforms. An interactive learning path on Microsoft Learn is available for further guidance.

speaker: Paul DeCarlo, Alvin Clark
title: The AI Show: Ep 51 | NVIDIA DeepStream development with Microsoft Azure
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses the capabilities of Graph Composer, a visual programming tool for building vision applications using NVIDIA DeepStream and Microsoft Azure. The tool allows users to easily incorporate custom GStreamer or DeepStream extensions, as well as third-party plugins, into their applications. The speaker also highlights the learning path created by Paul, which covers setting up the development environment, using Composer, containerization options, and deploying workloads to embedded devices using Azure IoT Edge. The speaker emphasizes that Graph Composer is not just for hobbyists, but can be used to build market-ready products with optimized performance.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: Kelly Freed, a PM on the Azure Cognitive Services team, discusses the latest technologies in Computer Vision. She explains how vision services make it easy to process images and extract insights from them. The major update is the availability of face detection and recognize text services in containers, providing flexibility and control for customers. Containers allow for easy deployment and testing of vision services in various environments.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: Containers offer a stable and repeatable software process for deploying and managing applications. They are particularly useful for running applications on premises or at the edge, where sensitive data needs to stay local. Running containers locally can also improve speed and performance, especially in environments with limited or unreliable connectivity. The services provided by containers are the same as those in the cloud, allowing for seamless integration and code reuse.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video explains how to deploy a cloud service locally using containers. By using the same code and API key, users can deploy the service on their own network and still receive usage data. The service offers a grace period for spotty Wi-Fi connections, and the free tier still applies to the locally deployed containers. To get started, users need to sign up for access, pull the service from the private ACR, and accept the EULA before running it with the API key.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: To deploy a container locally for face recognition, you can use the same keys as the online version. The only difference is specifying the billing endpoint. By copying the endpoint from the key overview and adding it to the docker run command, you can easily run the container locally. Testing locally is made simple by accessing localhost and checking for any errors. The calls made locally are the same as those made in the cloud, providing the same information in the same format.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses two services: Face and Recognized Text from Computer Vision. Recognized Text allows users to read text in images, even in challenging conditions such as shadows or similar background colors. It can be used for document understanding or real-time text recognition on the edge. Face, on the other hand, enables businesses to identify and analyze faces in various scenarios. Both services offer specific functionalities to empower businesses and enhance understanding of text and faces.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses the use of the face service in understanding customer demographics and sentiment. It highlights the ability to run real-time analysis on multiple cameras in various locations. The decision to focus on face and vision services was based on customer feedback, and the ease of use and empowerment of new scenarios with containers is emphasized. Other vision scenarios mentioned include video indexer and computer vision.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: Video Indexer is a powerful tool that provides detailed information about the content of videos. It uses computer vision to recognize text, objects, faces, and even custom images. It can determine if an image is real or a drawing, recognize celebrities and landmarks, and even caption images in multiple languages. With its capabilities, businesses can analyze images for marketing campaigns, brand recognition, and accessibility purposes. Video Indexer is user-friendly and can be easily accessed on its website.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video demonstrates how to use Microsoft's Cognitive Services, specifically focusing on Computer Vision and Custom Vision. Computer Vision allows users to analyze images and receive JSON data about them. Custom Vision allows users to customize and extend pre-trained models, and even export them for local use. The video also briefly mentions other features such as object detection. Overall, the video showcases the ease of use and flexibility of Microsoft's Cognitive Services for AI applications.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: To use object detection and classification in video, you can upload and tag images to train the model. The training process takes about two minutes and provides a performance analysis with precision and recall numbers. Adding more diverse images improves the model's accuracy. Object detection not only identifies what's in the image but also where it is located. Microsoft has even trained a specific domain for logo detection, achieving high precision.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses the use of custom vision in logo recognition and image tagging. It explains that the functionality can be accessed through API calls, allowing for automation of image upload and tagging. The video also addresses the question of how many images are needed for the system to work effectively, recommending 20 to 50 images per category. It emphasizes the importance of training the computer with sufficient data for accurate recognition. The video concludes by assuring viewers that the underlying technology is based on pre-trained models and sensible algorithms.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: In this video, the speaker explains how AI models are trained using pre-existing data and then fine-tuned with specific user data through transfer learning. The speaker emphasizes the importance of training models on relevant domains to achieve better accuracy. They also discuss the challenges of training models on a general domain versus a specific domain, using the example of logo detection.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: Containers have become significant in customer demand due to their ability to run applications locally and improve network response time. Early access to containers has received positive reception from customers, who are eager for public preview. Object detection can be used to count objects in an image, but accuracy may vary depending on the scenario and potential overlapping. For scenarios with neatly arranged objects, like on an assembly line, object counting can work effectively. However, for scenarios with overlapping or irregularly arranged objects, accuracy may be compromised.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses the use of custom vision models for non-coders, highlighting its user-friendly interface and quick setup process. It also mentions the inability to create custom domains due to the need for a large amount of data. The video introduces Azure machine learning services and video indexer, which can detect various elements in videos such as faces, words, and objects. Video indexer also allows for the identification and tagging of individuals throughout multiple videos.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video demonstrates how to use the Cognitive Services Video Indexer to analyze and extract insights from videos. It shows how the tool can identify keywords, sentiment, and translate the transcript into multiple languages. The speaker explains that the service is easy to use, requiring no technical expertise, and is priced based on the amount of video processed. The video also briefly mentions other scenarios that can be addressed using Computer Vision.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses computer vision and text recognition capabilities of the computer vision API. It can provide descriptions of images in multiple languages and identify celebrities in photos. The API can also read text from various fonts, shapes, and backgrounds, including handwritten text. It is not limited to English and can recognize text in different languages. The video also mentions the option to test images on the website without using the SDK.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: The video discusses the use of OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology in recognizing English characters in images. While the new OCR version performs well on blurry and hard-to-read images, it is specific to English characters. However, it can also be used with other Latin character-based languages with some room for errors on accents. The previous OCR version, which is more focused on document scanning, can work in multiple languages. The video also highlights the potential of cognitive services like video indexer in reducing costs and improving efficiency in businesses by automating tasks such as labeling and text extraction. Additionally, the newly introduced logo detection feature allows businesses to analyze their market presence by identifying when and where their logos appear in videos.

speaker: Kelly Freed
title: Computer Vision Made Easy!
summary: Containers for face recognition and OCR are separate to allow for efficient and edge computing. The size of the containers is not large, but the recommended system requirements are a two-core CPU with 8GB of memory for base recognition. GPU, FPGA, and ARM optimization are not currently supported, but the team is actively working on adding new language support. General availability is not yet determined, but signups are being reviewed.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: Cesar De la Torre Llorente discusses the new features in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML. He highlights the "white box" approach of AutoML, which allows users to access the training code of the models generated by Automated ML. This feature provides transparency, reproducibility, and control for users who require it. The code generation capability is available in the Azure Machine Learning Python SDK v2 and CLI v2.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: AutoML now provides the training code for the models it generates, allowing users to see and modify the code if desired. This feature is useful for understanding the inner workings of the model and making adjustments to settings such as feature risers and model hyperparameters. The training code includes the algorithm used, data featurization, and the training process. Code generation can be enabled or disabled when creating an AutoML experiment.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: The video showcases different models trained with AutoML, with a focus on the XGBoostClassifier model. It demonstrates how to access the training code for the model and provides a convenient notebook and a Python file for running the code. The video also highlights the data loading and preparation steps, as well as the use of hyperparameters for the model. The code includes a pipeline for featurization, preprocessing, and model training.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: The video showcases a circular pipeline for featurization, preprocessing, and model training using automated machine learning. The code for the notebook and model featurization is provided, making it easy to run and customize. The video also highlights the new features in version 2 of the development platform, including a CLI for AutoML and support for YAML files, enabling easy triggering of training runs for MLOps operations. Python SDK and DOD support are also available.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: The video showcases the improvements made in version 2 of AutoML in Azure Machine Learning. The code has been simplified, making it cleaner and easier to use. The video demonstrates how to use the command-line interface (CLI) to run an automated machine learning job by providing instructions in a YAML file. It also highlights the flexibility of running the job either through the CLI or the Python SDK.

speaker: Cesar De la Torre Llorente, Seth
title: Build Recap | What’s new in Azure Machine Learning Automated ML
summary: Azure Machine Learning has introduced several new features, including AutoML for different tasks such as classification, regression, computer vision, and NLP. The updates also include CodeGen, a new CLI with YAML descriptions and autocomplete in Visual Studio code, and a simplified SDK with factory methods and setters. These enhancements make it easier to configure and launch machine learning jobs. AutoML for images and improvements in forecasting and parakeets are also in preview.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Using custom adapters to surface your bot anywhere (Part 3 of 3)
summary: Gary Pretty, a Senior Engineer on the Bot Framework SDK team, explains how to extend the options available within Azure Bot Service by using custom adapters. These adapters allow you to build bots for platforms like WeChat, Alexa, Google Assistant, Twitter, and more. Gary demonstrates how to hook up a custom adapter to a bot and get started with Microsoft Docs and Bot Builder Community.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Using custom adapters to surface your bot anywhere (Part 3 of 3)
summary: The video discusses the use of adapters in building bots with the Microsoft Bot Framework. Adapters are responsible for transforming messages between the bot framework and different channels. If a desired channel is not available on Azure Bot Service, custom adapters can be built using the SDK or community-contributed adapters can be used. The process of implementing adapters is straightforward and involves installing the necessary NuGet package and adding an additional controller for the specific channel.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Using custom adapters to surface your bot anywhere (Part 3 of 3)
summary: Alexa can be easily integrated with existing bots using the Alexa adapter and error handling class. By creating an Alexa Skill and pointing it to the fulfillment URL, requests from Alexa are transformed into a format understood by the bot. The bot's responses are then transformed back into an Alexa-compatible format. This allows for multi-tenant conversations with Alexa and potential integration with other home assistants. Microsoft Docs provide guides for connecting adapters, and the Bot Builder community offers extensions for the Bot Framework.

speaker: Gary Pretty
title: Bot Framework – Using custom adapters to surface your bot anywhere (Part 3 of 3)
summary: In this video, the speaker discusses adapters in the context of building bots using the Microsoft Bot Framework. Adapters are used to handle the transformation of incoming requests from different platforms or channels, such as Teams, Alexa, or Google. The speaker explains that by using adapters, developers can build a single application that can send and receive messages across multiple platforms, while also taking advantage of platform-specific features. The video provides an overview of how adapters route and translate messages, allowing developers to tailor their conversations for different channels.

speaker: Dr. Katja Hofmann, Seth
title: New reinforcement learning methods aim to improve AI in gaming and beyond
summary: Dr. Katja Hofmann discusses reinforcement learning, an AI approach that trains game characters to behave naturally and react to human players. She explains key concepts of reinforcement learning in the context of Project Malmo, which uses Minecraft as a platform for AI research, and Project Paidia, which focuses on creating game agents that genuinely collaborate with human players. The episode also includes a demo of Project Paidia and provides resources for further learning.

speaker: Dr. Katja Hofmann, Seth
title: New reinforcement learning methods aim to improve AI in gaming and beyond
summary: Researchers are using reinforcement learning techniques to train AI agents in games like Minecraft and Bleeding Edge to solve complex problems and collaborate with human players. The goal is to create agents that can learn about their environment and take a sequence of actions to achieve their objectives. Project Paidia, a collaboration with Ninja Theory, focuses on creating AI agents that can genuinely collaborate with human players in team-based games.

speaker: Dr. Katja Hofmann, Seth
title: New reinforcement learning methods aim to improve AI in gaming and beyond
summary: In a collaboration with game developer Ninja Theory, Microsoft Research has developed AI agents that can effectively collaborate with human players in the game Bleeding Edge. Unlike in Minecraft, where AI agents require a reward function, the agents in Bleeding Edge can learn from human players and make strategic decisions based on their teammates' abilities. The project also explores the use of demonstration data to imitate human players and improve agent performance. Microsoft has released an interactive experience on their AI Innovation page to showcase the trained reinforcement learning agent.

speaker: Dr. Katja Hofmann, Seth
title: New reinforcement learning methods aim to improve AI in gaming and beyond
summary: In this interactive experience, a trained reinforcement learning agent collaborates with a human player in an escape room game. The agent understands the player's behavior and adapts its actions accordingly. Viewers are encouraged to try the interactive experience and learn more about reinforcement learning and its applications in video games. Links are provided to access the AI innovation page and an Azure resource for training reinforcement learning agents.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
summary: Mike Carter, Principal Program Manager on the Azure Cognitive Search team, discusses the latest security improvements in Azure Cognitive Search. He highlights the importance of security for enterprise and government customers and explains how Azure Cognitive Search meets their strict security requirements. Carter covers three main areas of security: data at rest, inbound security, and outbound security. He also explains the new encryption features that allow users to encrypt individual components of the service using custom managed keys stored in key vault.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
summary: The video discusses encryption and inbound security for a video service. Encryption at rest is achieved through the use of a custom managed key stored in a key vault, providing multiple layers of encryption. Inbound security options include IP restrictions and private link. IP restrictions allow for the restriction of traffic to specified IP addresses or ranges, while private link enables secure access to the service through a private endpoint. Both options enhance the security of the video service.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
summary: Private link and private endpoints allow for integration between a virtual network and a service without relying on internet calls. By making a search service private, it blocks all internet traffic and only allows traffic through a private link. The private endpoint has a stable private IP, which can be controlled and used for multiple private endpoints. This architecture provides enhanced protection for Azure cognitive search services. A demo showcasing the protection of Azure cognitive search service with private endpoints is also provided.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
summary: To ensure the security of real-world data in a search service, it is important to make the service private. This can be done by configuring IP restrictions or using a Virtual Network (VNet) with a private endpoint. By making the search service private, access to the data is restricted to authorized users within the VNet, ensuring that sensitive information is protected.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
summary: The video discusses the process of creating a private endpoint in Azure to give a virtual network access to a search service. The presenter explains the components involved, such as the virtual network and virtual machine, and highlights the importance of having a private DNS zone. The video demonstrates how to create a private endpoint and shows the connection in the Azure Portal.

speaker: Mike Carter
title: Azure Cognitive Search: What’s new in security
